在我们将这种自欺欺人视为赛马场常客独有的现象之前，我们应该看看我的邻居萨拉和她的同居男友蒂姆的故事。他们在一家医院相识，蒂姆是X光技师，萨拉是营养师。他们交往了一段时间，即使蒂姆失业后也依然如此，最终他们同居了。萨拉的生活并非一帆风顺：她希望蒂姆娶她，并戒掉酗酒的恶习；蒂姆却对这两件事都抗拒。在经历了一段尤为艰难的冲突之后，萨拉提出了分手，蒂姆搬了出去。与此同时，萨拉的一位前男友在离开多年后回到了镇上，并给她打了电话。他们开始在社交场合见面，并很快发展到足以筹备婚礼的地步。他们甚至已经定好了婚期并发出了邀请函，这时蒂姆打来了电话。他表示自己已经悔改，想要搬回来和萨拉同住。当萨拉告诉他自己的结婚计划时，他恳求她改变主意；他想和她像以前一样在一起。但萨拉拒绝了，她说她不想再过那样的生活了。蒂姆甚至向她求婚，但她仍然说她更喜欢另一个男友。最后，蒂姆主动提出，如果她肯答应，他就戒酒。萨拉觉得在这种情况下蒂姆占了上风，于是决定解除婚约，取消婚礼，撤回请柬，让蒂姆搬回来和她一起住。

Within a month, Tim informed Sara that he didn't think he needed to stop his drinking after all; a month later, he had decided that they should "wait and see" before getting married. Two years have since passed; Tim and Sara continue to live together exactly as before. He still drinks, there are still no marriage plans, yet Sara is more devoted to Tim than she ever was. She says that being forced to choose taught her that Tim really is number one in her heart. So, after choosing Tim over her other boyfriend, Sara became happier with him, even though the conditions under which she had made her choice have never been fulfilled. Obviously, horse-race bettors are not alone in their willingness to believe in the correctness of a difficult choice, once made. Indeed, we all fool ourselves from time to time in order to keep our thoughts and beliefs consistent with what we have already done or decided.

一个月后，蒂姆告诉萨拉，他觉得自己最终还是不需要戒酒；又过了一个月，他决定两人应该“再看看情况”再决定是否结婚。两年过去了，蒂姆和萨拉依然像以前一样生活在一起。他仍然喝酒，仍然没有结婚的打算，但萨拉对蒂姆的爱却比以往任何时候都更加深沉。她说，被迫做出选择让她明白，蒂姆才是她心中最重要的人。因此，在选择蒂姆而不是之前的男友之后，萨拉和他在一起更加快乐，尽管她当初做出选择的条件从未得到满足。显然，赛马赌徒并非唯一愿意相信自己做出的艰难抉择是正确的人。事实上，为了让自己的想法和信念与已经做出的决定保持一致，我们都会时不时地自欺欺人。

Psychologists have long understood the power of the consistency principle to direct human action. Prominent theorists such as Leon Festinger, Fritz Hieder, and Theodore Newcomb have viewed the desire for consistency as a central motivator of our behavior. But is this tendency to be consistent really strong enough to compel us to do what we ordinarily would not want to do? There is no question about it. The drive to be (and look) consistent constitutes a highly potent weapon of social influence, often causing us to act in ways that are clearly contrary to our own best interests.

心理学家早已认识到一致性原则对人类行为的强大影响。莱昂·费斯廷格、弗里茨·海德和西奥多·纽科姆等著名理论家都认为，追求一致性是我们行为的核心驱动力。但是，这种追求一致性的倾向真的强大到足以驱使我们去做那些我们通常不想做的事情吗？答案是肯定的。追求（以及看起来）一致性的驱动力构成了一种极具威力的社会影响力武器，它常常驱使我们做出明显违背自身利益的行为。

Take, as proof, what happened when psychologist Thomas Moriarty staged thefts on a New York City beach to see if onlookers would risk personal harm to halt the crime. In the study, a research accomplice would put a beach blanket down five feet from the blanket of a randomly chosen individual—the experimental subject. After a couple of minutes on the blanket spent relaxing and listening to music from a portable radio, the accomplice would stand up and leave the blanket to stroll down the beach. A few minutes later, a second researcher, pretending to be a thief, would approach, grab the radio, and try to hurry away with it. As you might guess, under normal conditions, subjects were very reluctant to put themselves in harm's way by challenging the thief—only four people did so in the twenty times, that the theft was staged. But when the same procedure was tried another twenty times, with a slight twist, the results were drastically different. In these incidents, before taking his stroll, the accomplice would simply ask the subject to please "watch my things," which each of them agreed to do. Now, propelled by the rule for consistency, nineteen of the twenty subjects became virtual vigilantes, running after and stopping the thief, demanding an explanation, and often restraining the thief physically or snatching the radio away.

以心理学家托马斯·莫里亚蒂在纽约海滩上模拟盗窃事件为例，看看旁观者是否会冒着生命危险阻止犯罪。在实验中，一名研究助手会在随机选择的实验对象（即受试者）的毯子五英尺外铺上一条沙滩毯。受试者在毯子上放松休息几分钟，听着便携式收音机播放的音乐后，助手会起身离开毯子，沿着沙滩漫步。几分钟后，另一名研究人员假扮成小偷，走近受试者，抢走收音机，试图迅速逃离。正如你可能猜到的那样，在正常情况下，受试者非常不愿意冒着生命危险去阻止小偷——在模拟盗窃的二十次实验中，只有四个人这样做。但是，当同样的实验程序稍作调整后再重复二十次时，结果却截然不同。在这些事件中，同伙在散步前只会请求受害者“帮我照看一下东西”，而每个人都会答应。如今，在“保持一致性”原则的驱使下，20名受害者中有19人几乎变成了义务警员，追赶并拦住窃贼，要求其解释，并且常常会制服窃贼或抢走收音机。

To understand why consistency is so powerful a motive, it is important to recognize that in most circumstances consistency is valued and adaptive. Inconsistency is commonly thought to be an undesirable personality trait. The person whose beliefs, words, and deeds don't match may be seen as indecisive, confused, two-faced, or even mentally ill. On the other side, a high degree of consistency is normally associated with personal and intellectual strength. It is at the heart of logic, rationality, stability, and honesty. A quote attributed to the great British chemist Michael Faraday suggests the extent to which being consistent is approved—sometimes more than being right. When asked after a lecture if he meant to imply that a hated academic rival was always wrong, Faraday glowered at the questioner and replied, "He's not that consistent."

要理解为何一致性如此强大，首先必须认识到，在大多数情况下，一致性是受人重视且具有适应性的。人们通常认为，前后矛盾是一种不良的性格特征。言行不一的人可能会被视为优柔寡断、糊涂、两面三刀，甚至精神有问题。另一方面，高度的一致性通常与个人和智力上的力量联系在一起。它是逻辑、理性、稳定和诚实的核心。英国伟大的化学家迈克尔·法拉第的一句名言表明了人们对一致性的认可程度——有时甚至超过了对“正确”的认可。在一次讲座后，有人问法拉第，他是否暗示一位他憎恨的学术竞争对手总是错的，法拉第怒视着提问者，回答说：“他没那么始终如一。”

Certainly, then, good personal consistency is highly valued in our culture. And well it should be. It provides us with a reasonable and gainful orientation to the world. Most of the time we will be better off if our approach to things is well laced with consistency. Without it our lives would be difficult, erratic, and disjointed.

因此，良好的个人一致性在我们的文化中备受推崇。这理所当然。它能为我们提供一种合理且有益的看待世界的方式。大多数时候，如果我们做事的方式始终如一，我们会过得更好。否则，我们的生活将会变得艰难、混乱且支离破碎。

But because it is so typically in our best interests to be consistent, we easily fall into the habit of being automatically so, even in situations where it is not the sensible way to be. When it occurs unthinkingly, consistency can be disastrous. Nonetheless, even blind consistency has its attractions.

但由于保持一致性通常符合我们的最佳利益，我们很容易养成自动保持一致的习惯，即使在不明智的情况下也是如此。当这种不假思索的一致性发生时，可能会带来灾难性的后果。尽管如此，即使是盲目的一致性也有其吸引力。

First, like most other forms of automatic responding, it offers a shortcut through the density of modern life. Once we have made up our minds about an issue, stubborn consistency allows us a very appealing luxury: We really don't have to think hard about the issue anymore. We don't have to sift through the blizzard of information we encounter every day to identify relevant facts; we don't have to expend the mental energy to weigh the pros and cons; we don't have to make any further tough decisions. Instead, all we have to do when confronted with the issue is to turn on our consistency tape, whirr, and we know just what to believe, say, or do. We need only believe, say, or do whatever is consistent with our earlier decision.

首先，和其他大多数自动反应一样，它为我们提供了一条穿越现代生活重重迷雾的捷径。一旦我们对某个问题下定决心，这种固执的一致性就能给我们带来一种极具吸引力的便利：我们真的不必再为此费心思考了。我们不必在每天铺天盖地的信息中筛选出相关的事实；不必耗费精力去权衡利弊；不必再做出任何艰难的决定。相反，当面对问题时，我们只需启动这种“一致性机制”，嗡嗡作响，我们就知道该相信什么、说什么或做什么。我们只需要相信、说或做任何与我们先前决定相符的事情即可。

The allure of such a luxury is not to be minimized. It allows us a convenient, relatively effortless, and efficient method for dealing with complex daily environments that make severe demands on our mental energies and capacities. It is not hard to understand, then, why automatic consistency is a difficult reaction to curb. It offers us a way to evade the rigors of continuing thought. And as Sir Joshua Reynolds noted, "There is no expedient to which a man will not resort to avoid the real labor of thinking." With our consistency tapes operating, then, we can go about our business happily excused from the toil of having to think too much.

这种奢侈的诱惑力不容小觑。它为我们提供了一种便捷、相对轻松且高效的方式来应对复杂的日常环境，这些环境对我们的精神能量和能力提出了极高的要求。因此，不难理解为什么自动一致性难以抑制。它为我们提供了一种逃避持续思考的途径。正如约书亚·雷诺兹爵士所言：“为了逃避真正的思考劳动，人们会不择手段。” 如此一来，在我们这种“一致性机制”的运作下，我们便可以心安理得地忙于各种事务，而无需承受过度思考的苦差事。

There is a second, more perverse attraction of mechanical consistency as well. Sometimes it is not the effort of hard, cognitive work that makes us shirk thoughtful activity, but the harsh consequences of that activity. Sometimes it is the cursedly clear and unwelcome set of answers provided by straight thinking that makes us mental slackers. There are certain disturbing things we simply would rather not realize. Because it is a preprogrammed and mindless method of responding, automatic consistency can supply a safe hiding place from those troubling realizations. Sealed within the fortress walls of rigid consistency, we can be impervious to the sieges of reason.

机械一致性还有第二个更为扭曲的吸引力。有时，让我们逃避思考的并非艰苦的认知劳动，而是这种劳动带来的严峻后果。有时，是直面思考所提供的清晰却令人厌恶的答案，让我们变得懒散。有些令人不安的事实，我们宁愿视而不见。由于这是一种预设的、无意识的反应方式，自动一致性可以为我们提供一个安全的避风港，让我们免受这些令人不安的现实的冲击。在僵化的一致性堡垒中，我们仿佛刀枪不入，对理性的围攻毫不在意。

One night at an introductory lecture given by the transcendental meditation (TM) program, I witnessed a nice illustration of how people will hide inside the walls of consistency to protect themselves from the troublesome consequences of thought. The lecture itself was presided over by two earnest young men and was designed to recruit new members into the program. The program claimed it could teach a unique brand of meditation that would allow us to achieve all manner of desirable things, ranging from simple inner peace to the more spectacular abilities to fly and pass through walls at the program's advanced (and more expensive) stages.

一天晚上，在一次由超验冥想（TM）项目举办的入门讲座上，我亲眼目睹了人们如何躲进循规蹈矩的壁垒中，以逃避思想带来的种种困扰。讲座由两位热情洋溢的年轻人主持，旨在招募新成员加入该项目。该项目声称，它能教授一种独特的冥想方法，使人获得各种各样令人向往的事物，从简单的内心平静到更高级（也更昂贵）阶段的飞行和穿墙等更惊人的能力。

I had decided to attend the meeting to observe the kind of compliance tactics used in recruitment lectures of this sort and had brought along an interested friend, a university professor whose areas of specialization were statistics and symbolic logic. As the meeting progressed and the lecturers explained the theory behind TM, I noticed my logician friend becoming increasingly restless. Looking more and more pained and shifting about constantly in his seat, he was finally unable to resist. When the leaders called for questions at the completion of the lecture, he raised his hand and gently but surely demolished the presentation we had just heard. In less than two minutes, he pointed out precisely where and why the lecturers' complex argument was contradictory, illogical, and unsupportable. The effect on the discussion leaders was devastating. After a confused silence, each attempted a weak reply only to halt midway to confer with his partner and finally to admit that my colleague's points were good ones "requiring further study."

我决定参加这次会议，是为了观察这类招聘讲座中使用的顺从策略，并带了一位感兴趣的朋友——一位大学教授，他的专长是统计学和符号逻辑。随着会议的进行，讲师们开始讲解TM背后的理论，我注意到我的逻辑学家朋友越来越焦躁不安。他看起来越来越痛苦，在座位上不停地挪动，最终忍不住了。讲座结束后，主持人征求提问，他举起了手，温和而有力地驳斥了我们刚才听到的演讲。不到两分钟，他就精准地指出了讲师们复杂的论证中哪些地方自相矛盾、逻辑混乱、站不住脚。这给讨论主持人带来了毁灭性的打击。一阵令人困惑的沉默之后，每个人都试图做出一个苍白的回应，但都半途而废，与同伴商量，最终承认我同事的观点很好，“需要进一步研究”。

More interesting to me, though, was the effect upon the rest of the audience. At the end of the question period, the two recruiters were faced with a crush of audience members submitting their seventy-five-dollar down payments for admission to the TM program. Nudging, shrugging, and chuckling to one another as they took in the payments, the recruiters betrayed signs of giddy bewilderment. After what appeared to have been an embarrassingly clear collapse of their presentation, the meeting had somehow turned into a great success, generating mystifyingly high levels of compliance from the audience. Although more than a bit puzzled, I chalked up the audience response to a failure to understand the logic of my colleague's arguments. As it turned out, however, just the reverse was the case.

不过，更让我感兴趣的是其他听众的反应。问答环节结束后，两位招聘人员面对着蜂拥而至的听众，他们纷纷缴纳75美元的TM项目入学定金。两位招聘人员一边收钱，一边互相推搡、耸肩、轻笑，脸上流露出既兴奋又困惑的神情。他们的演讲原本似乎以失败告终，但会议却出人意料地取得了巨大成功，听众的配合度高得令人费解。虽然我百思不得其解，但我还是把听众的反应归咎于他们不理解我同事的论点逻辑。然而，事实证明，情况恰恰相反。

Outside the lecture room after the meeting, we were approached by three members of the audience, each of whom had given a down payment immediately after the lecture. They wanted to know why we had come to the session. We explained, and we asked the same question of them. One was an aspiring actor who wanted desperately to succeed at his craft and had come to the meeting to learn if TM would allow him to achieve the necessary self-control to master the art; the recruiters had assured him that it would. The second described herself as a severe insomniac who had hopes that TM would provide her with a way to relax and fall asleep easily at night. The third served as unofficial spokesman. He also had a sleep-related problem. He was failing college because there didn't seem to be enough time to study. He had come to the meeting to find out if TM could help by training him to need fewer hours of sleep each night; the additional time could then be used for study. It is interesting to note that the recruiters informed him as well as the insomniac that Transcendental Meditation techniques could solve their respective, though opposite, problems.

会后，我们在讲堂外遇到了三位听众，他们都在讲座结束后立即支付了定金。他们想知道我们为什么来参加这次讲座。我们解释了原因，并问了他们同样的问题。其中一位是一位渴望成名的演员，他迫切希望在演艺事业上取得成功，来参加讲座是为了了解超觉冥想（TM）是否能帮助他获得必要的自控力，从而掌握表演艺术；招生人员向他保证可以。第二位自称患有严重的失眠症，希望超觉冥想能帮助她放松身心，轻松入睡。第三位算是我们的非正式发言人。他也存在睡眠问题。他因为睡眠不足，大学成绩很差。他来参加讲座是想了解超觉冥想是否能帮助他减少每晚的睡眠时间，从而节省出更多时间用于学习。值得注意的是，招聘人员告诉他以及失眠症患者，超验冥想技巧可以解决他们各自（尽管截然相反）的问题。

Still thinking that the three must have signed up because they hadn't understood the points made by my logician friend, I began to question them about aspects of his argument. To my surprise, I found that they had understood his comments quite well; in fact, all too well. It was precisely the cogency of his argument that drove them to sign up for the program on the spot. The spokesman put it best: "Well, I wasn't going to put down any money tonight because I'm really quite broke right now; I was going to wait until the next meeting. But when your buddy started talking, I knew I'd better give them my money now, or I'd go home and start thinking about what he said and never sign up."

我当时还以为这三个人报名是因为他们没听懂我那位逻辑学家朋友的讲解，于是开始询问他们一些关于他论证的问题。令我惊讶的是，我发现他们其实理解得相当透彻，甚至可以说是过于透彻了。正是他论证的说服力促使他们当场报名参加这个项目。发言人说得最贴切：“我本来今晚没打算交钱，因为我现在真的很穷，我打算等到下次会议再交。但是你朋友一开口，我就知道我最好现在就把钱给他们，不然我回家后会一直琢磨他说的那些话，最后可能永远都不会报名了。”

All at once, things began to make sense. These were people with real problems; and they were somewhat desperately searching for a way to solve those problems. They were seekers who, if our discussion leaders were to be believed, had found a potential solution in TM. Driven by their needs, they very much wanted to believe that TM was their answer.

突然间，一切都豁然开朗。这些人确实面临着实际的问题；而且他们正迫切地寻找解决之道。他们是寻求答案的人，如果我们的讨论主持人所言属实，他们似乎在超觉冥想中找到了潜在的解决方案。在自身需求的驱使下，他们非常渴望相信超觉冥想就是他们的答案。

Now, in the form of my colleague, intrudes the voice of reason, showing the theory underlying their newfound solution to be unsound. Panic! Something must be done at once before logic takes its toll and leaves them without hope again. Quickly, quickly, walls against reason are needed; and it doesn't matter that the fortress to be erected is a foolish one. "Quick, a hiding place from thought! Here, take this money. Whew, safe in the nick of time. No need to think about the issues any longer. The decision has been made, and from now on the consistency tape can be played whenever necessary: 'TM? Certainly I think it will help me; certainly I expect to continue; certainly I believe in TM. I already put my money down for it, didn't I?' Ah, the comforts of mindless consistency. I'll just rest right here for a while. It's so much nicer than the worry and strain of that hard, hard search."

这时，我的同事以理性的声音插了进来，指出他们新找到的解决方案背后的理论站不住脚。慌了！必须马上采取行动，否则逻辑会再次让他们绝望。快，快，需要筑起一道道抵御理性的屏障；就算要建的堡垒很愚蠢也无所谓。“快，找个地方躲避思考！给你，拿着这些钱。呼，千钧一发之际，安全了。不用再考虑那些问题了。决定已经做出，从现在开始，需要的时候就可以播放这段自洽的录音带了：‘TM？我当然认为它会对我有帮助；我当然打算继续；我当然相信TM。我已经付钱了，不是吗？’啊，这种无脑的自洽真让人感到舒适。我就在这儿休息一会儿吧。这比苦苦寻觅、焦虑不安要好得多。”

If, as it appears, automatic consistency functions as a shield against thought, it should not be surprising that such consistency can also be exploited by those who would prefer that we not think too much in response to their requests for our compliance. For the exploiters, whose interest will be served by an unthinking, mechanical reaction to their requests, our tendency for automatic consistency is a gold mine. So clever are they at arranging to have us play our consistency tapes when it profits them that we seldom realize we have been taken. In fine jujitsu fashion, they structure their interactions with us so that our own need to be consistent will lead directly to their benefit.

如果自动一致性真的像表面看起来那样，成为一种抵御思考的屏障，那么，这种一致性会被那些希望我们不要过多思考就能顺从他们的人所利用，也就不足为奇了。对于那些利用我们这种自动一致性的人来说，我们机械地、不假思索地回应他们的要求，就能从中获利，而我们这种自动一致性的倾向，正是他们牟利的摇钱树。他们如此巧妙地安排，让我们在对他们有利的时候，就自然而然地重复这种“一致性模式”，以至于我们很少意识到自己已经上当受骗。他们如同精湛的柔术一般，精心设计与我们的互动，让我们的这种“一致性”需求最终直接为他们带来好处。

Certain large toy manufacturers use just such an approach to reduce a problem caused by seasonal buying patterns. Of course, the boom time for toy sales occurs before and during the Christmas holiday season. The toy companies make fat profits during this period. Their problem is that toy sales then go into a terrible slump for the next couple of months. Their customers have already spent the full amount in their toy budgets and are stiffly resistant to their children's pleas for more. Even those children whose birthdays fall soon after the holidays receive fewer toys because of the recent Christmas spree.

一些大型玩具制造商正是利用这种方法来缓解季节性购买模式带来的问题。当然，玩具销售的旺季出现在圣诞节前后。玩具公司在这段时间里利润丰厚。但他们的问题在于，接下来的几个月玩具销量会急剧下滑。消费者们已经花光了玩具预算，对孩子们想要更多玩具的请求也变得难以接受。即使是那些生日在圣诞节后不久的孩子，也会因为之前的圣诞节购物狂潮而收到更少的玩具。

So the toy manufacturers are faced with a dilemma: how to keep sales high during the peak season and, at the same time, retain a healthy demand for toys in the immediately following months. Their difficulty certainly doesn't lie in convincing our naturally insatiable offspring to want a continuous flow of new amusements. A series of flashy television commercials placed among the Saturday morning cartoon shows will produce the usual amounts of begging, whining, and wheedling no matter when it appears during the year. No, the problem is not in motivating kids to want more toys after Christmas.

因此，玩具制造商面临着一个难题：如何在旺季保持高销量，同时又能在接下来的几个月里维持对玩具的健康需求。他们的难点当然不在于如何说服我们天生贪得无厌的孩子们不断追求新的娱乐产品。无论一年中的哪个时候，在周六早晨的动画片中穿插播放一系列炫目的电视广告，都会引发孩子们一如既往的乞求、哭闹和哄骗。不，问题不在于如何激发孩子们在圣诞节后对更多玩具的渴望。

The problem is in motivating postholiday spent-out parents to reach down for the price of yet another plaything for their already toy-glutted children. What could the toy companies possibly do to produce that unlikely behavior? Some have tried a greatly increased advertising campaign, others have reduced prices during the slack period, but neither of those standard sales devices has proved successful. Not only are both tactics costly, but both have also been ineffective in increasing sales to desired levels. Parents are simply not in a toy-buying mood, and the influences of advertising or reduced expense are not enough to shake that stony resistance.

问题在于如何激励节后精疲力竭的父母们再掏钱给已经玩具堆积如山的孩子们添置新玩具。玩具公司究竟该如何做才能促成这种不太可能发生的消费行为呢？一些公司尝试大幅增加广告投入，另一些公司则在淡季降价促销，但这些常见的销售手段都未能奏效。这些策略不仅成本高昂，而且也未能有效提升销量至预期水平。父母们根本没有购买玩具的欲望，广告宣传或降价促销都无法撼动他们根深蒂固的抵触情绪。

Certain large toy manufacturers, however, think they have found a solution. It's an ingenious one, involving no more than a normal advertising expense and an understanding of the powerful pull of the need for consistency. My first hint of how the toy companies' strategy worked came after I fell for it and then, in true patsy form, fell for it again.

然而，某些大型玩具制造商却认为他们找到了解决办法。这招十分巧妙，只需投入正常的广告费用，并深谙消费者对产品一致性的强烈需求。我第一次意识到玩具公司这套策略的运作原理，是在我上当受骗之后，然后，像个十足的傻瓜一样，我又一次中了当。

It was January, and I was in the town's largest toy store. After purchasing all too many gifts there for my son a month before, I had sworn not to enter that place or any like it for a long, long time. Yet there I was, not only in the diabolic place but also in the process of buying my son another expensive toy—a big, electric road-race set. In front of the road-race display, I happened to meet a former neighbor who was buying his son the same toy. The odd thing was that we almost never saw each other anymore. In fact, the last time was a year earlier in that same store where we were both buying our sons an expensive post-Christmas gift—that time a robot that walked, talked, and laid waste. We laughed about our strange pattern of seeing each other only once a year at the same time, in the same place, while doing the same thing. Later that day, I mentioned the coincidence to a friend who, it turned out, had once worked in the toy business.

那是1月份，我去了镇上最大的玩具店。一个月前，我在那里给儿子买了太多礼物，之后我发誓很长一段时间内都不会再踏进那家店，或者任何类似的地方。然而，我却不仅身处那个“魔鬼之地”，而且还在给儿子买另一件昂贵的玩具——一套大型电动赛车套装。在赛车展示柜前，我碰巧遇到了以前的邻居，他也在给儿子买同样的玩具。奇怪的是，我们几乎已经很久没见面了。事实上，我们上次见面还是在一年前，也是在同一家店里，当时我们都在给儿子买昂贵的圣诞节后礼物——那次是一个会走路、会说话、还会大闹一番的机器人。我们笑着说起我们之间奇怪的“巧合”：一年只在同一时间、同一地点碰面一次，而且做的都是同样的事情。那天晚些时候，我把这件巧合告诉了一位朋友，结果发现她以前也曾在玩具行业工作过。

"No coincidence," he said knowingly.

“这绝非巧合，”他意味深长地说。

"What do you mean, 'No coincidence'?"

“你的意思是‘绝非巧合’吗？”

"Look," he said, "let me ask you a couple of questions about the road-race set you bought this year. First, did you promise your son that he'd get one for Christmas?"

“听着，”他说，“我想问你几个关于你今年买的公路赛车套装的问题。首先，你答应过你儿子圣诞节会送他一套吗？”

"Well, yes, I did. Christopher had seen a bunch of ads for them on the Saturday morning cartoon shows and said that was what he wanted for Christmas. I saw a couple of the ads myself and it looked like fun, so I said okay."

“嗯，是的，我买了。克里斯托弗在周六早晨的卡通节目里看到了很多广告，说他想要这个作为圣诞礼物。我自己也看了几个广告，觉得挺有意思的，所以就答应了。”

"Strike one," he announced. "Now for my second question. When you went to buy one, did you find all the stores sold out?"

“第一击，”他宣布道。“现在问第二个问题。你去买的时候，是不是发现所有商店都卖光了？”

"That's right, I did! The stores said they'd ordered some but didn't know when they'd get any more in. So I had to buy Christopher some other toys to make up for the road-race set. But how did you know?"

“没错，是我买的！商店说他们订了一些，但不知道什么时候才能到货。所以我只好给克里斯托弗买了些别的玩具来弥补赛车套装的缺失。不过你是怎么知道的？”

"Strike two," he said. "Just let me ask one more question. Didn't this same sort of thing happen the year before with the robot toy?"

“第二次了，”他说。“让我再问一个问题。去年那个机器人玩具是不是也发生过类似的事情？”

"Wait a minute... you're right. That's just what happened. This is incredible. How did you know?"

“等等……你说得对。事情就是这样。这太不可思议了。你怎么知道的？”

"No psychic powers; I just happen to know how several of the big toy companies jack up their January and February sales. They start prior to Christmas with attractive TV ads for certain special toys. The kids, naturally, want what they see and extract Christmas promises for these items from their parents. Now here's where the genius of the companies' plan comes in: They undersupply the stores with the toys they've gotten the parents to promise. Most parents find those things sold out and are forced to substitute other toys of equal value. The toy manufacturers, of course, make a point of supplying the stores with plenty of these substitutes. Then, after Christmas, the companies start running the ads again for the other, special toys. That juices up the kids to want those toys more than ever. They go running to their parents whining, 'You promised, you promised,' and the adults go trudging off to the store to live up dutifully to their words."

“我没有超能力；我只是碰巧知道几家大型玩具公司是如何提升一月和二月销量的。他们在圣诞节前就开始投放一些特别玩具的电视广告。孩子们自然想要广告里展示的东西，并向父母套取圣诞礼物的承诺。而这些公司计划的精妙之处在于：他们故意减少商店里那些被父母承诺购买的玩具的供应量。大多数父母发现这些玩具已经售罄，只能被迫购买其他同等价值的替代品。当然，玩具制造商会确保商店里有大量的替代品。然后，圣诞节过后，这些公司又开始投放那些特别玩具的广告。这反而更加激发了孩子们对这些玩具的渴望。他们跑到父母身边哭诉：“你答应过，你答应过”，而大人们则不得不拖着疲惫的身体去商店，履行他们的诺言。”

"Where," I said, beginning to seethe now, "they meet other parents they haven't seen for a year, falling for the same trick, right?"

“他们在哪里？”我开始怒火中烧地说，“遇到一年没见的其他家长，然后又上当受骗，对吧？”

"Right. Uh, where are you going?"

“好的。呃，你要去哪儿？”

"I'm going to take that road-race set right back to the store." I was so angry I was nearly shouting.

“我要把那套公路赛车装备退回商店。”我气得几乎要喊出来了。

"Wait. Think for a minute first. Why did you buy it this morning?"

“等等，先想想。你今天早上为什么要买它？”

"Because I didn't want to let Christopher down and because I wanted to teach him that promises are to be lived up to."

“因为我不想让克里斯托弗失望，也因为我想教会他承诺要兑现。”

"Well, has any of that changed? Look, if you take his toy away now, he won't understand why. He'll just know that his father broke a promise to him. Is that what you want?"

“那么，这些事有改变吗？你看，如果你现在把他的玩具拿走，他不会明白为什么。他只会觉得他爸爸违背了对他的承诺。这就是你想要的吗？”

"No," I said, sighing, "I guess not. So, you're telling me that they doubled their profit on me for the past two years, and I never even knew it; and now that I do, I'm still trapped—by my own words. So, what you're really telling me is, 'Strike three.'"

“不，”我叹了口气说，“我想不是。所以，你的意思是说，过去两年他们从我身上赚了双倍的钱，而我竟然毫不知情；现在我知道了，却仍然被困在自己说过的话里。所以，你真正想告诉我的是，‘三振出局’。”

He nodded, "And you're out."

他点点头，“你出局了。”

COMMITMENT IS THE KEY

承诺是关键

Once we realize that the power of consistency is formidable in directing human action, an important practical question immediately arises: How is that force engaged? What produces the click that activates the whirr of the powerful consistency tape? Social psychologists think they know the answer: commitment. If I can get you to make a commitment (that is, to take a stand, to go on record), I will have set the stage for your automatic and ill-considered consistency with that earlier commitment. Once a stand is taken, there is a natural tendency to behave in ways that are stubbornly consistent with the stand.

一旦我们意识到一致性在引导人类行为方面具有强大的力量，一个重要的实际问题便会立即出现：这种力量是如何被激发出来的？是什么触发了这股强大的一致性机制？社会心理学家认为他们知道答案：承诺。如果我能让你做出承诺（即表明立场，公开表态），我就为你日后不假思索地坚持之前的承诺奠定了基础。一旦表明了立场，人们自然而然地会倾向于以与该立场完全一致的方式行事。

As we've already seen, social psychologists are not the only ones who understand the connection between commitment and consistency. Commitment strategies are aimed at us by compliance professionals of nearly every sort. Each of the strategies is intended to get us to take some action or make some statement that will trap us into later compliance through consistency pressures. Procedures designed to create commitment take various forms. Some are fairly straightforward; others are among the most subtle compliance tactics we will encounter.

正如我们已经看到的，并非只有社会心理学家才了解承诺与一致性之间的联系。几乎所有类型的合规专家都在针对我们制定承诺策略。每一种策略都旨在促使我们采取某种行动或发表某种声明，从而通过一致性压力让我们在日后屈服。旨在建立承诺的程序形式多样。有些相当直接；另一些则是我们所遇到的最隐蔽的合规策略之一。

For instance, suppose you wanted to increase the number of people in your area who would agree to go door-to-door collecting donations for your favorite charity. You would be wise to study the approach taken by social psychologist Steven J. Sherman. He simply called a sample of Bloomington, Indiana, residents as part of a survey he was taking and asked them to predict what they would say if asked to spend three hours collecting money for the American Cancer Society. Of course, not wanting to seem uncharitable to the survey taker or to themselves, many of these people said that they would volunteer. The consequence of this sly commitment procedure was a 700 percent increase in volunteers when, a few days later, a representative of the American Cancer Society did call and ask for neighborhood canvassers.

例如，假设你想增加你所在地区愿意挨家挨户为你最喜欢的慈善机构募捐的人数。那么，研究一下社会心理学家史蒂文·J·谢尔曼（Steven J. Sherman）的方法就很有意义。他当时正在进行一项调查，期间他随机抽取了印第安纳州布卢明顿市的居民进行电话调查，并询问他们如果被要求花三个小时为美国癌症协会募捐，他们会作何反应。当然，为了不让调查人员或自己显得不够慷慨，许多人都表示愿意做志愿者。这种巧妙的承诺策略带来的结果是，几天后，当美国癌症协会的代表打电话来招募社区募捐志愿者时，志愿者人数竟然增加了700%。

Using the same strategy, but this time asking Columbus, Ohio, residents to predict whether they would vote on Election Day, a team of researchers led by Anthony Greenwald were able to increase significantly the turnout in a U.S. presidential election among those called.

采用同样的策略，但这次他们询问俄亥俄州哥伦布市的居民是否会在选举日投票，由安东尼·格林沃尔德领导的一个研究团队成功地大幅提高了被询问者的美国总统选举投票率。

Perhaps an even more crafty commitment technique has been developed recently by telephone solicitors for charity. Have you noticed that callers asking you to contribute to some cause or another these days seem to begin things by inquiring about your current health and well-being? "Hello Mr./Ms. Targetperson," they say. "How are you feeling this evening?" Or, "How are you doing today?" The caller's intent with this sort of introduction is not merely to seem friendly and caring. It is to get you to respond—as you normally do to such polite, superficial inquiries—with a polite, superficial comment of your own: "Just fine" or "Real good" or "I'm doing great, thanks." Once you have publicly stated that all is well, it becomes much easier for the solicitor to corner you into aiding those for whom all is not well: "I'm glad to hear that, because I'm calling to ask if you'd be willing to make a donation to help out the unfortunate victims of..."

或许，最近慈善募捐电话中出现了一种更加狡猾的拉拢技巧。您是否注意到，如今那些请求您捐款的电话，似乎都会先询问您目前的健康状况？他们会说：“您好，[目标人物]先生/女士，您今晚感觉如何？”或者，“您今天过得怎么样？” 来电者这样开场白的目的并非仅仅是为了显得友好和关心。他们的目的是让您像往常一样，对这种礼貌而肤浅的询问做出礼貌而肤浅的回应，例如：“很好”、“非常好”或“我很好，谢谢”。一旦您公开表示一切都好，募捐者就更容易引导您去帮助那些不幸的人：“很高兴听到这个消息，因为我打电话来是想问问您是否愿意捐款，帮助那些不幸的受害者……”

The theory behind this tactic is that people who have just asserted that they are doing/feeling fine—even as a routine part of a sociable exchange—will consequently find it awkward to appear stingy in the context of their own admittedly favored circumstances. If all this sounds a bit farfetched, consider the findings of consumer researcher Daniel Howard, who put the theory to test. Dallas, Texas, residents were called on the phone and asked if they would agree to allow a representative of the Hunger Relief Committee to come to their homes to sell them cookies, the proceeds from which would be used to supply meals for the needy. When tried alone, that request (labeled the "standard solicitation approach") produced only 18 percent agreement. However, if the caller initially asked, "How are you feeling this evening?" and waited for a reply before proceeding to the standard approach, several noteworthy things happened. First, of the 120 individuals called, most (108) gave the customary favorable reply ("Good," "Fine," "Real well," etc.). Second, 32 percent of the people who got the "How are you feeling tonight" question agreed to receive the cookie seller at their homes, nearly twice the success rate of the standard solicitation approach. Third, true to the consistency principle, almost everyone who agreed to such a visit did, in fact, make a cookie purchase when contacted at home (89 percent).

这种策略背后的理论是，人们刚刚表示自己一切都好——即使这只是社交场合中的例行公事——之后，在自己明显处于有利地位的情况下，再表现得吝啬就会显得很尴尬。如果这一切听起来有点牵强，不妨看看消费者研究员丹尼尔·霍华德的发现，他用实际行动验证了这一理论。他打电话给德克萨斯州达拉斯市的居民，询问他们是否同意让饥饿救济委员会的代表上门推销饼干，所得款项将用于为贫困人群提供餐食。单独使用这种请求方式（被称为“标准推销方式”）时，只有18%的人同意。然而，如果打电话的人先问一句“您今晚感觉如何？”，然后等待对方回答后再进行标准推销，就会出现一些值得注意的现象。首先，在拨打电话的120人中，大多数人（108人）给出了惯常的积极回应（“很好”、“不错”、“非常好”等等）。其次，在被问及“你今晚感觉如何”的人中，有32%的人同意让饼干推销员上门，这一成功率几乎是标准推销方式的两倍。第三，正如一致性原则所体现的那样，几乎所有同意上门推销的人，在接到推销员的电话后都购买了饼干（89%）。

To make sure that this tactic doesn't generate its successes simply because a solicitor who uses it seems more concerned and courteous than one who doesn't use it, Howard conducted another study. This time callers began either with the question "How are you feeling this evening?" (and waited for a response before proceeding) or with the statement "I hope you are feeling well this evening" and then proceeded to the standard solicitation approach. Despite the fact that the caller started each type of interaction with a warm and friendly comment, the "How are you feeling" technique was, by far, superior to its rival (33 percent vs. 15 percent compliance), because it alone drew an exploitable public commitment from its targets. Note that the commitment was able to get twice as much compliance from those targets even though at the time it occurred it must have seemed to them an altogether inconsequential reply to an altogether superficial question—yet another fine example of social jujitsu at work.

为了确保这种策略的成功并非仅仅因为使用该策略的推销员看起来比不使用的推销员更关心客户、更有礼貌，霍华德进行了另一项研究。这次，电话推销员有两种不同的开场白：一种是先问“您今晚感觉如何？”（并等待对方回答后再继续），另一种是先说“希望您今晚感觉良好”，然后再进行标准的推销。尽管两种开场白都是热情友好的问候，但“您感觉如何？”的技巧远胜于另一种（33% 对 15%），因为它能从目标对象那里获得可利用的公开承诺。值得注意的是，这种承诺能够使目标对象的配合度翻倍，尽管在当时，他们可能觉得这只是对一个肤浅问题的无关紧要的回应——这又是社交技巧运用的又一绝佳例证。

The question of what makes a commitment effective has a number of answers. A variety of factors affect the ability of a commitment to constrain our future behavior. One large-scale program designed to produce compliance illustrates nicely how several of the factors work. The remarkable thing about this program is that it was systematically employing these factors decades ago, well before scientific research had identified them.

关于什么因素使承诺有效，答案有很多。多种因素会影响承诺约束我们未来行为的能力。一项旨在提高服从性的大型项目很好地说明了其中几个因素是如何运作的。这个项目的非凡之处在于，早在几十年前，也就是科学研究发现这些因素之前，它就已经系统地运用了这些因素。

During the Korean War, many captured American soldiers found themselves in prisoner-of-war (POW) camps run by the Chinese Communists. It became clear early in the conflict that the Chinese treated captives quite differently than did their allies, the North Koreans, who favored savagery and harsh punishment to gain compliance. Specifically avoiding the appearance of brutality, the Red Chinese engaged in what they termed their "lenient policy," which was in reality a concerted and sophisticated psychological assault on their captives. After the war, American psychologists questioned the returning prisoners intensively to determine what had occurred. The intensive psychological investigation took place, in part, because of the unsettling success of some aspects of the Chinese program. For example, the Chinese were very effective in getting Americans to inform on one another, in striking contrast to the behavior of American POWs in World War II. For this reason, among others, escape plans were quickly uncovered and the escape attempts themselves almost always unsuccessful. "When an escape did occur," wrote Dr. Edgar Schein, a principal American investigator of the Chinese indoctrination program in Korea, "the Chinese usually recovered the man easily by offering a bag of rice to anyone turning him in." In fact, nearly all American prisoners in the Chinese camps are said to have collaborated with the enemy in one form or an-other. 2

朝鲜战争期间，许多被俘的美军士兵被关押在中国共产党管理的战俘营中。战争初期，人们就发现中国对待战俘的方式与他们的盟友朝鲜截然不同。朝鲜倾向于使用残酷的手段和严厉的惩罚来迫使战俘屈服。为了避免给人留下残暴的印象，红色中国采取了他们所谓的“宽容政策”，而这实际上是对战俘精心策划的心理战。战后，美国心理学家对返回的战俘进行了深入的调查，以了解战俘的遭遇。之所以进行如此深入的心理调查，部分原因是中国某些做法取得了令人不安的成功。例如，中国非常有效地让美国人互相告密，这与二战时期美国战俘的行为形成了鲜明的对比。正因如此，越狱计划很快就被识破，而越狱尝试本身也几乎总是以失败告终。 “一旦发生逃跑事件，”美国调查人员埃德加·沙因博士写道，他是研究中国在朝鲜推行的思想灌输计划的主要研究者之一，“中国人通常会给举报人一袋米，就能轻易地把他抓回来。”事实上，据说几乎所有被关押在中国战俘营的美国战俘都以某种形式与敌人合作过。

An examination of the Chinese prison-camp program shows that its personnel relied heavily on commitment and consistency pressures to gain the desired compliance from prisoners. Of course, the first problem facing the Chinese was how to get any collaboration at all from the Americans. These were men who were trained to provide nothing but name, rank, and serial number. Short of physical brutalization, how could the captors hope to get such men to give military information, turn in fellow prisoners, or publicly denounce their country? The Chinese answer was elementary: Start small and build.

对中国战俘营项目的考察表明，其工作人员主要依靠囚犯的忠诚度和持续压力来获得所需的服从。当然，中国人面临的首要问题是如何从美国人那里获得任何合作。这些人受过训练，除了姓名、军衔和编号之外，什么都不肯提供。除了肉体上的虐待，俘虏者如何才能指望这些人提供军事情报、出卖其他战俘或公开谴责自己的国家呢？中国人的答案很简单：从小规模做起，逐步扩大规模。

For instance, prisoners were frequently asked to make statements so mildly anti-American or pro-Communist as to seem inconsequential ("The United States is not perfect." "In a Communist country, unemployment is not a problem."). But once these minor requests were complied with, the men found themselves pushed to submit to related yet more substantive requests. A man who had just agreed with his Chinese interrogator that the United States is not perfect might then be asked to indicate some of the ways in which he thought this was the case. Once he had so explained himself, he might be asked to make a list of these "problems with America" and to sign his name to it. Later he might be asked to read his list in a discussion group with other prisoners. "After all, it's what you really believe, isn't it?" Still later he might be asked to write an essay expanding on his list and discussing these problems in greater detail.

例如，囚犯经常被要求发表一些看似无关紧要的、带有轻微反美或亲共色彩的言论（“美国并不完美。”“在共产主义国家，失业不是问题。”）。但一旦这些无关紧要的要求得到满足，他们就会发现自己被迫接受一些相关但更为实质性的要求。一个刚刚同意中国审讯员关于美国并不完美的人，可能会被要求指出他认为美国有哪些不完美之处。一旦他解释清楚，他可能会被要求列出这些“美国的问题”，并在上面签名。之后，他可能会被要求在与其他囚犯的讨论小组中朗读这份清单。“毕竟，这才是你真正相信的，不是吗？”再过一段时间，他可能会被要求写一篇文章，扩展他的清单，更详细地讨论这些问题。

The Chinese might then use his name and his essay in an anti-American radio broadcast beamed not only to the entire camp, but to other POW camps in North Korea, as well as to American forces in South Korea. Suddenly he would find himself a "collaborator," having given aid to the enemy. Aware that he had written the essay without any strong threats or coercion, many times a man would change his image of himself to be consistent with the deed and with the new "collaborator" label, often resulting in even more extensive acts of collaboration. Thus, while "only a few men were able to avoid collaboration altogether," according to Dr. Schein, "the majority collaborated at one time or another by doing things which seemed to them trivial but which the Chinese were able to turn to their own advantage.... This was particularly effective in eliciting confessions, self-criticism, and information during interrogation."

中国人随后可能会在反美广播中利用他的名字和文章，不仅向整个战俘营播出，还会向朝鲜的其他战俘营以及驻韩美军播出。他突然发现自己成了“通敌者”，因为他向敌人提供了帮助。由于意识到这篇文章并非出于任何强烈的威胁或胁迫而写，许多人会改变自己的认知，以符合自己的行为和新的“通敌者”标签，这往往会导致更广泛的合作行为。因此，正如沙因博士所说，“只有少数人能够完全避免合作”，“但大多数人或多或少都曾以一些在他们看来微不足道的方式与中国人合作，而中国人却能利用这些行为为自己谋利……这在审讯中尤其有效地诱使战俘供认不讳、自我批评并提供情报。”

If the Chinese know about the subtle power of this approach, it should not be surprising that another group of people interested in compliance is also aware of its usefulness. Many business organizations employ it regularly.

如果中国人了解这种方法的微妙力量，那么另一群关注合规的人士也意识到它的效用也就不足为奇了。许多商业机构经常使用这种方法。

For the salesperson, the strategy is to obtain a large purchase by starting with a small one. Almost any small sale will do, because the purpose of that small transaction is not profit. It is commitment. Further purchases, even much larger ones, are expected to flow naturally from the commitment. An article in the trade magazine American Salesman put it succinctly:

对销售人员来说，策略是通过小额订单来促成大额订单。几乎任何小额订单都可以，因为小额交易的目的并非盈利，而是为了建立客户关系。后续订单，甚至是更大的订单，都会自然而然地从这种客户关系中衍生出来。《美国推销员》杂志上的一篇文章对此做了精辟的阐述：

The general idea is to pave the way for full-line distribution by starting with a small order.... Look at it this way—when a person has signed an order for your merchandise, even though the profit is so small it hardly compensates for the time and effort of making the call, he is no longer a prospect—he is a customer. 4
总体思路是从小订单开始，逐步铺平通往全线分销的道路……不妨这样想：当有人下了订单购买你的商品时，即使利润微薄，几乎不足以弥补你花费的时间和精力，他也不再是潜在客户，而是你的客户了。

The tactic of starting with a little request in order to gain eventual compliance with related larger requests has a name: the foot-in-the-door technique. Social scientists first became aware of its effectiveness in the mid-1960s when psychologists Jonathan Freedman and Scott Fraser published an astonishing set of data. They reported the results of an experiment in which a researcher, posing as a volunteer worker, had gone door to door in a residential California neighborhood making a preposterous request of homeowners. The homeowners were asked to allow a public-service billboard to be installed on their front lawns. To get an idea of just how the sign would look, they were shown a photograph depicting an attractive house, the view of which was almost completely obscured by a very large, poorly lettered sign reading DRIVE CAREFULLY. Although the request was normally and understandably refused by the great majority (83 percent) of the other residents in the area, this particular group of people reacted quite favorably. A full 76 percent of them offered the use of their front yards.

这种先提出一个小请求，最终促使对方同意提出更大请求的策略，有一个专门的名称：登门槛效应。社会科学家在20世纪60年代中期首次意识到这种策略的有效性，当时心理学家乔纳森·弗里德曼和斯科特·弗雷泽发表了一组令人震惊的数据。他们报告了一项实验的结果：一位研究人员伪装成志愿者，挨家挨户地走访加州的一个居民区，向房主们提出了一个荒谬的请求。房主们被要求允许在自家前院安装一块公益广告牌。为了让房主们了解广告牌的实际效果，研究人员给他们看了一张照片，照片上是一栋漂亮的房子，但房子几乎完全被一块巨大的、字体很小的“小心驾驶”广告牌遮挡住了。虽然该地区绝大多数居民（83%）都理所当然地拒绝了这一请求，但这个特殊的群体却反应相当积极。其中高达 76% 的人表示愿意使用自家前院。

The prime reason for their startling compliance has to do with something that had happened to them about two weeks earlier: They had made a small commitment to driver safety. A different volunteer worker had come to their doors and asked them to accept and display a little three-inch-square sign that read BE A SAFE DRIVER. It was such a trifling request that nearly all of them had agreed to it. But the effects of that request were enormous. Because they had innocently complied with a trivial safe-driving request a couple of weeks before, these homeowners became remarkably willing to comply with another such request that was massive in size.

他们如此积极配合的主要原因，与大约两周前发生在他们身上的一件事有关：他们曾做出过一个小小的安全驾驶承诺。一位志愿者来到他们家门口，请他们接受并张贴一张三英寸见方的小牌子，上面写着“安全驾驶”。这是一个微不足道的要求，几乎所有人都同意了。但这个要求的影响却非常巨大。因为几周前他们无意中配合了一个无关紧要的安全驾驶请求，这些房主们现在却出奇地乐于配合另一个规模更大的类似请求。

Freedman and Fraser didn't stop there. They tried a slightly different procedure on another sample of homeowners. These people first received a request to sign a petition that favored "keeping California beautiful." Of course, nearly everyone signed, since state beauty, like efficiency in government or sound prenatal care, is one of those issues almost no one is against. After waiting about two weeks, Freedman and Fraser sent a new "volunteer worker" to these same homes to ask the residents to allow the big DRIVE CAREFULLY sign to be erected on their lawns. In some ways, their response was the most astounding of any of the homeowners in the study. Approximately half of these people consented to the installation of the DRIVE CAREFULLY billboard, even though the small commitment they had made weeks earlier was not to driver safety but to an entirely different public-service topic, state beautification.

弗里德曼和弗雷泽并没有就此止步。他们对另一组房主采用了略有不同的方法。这些人首先收到一份请愿书，支持“保持加州美丽”。当然，几乎所有人都签了名，因为州的美丽，就像政府效率或完善的产前护理一样，几乎无人反对。大约两周后，弗里德曼和弗雷泽派了一名新的“志愿者”到这些房主家中，询问他们是否允许在自家草坪上竖立“小心驾驶”的大型标牌。在某种程度上，他们的反应是所有房主中最令人惊讶的。大约有一半的房主同意安装“小心驾驶”的广告牌，尽管他们几周前做出的“小小的承诺”并非为了驾驶安全，而是为了一个完全不同的公共服务议题——州的美丽。

At first, even Freedman and Fraser were bewildered by their findings. Why should the little act of signing a petition supporting state beautification cause people to be so willing to perform a different and much larger favor? After considering and discarding other explanations, Freedman and Fraser came upon one that offered a solution to the puzzle: Signing the beautification petition changed the view these people had of themselves. They saw themselves as public-spirited citizens who acted on their civic principles. When, two weeks later, they were asked to perform another public service by displaying the DRIVE CAREFULLY sign, they complied in order to be consistent with their newly formed self-images. According to Freedman and Fraser,

起初，就连弗里德曼和弗雷泽也对他们的发现感到困惑。为什么签署一份支持州内美化工程的请愿书这样的小事，会让人们如此乐意去做另一件截然不同、意义重大的事呢？在考虑并排除其他解释之后，弗里德曼和弗雷泽找到了一个能够解开这个谜题的答案：签署美化工程的请愿书改变了这些人对自身的看法。他们把自己视为具有公共精神、践行公民原则的公民。两周后，当他们被要求通过展示“小心驾驶”的标志来提供另一项公共服务时，为了与他们新形成的自我认知保持一致，他们欣然接受了。根据弗里德曼和弗雷泽的说法，

What may occur is a change in the person's feelings about getting involved or taking action. Once he has agreed to a request, his attitude may change, he may become, in his own eyes, the kind of person who does this sort of thing, who agrees to requests made by strangers, who takes action on things he believes in, who cooperates with good causes. 6
可能会出现的情况是，当事人对参与或采取行动的感受发生变化。一旦他同意了某个请求，他的态度可能会改变，在他自己看来，他可能会变成那种会做这类事情的人，那种会同意陌生人请求的人，那种会为自己相信的事情采取行动的人，那种会与公益事业合作的人。

What the Freedman and Fraser findings tell us, then, is to be very careful about agreeing to trivial requests. Such an agreement can not only increase our compliance with very similar, much larger re-quests, it can also make us more willing to perform a variety of larger favors that are only remotely connected to the little one we did earlier. It's this second, general kind of influence concealed within small commitments that scares me.

弗里德曼和弗雷泽的研究结果告诉我们，在答应琐碎的请求时务必格外谨慎。这样的承诺不仅会让我们更容易接受类似但更重要的请求，还会让我们更乐意去做各种与之前的小事只有间接联系的大事。正是这种隐藏在小承诺中的普遍影响让我感到担忧。

It scares me enough that I am rarely willing to sign a petition anymore, even for a position I support. Such an action has the potential to influence not only my future behavior but also my self-image in ways I may not want. And once a person's self-image is altered, all sorts of subtle advantages become available to someone who wants to exploit that new image.

这让我感到十分恐惧，以至于我现在很少愿意签署请愿书，即使是支持我所认同的立场。这样的行为不仅可能影响我未来的行为，还可能以我不希望的方式改变我的自我认知。一旦一个人的自我认知发生改变，那些想要利用这种新认知的人就能获得各种微妙的优势。

Who among Freedman and Fraser's homeowners would have thought that the "volunteer worker" who asked them to sign a state beautification petition was really interested in having them display a safe-driving billboard two weeks later? And who among them could have suspected that their decision to display the billboard was largely due to the act of signing the petition? No one, I'd guess. If there were any regrets after the billboard went up, who could they conceivably hold responsible but themselves and their own damnably strong civic spirit? They probably never even considered the guy with the "keeping California beautiful" petition and all that knowledge of jujitsu.

弗里德曼和弗雷泽的房主们，谁会想到，那个请他们签署州政府美化请愿书的“志愿者”，两周后竟然真的想让他们竖起一块安全驾驶的广告牌？他们当中又有谁会想到，竖起这块广告牌的决定，很大程度上要归功于签署请愿书这件事呢？我想，应该没人会想到。如果广告牌竖起来之后他们后悔了，除了他们自己和他们那该死的强烈的公民意识，他们还能怪谁呢？他们大概根本就没想过，那个拿着“保持加州美丽”请愿书、还懂柔术的家伙，会不会有什么阴谋。

Notice that all of the foot-in-the-door experts seem to be excited about the same thing: You can use small commitments to manipulate a person's self-image; you can use them to turn citizens into "public servants," prospects into "customers," prisoners into "collaborators." And once you've got a man's self-image where you want it, he should comply naturally with a whole range of your requests that are consistent with this view of himself.

你会发现，所有“登门槛效应”专家似乎都对同一件事感到兴奋：你可以利用一些小的承诺来操纵一个人的自我认知；你可以用这些承诺把公民变成“公仆”，把潜在客户变成“顾客”，把囚犯变成“合作者”。一旦你成功地塑造了一个人的自我认知，他就会自然而然地接受你提出的各种与这种自我认知相符的要求。

Not all commitments affect self-image, however. There are certain conditions that should be present for a commitment to be effective in this way. To discover what they are, we can once again look to the American experience in the Chinese prison camps of Korea. It is important to understand that the major intent of the Chinese was not simply to extract information from their prisoners. It was to indoctrinate them, to change their attitudes and percep-tions of themselves, of their political system, of their country's role in the war, and of communism. And there is evidence that the program often worked alarmingly well.

然而，并非所有承诺都会影响自我认知。一项承诺要产生这种效果，必须具备某些条件。为了探究这些条件，我们可以再次回顾美国在朝鲜战争中关押中国战俘的经历。重要的是要理解，中国人的主要目的并非仅仅是从战俘身上获取情报，而是要对他们进行灌输，改变他们对自身、对政治制度、对国家在战争中的角色以及对共产主义的态度和认知。而且有证据表明，这项计划往往出奇地有效。

Dr. Henry Segal, chief of the neuropsychiatric evaluation team that examined returning POWs at the war's end, reported that war-related beliefs had been substantially shifted. The majority of the men believed the Chinese story that the United States had used germ warfare, and many felt that their own forces had been the initial aggressors in starting the war. Similar inroads had been made in the political attitudes of the men:

亨利·西格尔博士是战后对归国战俘进行神经精神评估的小组组长，他报告说，战俘们对战争的看法发生了显著转变。大多数战俘相信了中国方面的说法，即美国使用了细菌战，许多人甚至认为他们自己的军队才是挑起战争的侵略者。战俘们的政治态度也发生了类似的转变：

Many expressed antipathy toward the Chinese Communists but at the same time praised them for "the fine job they have done in China." Others stated that "although communism won't work in America, I think it's a good thing for Asia." 7
许多人对中国共产党表示反感，但同时又称赞他们“在中国做得非常出色”。另一些人则表示，“虽然共产主义在美国行不通，但我认为这对亚洲来说是件好事。”

It appears that the real goal of the Chinese was to modify, at least for a time, the hearts and minds of their captives. If we measure their achievement in terms of "defection, disloyalty, changed attitudes and beliefs, poor discipline, poor morale, poor esprit, and doubts as to America's role," Dr. Segal concluded that "their efforts were highly successful." Because commitment tactics were so much a part of the effective Chinese assault on hearts and minds, it is quite informative to examine the specific features of the tactics they used.

看来，中国人的真正目标是至少在一段时间内改变俘虏们的思想和观念。如果我们以“叛逃、不忠、态度和信仰的改变、纪律涣散、士气低落、精神萎靡以及对美国角色产生怀疑”来衡量他们的成果，西格尔博士得出结论：“他们的努力非常成功。” 由于争取支持是中国人有效影响俘虏思想策略的重要组成部分，因此研究他们所使用的具体策略具有重要的参考价值。

The Magic Act

魔术表演

Our best evidence of what people truly feel and believe comes less from their words than from their deeds. Observers trying to decide what a man is like look closely at his actions. What the Chinese have discovered is that the man himself uses this same evidence to decide what he is like. His behavior tells him about himself; it is a primary source of information about his beliefs and values and attitudes. Understanding fully this important principle of self-perception, the Chinese set about arranging the prison-camp experience so that their captives would consistently act in desired ways. Before long, the Chinese knew, these actions would begin to take their toll, causing the men to change their views of themselves to align with what they had done.

我们了解人们真实感受和信念的最佳证据，与其说是来自他们的言语，不如说是来自他们的行为。观察者试图判断一个人的为人时，会仔细观察他的行为。中国人发现，人自己也会利用同样的证据来判断自己。他的行为反映了他自身；这是了解其信仰、价值观和态度的主要信息来源。充分理解了这一重要的自我认知原则后，中国人开始精心安排战俘营的囚禁生活，使俘虏的行为始终符合他们的期望。中国人知道，不久之后，这些行为就会产生影响，使俘虏改变对自身的看法，使其与自己的所作所为相符。

Writing was one sort of confirming action that the Chinese urged incessantly upon the men. It was never enough for the prisoners to listen quietly or even to agree verbally with the Chinese line; they were always pushed to write it down as well. So intent were the Chinese on securing a written statement that if a prisoner was not willing to write a desired response freely, he was prevailed upon to copy it. The American psychologist Edgar Schein describes a standard indoctrination session tactic of the Chinese in these terms:

写作是中国人不断敦促囚犯们采取的一种确认行为。囚犯们仅仅安静地听着，甚至口头上同意中国人的观点，都远远不够；他们总是被强迫写下来。中国人如此执着于获取书面声明，以至于如果囚犯不愿意自由地写下他们想要的答案，就会被强迫抄写。美国心理学家埃德加·沙因（Edgar Schein）用以下的话语描述了中国人常用的灌输策略：

A further technique was to have the man write out the question and then the [pro-Communist] answer. If he refused to write it voluntarily, he was asked to copy it from the notebooks, which must have seemed like a harmless enough concession.
另一种方法是让受试者先写下问题，然后再写下（亲共产主义的）答案。如果他拒绝主动写下来，就要求他从笔记本上抄写，这在他看来似乎是一个无伤大雅的让步。

But, oh, those "harmless" concessions. We've already seen how apparently trifling commitments can lead to extraordinary further behavior. And the Chinese knew that, as a commitment device, a written declaration has some great advantages. First, it provides physical evidence that the act occurred. Once a man wrote what the Chinese wanted, it was very difficult for him to believe that he had not done so. The opportunities to forget or to deny to himself what he had done were not available, as they are for purely verbal statements. No; there it was in his own handwriting, an irrevocably documented act driving him to make his beliefs and his self-image consistent with what he had undeniably done.

但是，哦，那些看似“无害”的让步。我们已经看到，看似微不足道的承诺是如何导致非凡的后续行为的。中国人深知，作为一种承诺手段，书面声明具有诸多优势。首先，它提供了行为发生的实物证据。一旦一个人写下了中国人想要他做的事，他就很难相信自己没有做过。不像口头声明那样，他没有机会忘记或否认自己做过的事。不，那是他亲笔写下的，一份无可辩驳的记录，迫使他让自己的信念和自我认知与他无可否认的行为保持一致。

A second advantage of a written testament is that it can be shown to other people. Of course, that means it can be used to persuade those people. It can persuade them to change their own attitudes in the direction of the statement. But more important for the purpose of commitment, it can persuade them that the author genuinely believes what was written. People have a natural tendency to think that a statement reflects the true attitude of the person who made it. What is surprising is that they continue to think so even when they know that the person did not freely choose to make the statement.

书面遗嘱的第二个优点是可以向他人展示。当然，这意味着它可以用来说服他人，让他们改变自身态度，认同遗嘱中的陈述。但更重要的是，就承诺而言，它可以让他们相信立遗嘱人真心相信自己所写的内容。人们天生倾向于认为，一份声明反映了立遗嘱人的真实想法。令人惊讶的是，即使他们知道立遗嘱人并非出于自愿，他们仍然会这样认为。

Some scientific evidence that this is the case comes from a study by psychologists Edward Jones and James Harris, who showed people an essay that was favorable to Fidel Castro and asked them to guess the true feelings of its author. Jones and Harris told some of these people that the author had chosen to write a pro-Castro essay; and they told the other people that the author had been required to write in favor of Castro. The strange thing was that even those people who knew that the author had been assigned to do a pro-Castro essay guessed that he liked Castro. It seems that a statement of belief produces a click, whirr response in those who view it. Unless there is strong evidence to the contrary, observers automatically assume that someone who makes such a statement means it.

心理学家爱德华·琼斯和詹姆斯·哈里斯的一项研究提供了一些科学证据，支持了这一观点。他们向一些参与者展示了一篇赞扬菲德尔·卡斯特罗的文章，并让他们猜测作者的真实想法。琼斯和哈里斯告诉部分参与者，作者是自愿撰写这篇支持卡斯特罗的文章；而告诉另一些参与者，作者是被要求撰写支持卡斯特罗的文章。奇怪的是，即使是那些知道作者是被指派撰写支持卡斯特罗文章的人，也猜到作者喜欢卡斯特罗。看来，人们在看到某种信念陈述时，会产生一种“咔哒”一声的直觉反应。除非有强有力的反证，否则观察者会自动假设发表这种陈述的人是真心实意的。

Think of the double-barreled effects on the self-image of a prisoner who wrote a pro-Chinese or anti-American statement. Not only was it a lasting personal reminder of his action, it was also likely to persuade those around him that the statement reflected his actual beliefs. And, as we will see in Chapter 4, what those around us think is true of us is enormously important in determining what we ourselves think is true. For example, one study found that after hearing that they were considered charitable people, New Haven, Connecticut, housewives gave much more money to a canvasser from the Multiple Sclerosis Associ-ation. 9 Apparently the mere knowledge that someone viewed them as charitable caused these women to make their actions consistent with another's perception of them.

想想看，如果一个囚犯写下亲华或反美的声明，会对他的自我认知产生怎样的双重影响。这不仅会让他时刻铭记自己的行为，还可能让周围的人误以为这份声明反映了他的真实想法。正如我们将在第四章看到的，周围的人如何看待我们，对我们自己如何看待自己至关重要。例如，一项研究发现，康涅狄格州纽黑文的家庭主妇们在得知自己被认为乐善好施之后，会向多发性硬化症协会的募捐人员捐赠更多钱。显然，仅仅是知道有人认为她们乐善好施，就促使这些女性调整自己的行为，以符合他人对她们的看法。

Once an active commitment is made, then, self-image is squeezed from both sides by consistency pressures. From the inside, there is a pressure to bring self-image into line with action. From the outside, there is a sneakier pressure—a tendency to adjust this image according to the way others perceive us. And because others see us as believing what we have written (even when we've had little choice in the matter), we will once again experience a pull to bring self-image into line with the written statement.

一旦做出积极的承诺，自我形象就会受到来自两方面的压力。一方面，内心会有一种压力，促使自我形象与行动保持一致；另一方面，外部则存在一种更为隐蔽的压力——一种根据他人对我们的看法调整自我形象的倾向。而且，由于他人会认为我们相信自己写下的内容（即便我们对此几乎别无选择），我们又会再次感受到一种拉扯，促使自我形象与书面声明保持一致。

In Korea, several subtle devices were used to get the prisoners to write, without direct coercion, what the Chinese wanted. For example, the Chinese knew that many prisoners were eager to let their families know that they were alive. At the same time, the men knew that their captors were censoring the mails and that only some letters were being allowed out of camp. To ensure that their own letters would be released, some prisoners began including in their messages peace appeals, claims of kind treatment, and statements sympathetic to communism. The hope was that the Chinese would want such letters to surface and would, therefore, allow their delivery. Of course, the Chinese were happy to cooperate because those letters served their interests marvelously. First, their worldwide propaganda effort benefited greatly from the appearance of pro-Communist statements by American servicemen. Second, in the service of prisoner indoctrination, they had, without raising a finger of physical force, gotten many men to go on record as supporting the Chinese cause.

在朝鲜，中方运用了多种巧妙的手段，在不直接胁迫的情况下，让战俘写下他们想要的东西。例如，中方知道许多战俘都渴望让家人知道自己还活着。与此同时，战俘们也知道，他们的看守会审查邮件，只有部分信件被允许寄出。为了确保自己的信件能够被释放，一些战俘开始在信中加入和平呼吁、声称自己受到优待以及同情共产主义的言论。他们希望中方会乐于看到这些信件，从而允许它们被送出。当然，中方也乐于配合，因为这些信件对他们的利益大有裨益。首先，美国军人发表亲共言论极大地促进了中方在全球范围内的宣传活动。其次，为了对战俘进行思想灌输，中方在不动用任何武力的情况下，就让许多人公开表示支持中国事业。

A similar technique involved political essay contests that were regularly held in camp. The prizes for winning were invariably small—a few cigarettes or a bit of fruit—but were sufficiently scarce that they generated a lot of interest from the men. Usually the winning essay was one that took a solidly pro-Communist stand...but not always. The Chinese were wise enough to realize that most of the prisoners would not enter a contest that they could win only by writing a Communist tract. And the Chinese were clever enough to know how to plant small commitments to communism in the men that could be nurtured into later bloom. So the prize was occasionally given to an essay that generally supported the United States but that bowed once or twice to the Chinese view. The effects of this strategy were exactly what the Chinese wanted. The men continued to participate voluntarily in the contests because they saw that they could win with an essay highly favorable to their own country. But perhaps without realizing it, they began to shade their essays a bit toward communism in order to have a better chance of winning. The Chinese were ready to pounce on any concession to Communist dogma and to bring consistency pressures to bear upon it. In the case of a written declaration within a voluntary essay, they had a perfect commitment from which to build toward collaboration and conversion.

类似的策略之一是定期在集中营举办政治征文比赛。奖品总是微不足道——几支香烟或一些水果——但数量稀少，足以引起战俘们的极大兴趣。通常，获奖文章都明确持亲共立场……但并非总是如此。中国人很清楚，大多数战俘不会参加那种只有写一篇共产主义宣传文章才能获胜的比赛。中国人也足够聪明，懂得如何在战俘心中埋下对共产主义的种子，并加以培育，使其日后开花结果。因此，奖项有时会颁给那些总体上支持美国，但偶尔也会向中国观点妥协的文章。这种策略的效果正是中国人所希望的。战俘们继续自愿参加比赛，因为他们看到，只要写一篇高度有利于自己国家的文章就能获胜。但或许他们自己并没有意识到，为了增加获胜的几率，他们开始在文章中略微倾向于共产主义。中国人随时准备抓住任何向共产主义教条做出的让步，并施加前后一致的压力。如果是在一篇自愿发表的文章中附有书面声明，他们就拥有了完美的承诺，可以以此为基础，推动合作和转变。

Other compliance professionals also know about the committing power of written statements. The enormously successful Amway Corporation, for instance, has hit upon a way to spur their sales personnel to greater and greater accomplishments. Members of the staff are asked to set individual sales goals and commit themselves to those goals by personally recording them on paper:

其他合规专业人士也深知书面声明的约束力。例如，业绩斐然的安利公司就找到了一种方法来激励销售人员取得更大的成就。公司要求员工设定个人销售目标，并通过亲自将目标记录在纸上来确保自己能够实现这些目标。

One final tip before you get started: Set a goal and write it down. Whatever the goal, the important thing is that you set it, so you've got something for which to aim—and that you write it down. There is something magical about writing things down. So set a goal and write it down. When you reach that goal, set another and write that down. You'll be off and running.
开始之前，最后一个建议：设定目标并写下来。无论目标是什么，重要的是你要设定它，这样你才有努力的方向——而且一定要把它写下来。把事情写下来有一种神奇的力量。所以，设定一个目标并写下来。当你实现这个目标后，再设定另一个目标并写下来。这样你就能步入正轨了。

If the Amway people have found "something magical about writing things down," so have other business organizations. Some door-to-door sales companies use the magic of written commitments to battle the "cooling-off" laws recently passed in many states. The laws are designed to allow customers a few days after purchasing an item to cancel the sale and receive a full refund. At first this legislation hurt the hard-sell companies deeply. Because they emphasize high-pressure tactics, their customers often buy, not because they want the product but because they are duped or intimidated into the sale. When the new laws went into effect, these customers began canceling in droves.

如果安利的人发现了“把事情写下来有神奇的魔力”，那么其他商业机构也发现了。一些上门推销公司利用书面承诺的魔力来对抗许多州最近通过的“冷静期”法律。这些法律旨在允许顾客在购买商品后的几天内取消订单并获得全额退款。起初，这项立法对那些强买强卖的公司造成了沉重打击。由于这些公司强调高压销售策略，他们的顾客往往并非出于购买意愿，而是被欺骗或胁迫才购买的。新法律生效后，这些顾客开始大量取消订单。

The companies have since learned a beautifully simple trick that cuts the number of such cancellations drastically. They merely have the customer, rather than the salesman, fill out the sales agreement. According to the sales-training program of a prominent encyclopedia company, that personal commitment alone has proved to be "a very important psychological aid in preventing customers from backing out of their contracts." Like the Amway Corporation, then, these organizations have found that something special happens when people personally put their commitments on paper: They live up to what they have written down.

这些公司后来发现了一个简单有效的技巧，可以大幅减少此类取消订单的情况。他们只需让客户而非销售人员填写销售协议即可。据一家知名百科全书公司的销售培训项目显示，这种个人承诺本身就“在防止客户违约方面起到了非常重要的心理作用”。因此，与安利公司一样，这些机构发现，当人们亲自将承诺写在纸上时，会产生一种奇妙的效果：他们会履行自己写下的承诺。

Another common way for businesses to cash in on the "magic" of written declarations occurs through the use of an innocent-looking promotional device. Before I began to study weapons of social influence, I used to wonder why big companies such as Procter & Gamble and General Foods are always running those "25-, 50-, or 100 words or less" testimonial contests. They all seem to be alike. The contestant is to compose a short personal statement that begins with the words, "Why I like." and goes on to laud the features of whatever cake mix or floor wax happens to be at issue. The company judges the entries and awards some stunningly large prizes to the winners. What had puzzled me was what the companies got out of the deal. Often the contest requires no purchase; anyone submitting an entry is eligible. Yet, the companies appear to be strangely willing to incur the huge costs of contest after contest.

企业利用书面声明的“魔力”牟利的另一种常见方式，是使用看似无害的促销手段。在我开始研究社会影响力武器之前，我一直很疑惑，为什么像宝洁和通用食品这样的大公司总是举办“25字、50字或100字以内”的证言征集活动。这些活动似乎都大同小异。参赛者需要撰写一段简短的个人陈述，以“我喜欢”开头，然后赞扬某种蛋糕粉或地板蜡等产品的特性。公司会评选参赛作品，并为获奖者颁发丰厚的奖品。我一直不明白的是，这些公司究竟能从中获得什么好处。通常，这些比赛无需购买任何产品；任何提交作品的人都有资格参赛。然而，这些公司似乎却乐于承担一次又一次比赛的巨额成本。

I am no longer puzzled. The purpose behind the testimonial contests is the same as the purpose behind the political essay contests of the Chinese Communists. In both instances, the aim is to get as many people as possible to go on record as liking the product. In Korea, the product was a brand of Chinese communism; in the United States, it might be a brand of cuticle remover. The type of product doesn't matter; the process is the same. Participants voluntarily write essays for attractive prizes that they have only a small chance to win. But they know that for an essay to have any chance of winning at all, it must include praise for the product. So they find praiseworthy features of the product and describe them in their essays. The result is hundreds of men in Korea or hundreds of thousands of people in America who testify in writing to the product's appeal and who, consequently, experience that "magical" pull to believe what they have written.

我不再感到困惑。这些证言竞赛背后的目的与中国共产党的政治征文比赛如出一辙。两者的目的都是为了让尽可能多的人公开表示喜欢该产品。在韩国，该产品是中国共产主义的象征；在美国，它可能是一种角质去除剂。产品类型并不重要，重要的是过程。参与者自愿撰写文章，以争取诱人的奖品，尽管中奖几率很小。但他们知道，要想文章有机会获奖，就必须包含对产品的赞美之词。因此，他们会找出产品值得称赞的特点，并在文章中加以描述。结果是，韩国成百上千的人或美国的数十万人以书面形式证明产品的吸引力，并因此体验到那种“神奇”的吸引力，相信自己所写的内容。

The Public Eye

公众之眼

One reason that written testaments are effective in bringing about genuine personal change is that they can so easily be made public. The prisoner experience in Korea showed the Chinese to be quite aware of an important psychological principle: Public commitments tend to be lasting commitments. The Chinese constantly arranged to have the proCommunist statements of their captives seen by others. A man who had written a political essay the Chinese liked, for example, might find copies of it posted around camp, or might be asked to read it to a prisoner discussion group, or even to read it on the camp radio broadcast. As far as the Chinese were concerned, the more public the better. Why?

书面证词之所以能有效促成真正的个人改变，其中一个原因在于它们很容易被公开。朝鲜战争期间的战俘经历表明，中国人非常清楚一个重要的心理学原理：公开的承诺往往是持久的承诺。中国人不断安排让战俘的亲共声明被他人看到。例如，如果有人写了一篇中国人喜欢的政治文章，他的文章可能会被张贴在营地各处，或者被要求在战俘讨论小组中朗读，甚至在营地广播中朗读。在中国人看来，越公开越好。为什么呢？

Whenever one takes a stand that is visible to others, there arises a drive to maintain that stand in order to look like a consistent person. Remember that earlier in this chapter we described how desirable good personal consistency is as a trait; how someone without it could be judged as fickle, uncertain, pliant, scatterbrained, or unstable; how someone with it is viewed as rational, assured, trustworthy, and sound. Given this context, it is hardly surprising that people try to avoid the look of inconsistency. For appearances' sake, then, the more public a stand, the more reluctant we will be to change it.

当一个人公开表明立场时，就会产生一种维持立场的动力，以显得自己言行一致。请记住，本章前面我们曾描述过，良好的个人一致性是一种多么可贵的品质；缺乏这种一致性的人可能会被认为反复无常、优柔寡断、唯唯诺诺、心不在焉或不稳定；而拥有这种一致性的人则会被视为理性、自信、值得信赖且稳重可靠。鉴于此，人们试图避免给人留下言行不一的印象也就不足为奇了。因此，为了维护形象，我们的立场越是公开，就越不愿意改变。

An illustration of how public commitments can lead to doggedly consistent further action is provided in a famous experiment performed by a pair of prominent social psychologists, Morton Deutsch and Harold Gerard. The basic procedure was to have college students first estimate in their own minds the length of lines they were shown. At this point, one sample of the students had to commit themselves publicly to their initial judgments by writing them down, signing their names to them, and turning them in to the experimenter. A second sample of students also committed themselves to their first estimates, but they did so privately by putting them on a Magic Writing Pad and then erasing them by lifting the Magic Pad's plastic cover before anyone could see what they had written. A third set of students did not commit themselves to their initial estimates at all; they just kept the estimates in mind privately.

著名社会心理学家莫顿·德意志和哈罗德·杰拉德进行的一项著名实验，生动地展现了公开承诺如何促成坚定不移的后续行动。实验的基本流程是：首先让大学生们在脑海中估算他们看到的线条的长度。然后，一组学生必须公开承诺他们最初的判断，将估算结果写下来，签名后交给实验人员。另一组学生也同样承诺了他们的估算结果，但他们是私下进行的：将估算结果写在“神奇写字板”上，然后在任何人看到之前揭开写字板的塑料盖将其擦除。第三组学生则完全没有承诺他们的估算结果，他们只是将这些估算结果记在心里。

In these ways, Deutsch and Gerard had cleverly arranged for some students to commit themselves publicly, some privately, and some not at all to their initial decisions. What Deutsch and Gerard wanted to find out was which of the three types of students would be most inclined to stick with their first judgments after receiving information that those judgments were incorrect. So all of the students were given new evidence suggesting that their initial estimates were wrong, and they were then given the chance to change their estimates.

通过这些巧妙的安排，德意志和杰拉德让一些学生公开表态，一些学生私下表态，还有一些学生则完全不表态。他们想要探究的是，在得知最初的判断是错误的之后，这三种类型的学生中哪一种最倾向于坚持自己的判断。因此，所有学生都获得了新的证据，表明他们最初的估计是错误的，然后他们有机会改变自己的估计。

The results were quite clear. The students who had never written down their first choices were the least loyal to those choices. When new evidence was presented that questioned the wisdom of decisions that had never left their heads, these students were the most influenced by the new information to change what they had viewed as the "correct" decision. Compared to these uncommitted students, those who had merely written their decisions for a moment on a Magic Pad were significantly less willing to change their minds when given the chance. Even though they had committed themselves under the most anonymous of circumstances, the act of writing down their first judgments caused them to resist the influence of contradictory new data and to remain consistent with the preliminary choices. But Deutsch and Gerard found that, by far, it was the students who had publicly recorded their initial positions who most resolutely refused to shift from those positions later. Public commitment had hardened them into the most stubborn of all.

结果非常明确。那些从未写下最初选择的学生，对这些选择的忠诚度最低。当出现质疑他们脑海中从未动摇过的决定的新证据时，这些学生最容易受到新信息的影响，从而改变他们原本认为的“正确”选择。与这些没有明确表态的学生相比，那些仅仅在电子记事本上匆匆写下决定的学生，在有机会改变主意时，明显更不愿意改变。即使他们是在最匿名的情况下做出决定的，但写下最初判断的行为仍然使他们能够抵制矛盾的新数据的影响，并坚持最初的选择。然而，德意志和杰拉德发现，迄今为止，最坚决不肯改变立场的，反而是那些公开记录了最初立场的学生。公开表态使他们变得最为固执。

This sort of stubbornness can occur even in situations where accuracy should be more important than consistency. In one study, when six- or twelve-person experimental juries were deciding a close case, hung juries were significantly more frequent if the jurors had to express their opinions with a visible show of hands rather than by secret ballot. Once jurors had stated their initial views publicly, they were reluctant to allow themselves to change publicly, either. Should you ever find yourself as the foreperson of a jury under these conditions, then, you could reduce the risk of a^hung jury by choosing a secret rather than public balloting technique.

这种固执甚至在准确性比一致性更重要的情况下也会出现。一项研究表明，当由六人或十二人组成的实验陪审团审理一起势均力敌的案件时，如果陪审员必须以公开举手的方式表达意见，而不是通过秘密投票，则陪审团无法达成一致意见的情况会显著增加。一旦陪审员公开表达了他们的初步意见，他们也不愿意公开改变自己的看法。因此，如果您不幸成为此类情况下的陪审团主席，您可以通过选择秘密投票而非公开投票的方式来降低陪审团无法达成一致意见的风险。

The Deutsch and Gerard finding that we are truest to our decisions if we have bound ourselves to them publicly can be put to good use. Consider the organizations dedicated to helping people rid themselves of bad habits. Many weight-reduction clinics, for instance, understand that often a person's private decision to lose weight will be too weak to withstand the blandishments of bakery windows, wafting cooking scents, and late-night Sara Lee commercials. So they see to it that the decision is buttressed by the pillars of public commitment. They require their clients to write down an immediate weight-loss goal and show that goal to as many friends, relatives, and neighbors as possible. Clinic operators report that frequently this simple technique works where all else has failed.

德意志和杰拉德的研究发现，如果我们公开承诺，就会更加忠于自己的决定，这一发现可以得到很好的应用。想想那些致力于帮助人们戒除不良习惯的机构。例如，许多减肥诊所都明白，人们私下里决定减肥往往难以抵挡面包店橱窗的诱惑、飘来的烹饪香味以及深夜播放的莎莉·李（Sara Lee）广告。因此，他们会确保人们的决心得到公开承诺的支撑。他们要求客户写下一个近期减肥目标，并尽可能多地向朋友、亲戚和邻居展示这个目标。诊所经营者表示，这种简单的方法往往在其他方法都无效的情况下也能奏效。

Of course, there's no need to pay a special clinic in order to engage a visible commitment as an ally. One San Diego woman described to me how she employed a public promise to help herself finally stop smoking:

当然，并不需要花钱去专门的诊所才能公开表明自己是戒烟盟友。一位圣地亚哥的女士向我讲述了她如何通过公开承诺最终成功戒烟：

I remember it was after I heard about another scientific study showing that smoking causes cancer. Every time one of those things came out, I used to get determined to quit, but I never could. This time, though, I decided I had to do something. I'm a proud person. It matters to me if other people see me in a bad light. So I thought, "Maybe I can use that pride to help me dump this damn habit." So I made a list of all the people who I really wanted to respect me. Then I went out and got some blank business cards and I wrote on the back of each card, "I promise you that I will never smoke another cigarette."
我记得那是在我听到又一项科学研究表明吸烟致癌之后。以前每次听到这类消息，我都会下定决心戒烟，但总是失败。不过这次，我决定必须做点什么。我是一个自尊心很强的人。我很在意别人怎么看我。所以我想：“也许我可以利用这份自尊来帮助我戒掉这个该死的习惯。”于是，我列了一张名单，上面都是我真心希望得到我尊重的人。然后我去买了一些空白的名片，在每张名片的背面写着：“我保证我再也不会抽烟了。”

Within a week, I had given or sent a signed card to everybody on the list—my dad, my brother back East, my boss, my best girlfriend, my ex-husband, everybody but one—the guy I was dating then. I was just crazy about him, and I really wanted him to value me as a person. Believe me, I thought twice about giving him a card because I knew that if I couldn't keep my promise to him I'd die. But one day at the of-fice—he worked in the same building as I did—I just walked up to him, handed him the card, and walked away without saying anything.

不到一周，我就把签名的卡片送给了名单上的所有人——我爸、远在东部的哥哥、我的老板、我最好的闺蜜、我的前夫，除了一个人——我当时交往的那个男生。我当时对他简直着迷，真心希望他能珍惜我这个人。说实话，我犹豫了好久才决定要不要给他送卡片，因为我知道如果我不能信守对他的承诺，我会崩溃的。但有一天在办公室——他和我在同一栋楼里办公——我径直走到他面前，把卡片递给他，然后一句话也没说就走了。

Quitting "cold turkey" was the hardest thing I've ever done. There must have been a thousand times when I thought I had to have a smoke. But whenever that happened, I'd just picture how all of the people on my list, especially this one guy, would think less of me if I couldn't stick to my guns. And that's all it took. I've never taken another puff.

戒烟“突然戒断”是我做过的最难的事。我肯定有上千次都想抽烟。但每次这样想的时候，我就会想象，如果我坚持不下去，我名单上的所有人，特别是那个人，会怎么看我。就这么简单。我再也没抽过烟。

You know, the interesting thing is the guy turned out to be a real schmuck. I can't figure out what I saw in him back then. But at the time, without knowing it, he helped me get through the toughest part of the toughest thing I've ever had to do. I don't even like him anymore. Still, I do feel grateful in a way because I think he saved my life.

你知道吗，最有意思的是，那家伙后来证明是个十足的混蛋。我真想不明白当时我到底看上他哪一点。但当时，他无意中帮我度过了人生中最艰难的时刻。我现在甚至都不喜欢他了。不过，从某种程度上来说，我还是挺感激他的，因为我觉得他救了我的命。

The Effort Extra

额外付出

Yet another reason that written commitments are so effective is that they require more work than verbal ones. And the evidence is clear that the more effort that goes into a commitment, the greater is its ability to influence the attitudes of the person who made it. We can find that evidence quite close to home or as far away as the back regions of the primitive world. For example, there is a tribe in southern Africa, the Thonga, that requires each of its boys to go through an elaborate initiation ceremony before he can be counted a man of the tribe. As with many other primitive peoples, a Thonga boy endures a great deal before he is admitted to adult membership in the group. Anthropologists Whiting, Kluckhohn, and Anthony have described this three-month ordeal in brief but vivid terms:

书面承诺之所以如此有效，另一个原因是它比口头承诺需要付出更多努力。而且有确凿的证据表明，投入到承诺中的努力越多，它对做出承诺者的态度的影响力就越大。我们可以在身边找到这样的证据，也可以在遥远的原始世界找到。例如，在南部非洲的通加部落，每个男孩都必须经历一套复杂的成人礼才能被视为部落的成年成员。与其他许多原始部落一样，通加男孩在被接纳为部落成年成员之前，要经历许多磨难。人类学家惠廷、克拉克洪和安东尼用简洁而生动的语言描述了这三个月的考验：

When a boy is somewhere between 10 and 16 years of age, he is sent by his parents to "circumcision school," which is held every 4 or 5 years. Here in company with his age-mates he undergoes severe hazing by the adult males of the society. The initiation begins when each boy runs the gauntlet between two rows of men who beat him with clubs. At the end of this experience he is stripped of his clothes and his hair is cut. He is next met by a man covered with lion manes and is seated upon a stone facing this "lion man." Someone then strikes him from behind and when he turns his head to see who has struck him, his foreskin is seized and in two movements cut off by the "lion man." Afterward he is secluded for three months in the "yard of mysteries," where he can be seen only by the initiated.
男孩大约在10到16岁之间，会被父母送到“割礼学校”，这种学校每4到5年举办一次。在那里，他会和同龄人一起，接受成年男性的严酷考验。入会仪式从每个男孩从两排用棍棒殴打的男子中间穿过开始。仪式结束后，男孩会被剥光衣服，头发也会被剪掉。接下来，他会见到一个浑身长满狮鬃的男人，并被安排坐在一块石头上，面对着这个“狮人”。这时，有人会从背后袭击他，当他转头去看是谁打他时，“狮人”会抓住他的包皮，两下就将其割掉。之后，男孩会被隔离在“神秘庭院”三个月，只有入会者才能见到他。
During the course of his initiation, the boy undergoes six major trials: beatings, exposure to cold, thirst, eating of unsavory foods, punishment, and the threat of death. On the slightest pretext, he may be beaten by one of the newly initiated men, who is assigned to the task by the older men of the tribe. He sleeps without covering and suffers bitterly from the winter cold. He is forbidden to drink a drop of water during the whole three months. Meals are often made nauseating by the half-digested grass from the stomach of an antelope, which is poured over his food. If he is caught breaking any important rule governing the ceremony, he is severely punished. For example, in one of these punishments, sticks are placed between the fingers of the offender, then a strong man closes his hand around that of the novice, practically crushing his fingers. He is frightened into submission by being told that in former times boys who had tried to escape or who had revealed the secrets to women or to the uninitiated were hanged and their bodies burned to ashes. 1
在入会仪式期间，男孩要经历六项重大考验：鞭打、严寒、干渴、食用难以下咽的食物、惩罚以及死亡的威胁。他稍有不慎，就会被部落中由长者指派的新晋男子鞭打。他睡觉时不盖被子，饱受冬日严寒的折磨。整整三个月，他都被禁止饮水。饭菜里常常会浇上半消化的羚羊胃里的草，令人作呕。如果他违反了任何重要的仪式规则，就会受到严厉的惩罚。例如，其中一种惩罚是，将木棍夹在犯错者的手指间，然后一个壮汉会紧紧抓住他的手，几乎要将他的手指捏碎。他被告知，过去那些试图逃跑或向女人或未入会者泄露秘密的男孩都会被绞死，尸体还会被焚烧成灰烬，这吓得他乖乖就范。

On the face of it, these rites seem extraordinary and bizarre. Yet, at the same time, they can be seen to be remarkably similar in principle and even in detail to the common initiation ceremonies of school fraternities. During the traditional "Hell Week" held yearly on college campuses, fraternity pledges must persevere through a variety of activities designed by the older members to test the limits of physical exertion, psychological strain, and social embarrassment. At week's end, the boys who have persisted through the ordeal are accepted for full group membership. Mostly their tribulations have left them no more than greatly tired and a bit shaky, although sometimes the negative effects are more serious.

乍看之下，这些仪式似乎非同寻常，甚至匪夷所思。然而，与此同时，它们在原则上乃至细节上，都与学校兄弟会的入会仪式惊人地相似。在大学校园每年举行的传统“地狱周”期间，兄弟会的新成员必须坚持完成由老成员设计的各种活动，这些活动旨在考验他们的体能极限、心理承受能力和社交尴尬程度。一周结束后，那些坚持下来的男生将被正式接纳为兄弟会成员。大多数情况下，他们的磨难只会让他们感到筋疲力尽、有些虚弱，尽管有时负面影响会更加严重。

What is interesting is how closely the particular features of Hell Week tasks match those of the tribal initiation rites. Recall that anthropologists identified six major trials to be endured by a Thonga initiate during his stay in the "yard of mysteries." A scan of newspaper reports shows that each trial also has its place in the hazing rituals of Greek-letter societies:

有趣的是，“地狱周”任务的具体内容与部落的入会仪式竟如此相似。回想一下，人类学家曾指出，通加族新成员在“神秘庭院”期间要经历六项主要考验。浏览报纸报道可知，每项考验在希腊字母兄弟会的入会仪式中也都有其对应之处：

  • Beatings. Fourteen-year-old Michael Kalogris spent three weeks in a Long Island hospital recovering from internal injuries suffered during a Hell Night initiation ceremony of his high-school fraternity, Omega Gamma Delta. He had been administered the "atomic bomb" by his prospective brothers, who told him to hold his hands over his head and keep them there while they gathered around to slam fists into his stomach and back simultaneously and repeatedly.

    殴打。14岁的迈克尔·卡洛格里斯在长岛一家医院住了三个星期，治疗他在高中兄弟会欧米伽伽玛德尔塔的“地狱之夜”入会仪式上遭受的内伤。他的准兄弟们对他施以“原子弹”般的酷刑：他们命令他双手举过头顶，保持这个姿势，然后围拢过来，同时反复地用拳头猛击他的腹部和背部。
  • Exposure to cold. On a winter night, Frederick Bronner, a California junior-college student, was taken three thousand feet up and ten miles into the hills of a national forest by his prospective fraternity brothers. Left to find his way home wearing only a thin sweatshirt and slacks, Fat Freddy, as he was called, shivered in a frigid wind until he tumbled down a steep ravine, fracturing bones and hurting his head. Prevented by his injuries from going on, he huddled there against the cold until he died of exposure.

    暴露于严寒之中。在一个冬夜，加州一所专科学校的学生弗雷德里克·布朗纳被他未来的兄弟会成员带到国家森林公园的山上，海拔三千英尺，行程十英里。他只穿着一件薄薄的运动衫和休闲裤，被人戏称为“胖弗雷迪”，独自一人摸索回家的路。凛冽的寒风中瑟瑟发抖，他不慎跌落陡峭的山沟，摔断了骨头，头部也受了伤。由于伤势过重，他无法继续前行，只能蜷缩在山沟里抵御严寒，最终冻死。
  • Thirst. Two Ohio State University freshmen found themselves in the "dungeon" of their prospective fraternity house after breaking the rule requiring all pledges to crawl into the dining area prior to Hell Week meals. Once locked in the house storage closet, they were given only salty foods to eat for nearly two days. Nothing was provided for drinking purposes except a pair of plastic cups in which they could catch their own urine.

    口渴。两名俄亥俄州立大学新生因违反兄弟会规定而被关进了他们即将加入的兄弟会的“地牢”。兄弟会规定所有新成员在“地狱周”用餐前必须爬进餐厅。他们被锁在兄弟会的储物间里，近两天来只能吃到咸味食物。除了两个用来接尿液的塑料杯外，没有任何其他饮用水。
  • Eating of unsavory foods. At Kappa Sigma house on the campus of the University of Southern California, the eyes of eleven pledges bulged when they saw the sickening task before them. Eleven quarter-pound slabs of raw liver lay on a tray. Cut thick and soaked in oil, each was to be swallowed whole, one to a boy. Gagging and choking repeatedly, young Richard Swanson failed three times to down his piece.
