Determined to succeed, he finally got the oil-soaked meat into his throat where it lodged and, despite all efforts to remove it, killed him.

    吞食令人作呕的食物。在南加州大学校园内的卡帕西格玛兄弟会会所，11名新成员看到眼前令人作呕的任务时，都瞪大了眼睛。托盘上放着11块四分之一磅重的生肝。这些肝切得很厚，浸泡在油里，每块都要一口吞下，每个男孩一块。年轻的理查德·斯旺森（Richard Swanson）三次尝试吞下自己的那块肝，都失败了，他反复干呕、呛咳。但他决心要成功，最终还是把这块浸透了油的肉吞进了喉咙，卡住了，尽管他竭尽全力想把它取出来，但最终还是死了。
  • Punishment. In Wisconsin, a pledge who forgot one section of a ritual incantation to be memorized by all initiates was punished for his error. He was required to keep his feet under the rear legs of a folding chair while the heaviest of his fraternity brothers sat down and drank a beer. Although the pledge did not cry out during the punishment, a bone in each of his feet was broken.

    惩罚。在威斯康星州，一名新入会成员忘记了所有新成员都必须记住的仪式咒语的一部分，因此受到了惩罚。他被要求将双脚放在折叠椅的后腿下，而他兄弟会中最重的一位成员则坐在椅子上喝啤酒。尽管这名新成员在受罚过程中没有发出任何声音，但他的双脚各断了一根骨头。
  • Threats of death. A pledge of Zeta Beta Tau fraternity was taken to a beach area of New Jersey and told to dig his "own grave." Seconds after he complied with orders to lie flat in the finished hole, the sides collapsed, suffocating him before his prospective fraternity brothers could dig him out.

    死亡威胁。一名 Zeta Beta Tau 兄弟会的入会新生被带到新泽西州的海滩，并被告知要挖自己的“坟墓”。他遵照命令平躺在挖好的坑里几秒钟后，坑壁坍塌，在他未来的兄弟会成员来得及把他挖出来之前，他就窒息而亡了。

There is another striking similarity between the initiation rites of tribal and fraternal societies: They simply will not die. Resisting all attempts to eliminate or suppress them, such hazing practices have been phenomenally resilient. Authorities, in the form of colonial governments or university administrations, have tried threats, social pressures, legal actions, banishments, bribes, and bans to persuade the groups to remove the hazards and humiliations from their initiation ceremonies. None has been successful. Oh, there may be a change while the authority is watching closely. But this is usually more apparent than real, the harsher trials occurring under more secret circumstances until the pressure is off and they can surface again.

部落和兄弟会的入会仪式还有另一个惊人的相似之处：它们顽强地存在着，难以消亡。这些欺凌习俗顽强地抵抗着一切试图消除或压制它们的努力。无论是殖民政府还是大学管理部门，都曾尝试过威胁、社会压力、法律诉讼、驱逐、贿赂和禁令等手段，试图说服这些团体消除入会仪式中的危险和羞辱。但这些努力都以失败告终。或许在当局的密切关注下，情况会有所改变。但这通常只是表面现象，真正的考验往往在更加隐秘的情况下进行，直到压力解除，它们才会再次浮出水面。

On some college campuses, officials have tried to eliminate dangerous hazing practices by substituting a "Help Week" of civic service or by taking direct control of the initiation rituals. When such attempts are not slyly circumvented by fraternities, they are met with outright physical resistance. For example, in the aftermath of Richard Swanson's choking death at USC, the university president issued new rules requiring that all pledging activities be reviewed by school authorities before going into effect and that adult advisers be present during initiation ceremonies. According to one national magazine, "The new 'code' set off a riot so violent that city police and fire detachments were afraid to enter campus."

在一些大学校园里，校方试图通过设立“社区服务周”或直接接管入会仪式来消除危险的欺凌行为。然而，当兄弟会没有巧妙地规避这些措施时，就会遭到公开的暴力抵抗。例如，在南加州大学理查德·斯旺森被勒死后，该校校长颁布了新规，要求所有入会活动在生效前都必须经过校方审查，并且入会仪式期间必须有成年顾问在场。据一家全国性杂志报道，“这项新规引发了一场极其激烈的骚乱，以至于市警察和消防部门都不敢进入校园。”

Resigning themselves to the inevitable, other college representatives have given up on the possibility of abolishing the degradations of Hell Week. "If hazing is a universal human activity, and every bit of evidence points to this conclusion, you most likely won't be able to ban it effectively. Refuse to allow it openly and it will go underground. You can't ban sex, you can't prohibit alcohol, and you probably can't eliminate hazing!"

其他大学代表无奈地接受了现实，放弃了废除“地狱周”羞辱性行为的希望。“如果欺凌是人类普遍存在的现象，而且所有证据都指向这个结论，那么你很可能无法有效地禁止它。拒绝公开允许它，它就会转入地下。你无法禁止性行为，你无法禁止饮酒，你大概也无法根除欺凌！”

What is it about hazing practices that make them so precious to these societies? What could make the groups want to evade, undermine, or contest any effort to ban the degrading and perilous features of their initiation rites? Some have argued that the groups themselves are composed of psychological or social miscreants whose twisted needs demand that others be harmed and humiliated. But the evidence does not support such a view. Studies done on the personality traits of fraternity members, for instance, show them to be, if anything, slightly healthier than other college students in their psychological adjustment. Similarly, fraternities are known for their willingness to engage in beneficial community projects for the general social good. What they are not willing to do, however, is substitute these projects for their initiation ceremonies. One survey at the University of Washington found that, of the fraternity chapters examined, most had a type of Help Week tradition but that this community service was in addition to Hell Week. In only one case was such service directly related to initiation procedures.

究竟是什么让这些社团如此珍视入会仪式中的欺凌行为？又是什么原因促使他们想要逃避、破坏或反对任何禁止这些有辱人格且危险的入会仪式的努力？有人认为，这些社团本身就是由心理或社会上的恶棍组成，他们扭曲的需求驱使他们伤害和羞辱他人。但证据并不支持这种观点。例如，对兄弟会成员人格特征的研究表明，他们的心理适应能力甚至比其他大学生略好一些。同样，兄弟会也以积极参与有益于社会公益的社区项目而闻名。然而，他们却不愿意用这些项目来取代他们的入会仪式。华盛顿大学的一项调查发现，在接受调查的兄弟会分会中，大多数都有类似“援助周”的传统，但这种社区服务是在“地狱周”之外进行的。只有一种情况是，这种服务与入会程序直接相关。

The picture that emerges of the perpetrators of hazing practices is of normal individuals who tend to be psychologically stable and socially concerned but who become aberrantly harsh as a group at only one time—immediately before the admission of new members to the society. The evidence, then, points to the ceremony as the culprit. There must be something about its rigors that is vital to the group. There must be some function to its harshness that the group will fight relentlessly to maintain. What?

由此可见，欺凌行为的实施者通常是心理稳定、关心社会的普通人，但他们却会在某个特定时刻——新成员入会仪式之前——集体变得异常严苛。由此可见，罪魁祸首正是仪式本身。仪式的严苛必然对这个群体至关重要。这种严苛必然有其存在的意义，以至于这个群体会不遗余力地维护它。究竟是什么呢？

My own view is that the answer appeared in 1959 in the results of a study little known outside of social psychology. A pair of young researchers, Elliot Aronson and Judson Mills, decided to test their observation that "persons who go through a great deal of trouble or pain to attain something tend to value it more highly than persons who attain the same thing with a minimum of effort." The real stroke of inspiration came in their choice of the initiation ceremony as the best place to examine this possibility. They found that college women who had to endure a severely embarrassing initiation ceremony in order to gain access to a sex discussion group convinced themselves that their new group and its discussions were extremely valuable, even though Aronson and Mills had previously rehearsed the other group members to be as "worthless and uninteresting" as possible. Different coeds, who went through a much milder initiation ceremony or went through no initiation at all, were decidedly less positive about the "worthless" new group they had joined. Additional research showed the same results when coeds were required to endure pain rather than embarrassment to get into a group. The more electric shock a woman received as part of the initiation ceremony, the more she later persuaded herself that her new group and its activities were interesting, intelligent, and desirable.

我认为答案早在1959年就已出现，源于一项鲜为人知、仅限于社会心理学领域的研究。两位年轻的研究者，埃利奥特·阿伦森和贾德森·米尔斯，决定验证他们的观察结果：“那些历经艰辛或痛苦才获得某样东西的人，往往比那些毫不费力就获得同样东西的人更看重它。” 他们选择以入会仪式作为检验这一可能性的最佳场所，这才是真正的灵感来源。他们发现，那些为了加入性讨论小组而不得不忍受极其尴尬的入会仪式的女大学生，尽管阿伦森和米尔斯事先已经把其他小组成员描述得“毫无价值、乏味无趣”，却仍然坚信她们的新小组及其讨论内容极其有价值。而那些经历了较为温和的入会仪式，甚至根本没有经历任何入会仪式的女大学生，对她们加入的这个“毫无价值”的新小组则明显持更为消极的态度。进一步的研究表明，当女大学生被要求忍受痛苦而非羞辱才能加入某个团体时，结果也相同。女性在入会仪式中受到的电击越多，她之后就越会说服自己，她加入的新团体及其活动是有趣、有深度且令人向往的。

Now the harassments, the exertions, even the beatings of initiation rituals begin to make sense. The Thonga tribesman watching, with tears in his eyes, his ten-year-old son tremble through a night on the cold ground of the "yard of mysteries," the college sophomore punctuating his Hell Night paddling of his fraternity "little brother" with bursts of nervous laughter—these are not acts of sadism. They are acts of group survival. They function, oddly enough, to spur future society members to find the group more attractive and worthwhile. As long as it is the case that people like and believe in what they have struggled to get, these groups will continue to arrange effortful and troublesome initiation rites. The loyalty and dedication of those who emerge will increase to a great degree the chances of group cohesiveness and survival. Indeed, one study of fifty-four tribal cultures found that those with the most dramatic and stringent initiation ceremonies were those with the greatest group solidarity. Given Aronson and Mills's demonstration that the severity of an initiation ceremony significantly heightens the newcomer's commitment to the group, it is hardly surprising that groups will oppose all attempts to eliminate this crucial link to their future strength.

现在，那些骚扰、折磨，甚至入会仪式中的鞭打都开始变得有意义了。一位通加族人含着泪看着他十岁的儿子在“神秘庭院”冰冷的地面上瑟瑟发抖地度过一夜；一位大学二年级学生在“地狱之夜”用木板抽打他的兄弟会“小弟”时，时不时发出紧张的笑声——这些并非虐待狂的行为，而是群体生存的手段。说来也怪，它们的作用在于激励未来的成员觉得这个群体更有吸引力、更有价值。只要人们喜欢并相信他们努力争取来的成果，这些群体就会继续安排这些费力且令人烦恼的入会仪式。而那些最终脱颖而出的人的忠诚和奉献精神，将极大地增强群体的凝聚力和生存能力。事实上，一项针对54个部落文化的研究发现，那些拥有最隆重、最严格的入会仪式的部落，其群体凝聚力也最强。鉴于阿伦森和米尔斯的研究表明，入会仪式的严苛程度会显著增强新成员对群体的忠诚度，因此，群体反对任何试图消除这一对其未来力量至关重要的纽带的企图也就不足为奇了。

Military groups and organizations are by no means exempt from these same processes. The agonies of "boot camp" initiations to the armed services are legendary. The novelist William Styron, a former Marine, catalogs his own experiences in language we could easily apply to the Thongas (or, for that matter, to the Kappas or Betas or Alphas): "the remorseless close-order drill hour after hour in the burning sun, the mental and physical abuse, the humiliations, the frequent sadism at the hands of drill sergeants, all the claustrophobic and terrifying insults to the spirit which can make an outpost like Quantico or Parris Island one of the closest things in the free world to a concentration camp." But, in his commentary, Styron does more than recount the misery of this "training nightmare"—he recognizes its intended outcome: "There is no ex-Marine of my acquaintance, regardless of what direction he may have taken spiritually or politically after those callow gung-ho days, who does not view the training as a crucible out of which he emerged in some way more resilient, simply braver and better for the wear."

军事团体和组织也绝非能免于这些程序。新兵训练营的残酷入伍体验早已闻名遐迩。小说家威廉·斯泰伦（William Styron）曾是一名海军陆战队员，他用描述自己的经历的语言，我们完全可以将其套用到通加兄弟会（或者，就此而言，也适用于卡帕兄弟会、贝塔兄弟会或阿尔法兄弟会）身上：“在烈日下，一小时又一小时无情的队列训练；精神和肉体的虐待；羞辱；教官们频繁的虐待；所有那些令人窒息、令人恐惧的精神折磨，使得像匡蒂科或帕里斯岛这样的前哨基地，成为自由世界中最接近集中营的地方之一。”但是，斯泰伦在他的评论中，不仅描述了这种“训练噩梦”的痛苦，他还认识到了其预期结果：“我认识的所有前海军陆战队员，无论他们在那些懵懂无知、鲁莽行事的日子之后在精神上或政治上走向了什么方向，都把这种训练视为一个熔炉，从中他们变得更加坚韧，更加勇敢，也更加成熟。”

But why should we believe William Styron, the writer, in such matters? After all, for professional storytellers, the line between truth and fiction is often blurred. Indeed, why should we believe him when he alleges that the "infernal" character of his military training was not only successful, it was specifically intended, intended to create desired levels of pride and camaraderie among those who endured and survived it? At least one reason to accept his assessment comes from unfictionalized reality—the case of West Point cadet John Edwards, who was expelled from the U.S. Military Academy in 1988 on charges involving the authorized hazing that all first-year cadets experience at the hands of upperclassmen to ensure that the newcomers can withstand the rigors of West Point training. It was not that Mr. Edwards, who ranked academically near the top of his eleven-hundred-member class, had been unable to bear up under the ritual when he was subjected to it. Nor was he expelled because he had been aberrantly cruel in his treatment of the younger cadets. His offense was that he would not expose the newcomers to what he felt was "absurd and dehumanizing" treatment. Once again, then, it appears that, for groups concerned about creating a lasting sense of solidarity and distinction, the hardship of demanding initiation activities provides a valuable advantage that they will not easily surrender—either to aspiring members who are unwilling to take the harshness or to give it out.

但我们为什么要相信作家威廉·斯泰伦的说法呢？毕竟，对于职业故事讲述者来说，真假之间的界限往往模糊不清。的确，当他声称自己接受的军事训练“如同地狱般残酷”，不仅取得了成功，而且是刻意为之，旨在培养那些坚持下来并最终幸存下来的人的自豪感和战友情谊时，我们又该如何相信他呢？至少有一个理由可以让我们接受他的说法，那就是来自非虚构的现实——西点军校学员约翰·爱德华兹的案例。1988年，爱德华兹因参与新生入伍仪式而被美国军事学院开除。所有一年级学员都要接受高年级学生的“合法”欺凌，以确保他们能够承受西点军校严苛的训练。爱德华兹先生在1100名学员中名列前茅，他并非无法忍受这种仪式。他被开除并非因为他对待低年级学员过于残忍。他的过错在于，他不愿让新学员遭受他认为“荒谬且不人道”的待遇。由此可见，对于那些致力于建立持久团结和卓越感的团体而言，严苛的入会仪式能带来宝贵的优势，他们不会轻易放弃——无论是对那些不愿承受严苛考验的新成员，还是对那些不愿施加严苛考验的新成员。

# ↩

The Inner Choice

内心的选择

Examination of such diverse activities as the indoctrination practices of the Chinese Communists and the initiation rituals of college fraternities has provided some valuable information about commitment. It appears that commitments are most effective in changing a person's self-image and future behavior when they are active, public, and effortful. But there is another property of effective commitment that is more important than the other three combined. To understand what it is, we first need to solve a pair of puzzles in the actions of Communist interrogators and fraternity brothers.

对诸如中国共产党的灌输手段和大学兄弟会的入会仪式等各种活动的考察，为我们提供了关于承诺的一些宝贵信息。研究表明，积极主动、公开透明且付出努力的承诺，在改变一个人的自我认知和未来行为方面最为有效。然而，有效承诺还有另一个比前三个因素加起来更为重要的特质。要理解这个特质是什么，我们首先需要解开共产党审讯人员和兄弟会成员行为中的两个谜题。

The first puzzle comes from the refusal of fraternity chapters to allow public-service activities to be part of their initiation ceremonies. Recall that one survey showed that community projects, though frequent, were nearly always separated from the membership-induction program. But why? If an effortful commitment is what fraternities are after in their initiation rites, surely they could structure enough distasteful and strenuous civic activities for their pledges; there is plenty of exertion and unpleasantness to be had in the world of old-age-home repairs, mental-health-center yard work, and hospital bedpan duty. Besides, community-spirited endeavors of this sort would do much to improve the highly unfavorable public and media image of fraternity Hell Week rites; a survey showed that for every positive newspaper story concerning Hell Week, there were five negative stories. If only for public-rela-tions reasons, then, fraternities should want to incorporate communityservice efforts into their initiation practices. But they don't.

第一个难题在于兄弟会拒绝将公益活动纳入入会仪式。一项调查显示，社区项目虽然很常见，但几乎总是与会员入会流程分开。这是为什么呢？如果兄弟会希望通过入会仪式培养成员的奉献精神，那么他们完全可以为新成员安排足够多的令人不快且费力的公民活动；养老院维修、精神健康中心庭院维护、医院便盆清洁等工作，都足以让人感到疲惫和不快。此外，这类具有社区精神的活动也有助于改善兄弟会“地狱周”仪式在公众和媒体眼中极差的形象；一项调查显示，每有一篇关于“地狱周”的正面报道，就会有五篇负面报道。因此，即使仅仅出于公关考虑，兄弟会也应该将社区服务活动融入到入会仪式中。但他们并没有这样做。

To examine the second puzzle, we need to return to the Chinese prison camps of Korea and the regular political essay contests held for American captives. The Chinese wanted as many Americans as possible to enter these contests so that, in the process, they might write things favorable to the Communist view. If, however, the idea was to attract large numbers of entrants, why were the prizes so small? A few extra cigarettes or a little fresh fruit were often all that a contest winner could expect. In the setting, even these prizes were valuable, but still there were much larger rewards—warm clothing, special mail privileges, increased freedom of movement in camp—that the Chinese could have used to increase the number of essay writers. Yet they specifically chose to employ the smaller rather than the larger, more motivating rewards.

要探究第二个谜题，我们需要回到朝鲜的中国战俘营，以及那里定期为美国战俘举办的政治征文比赛。中国人希望尽可能多的美国人参加这些比赛，以便他们能够写出有利于共产主义观点的文章。然而，如果他们的目的是吸引大量参赛者，为什么奖品却如此微薄？比赛获胜者通常只能得到几支香烟或一些新鲜水果。在当时的环境下，即使是这些奖品也颇具价值，但中国人本可以利用更丰厚的奖励——保暖衣物、特殊的邮件特权、更大的营内行动自由——来增加参赛人数。然而，他们却特意选择了较小的奖励，而不是那些更丰厚、更具激励性的奖励。

Although the settings are quite different, the surveyed fraternities refused to allow civic activities into their initiation ceremonies for the same reason that the Chinese withheld large prizes in favor of less powerful inducements: They wanted the men to own what they had done. No excuses, no ways out were allowed. A man who suffered through an arduous hazing could not be given the chance to believe he did so for charitable purposes. A prisoner who salted his political essay with a few anti-American comments could not be permitted to shrug it off as motivated by a big reward. No, the fraternity chapters and Chinese Communists were playing for keeps. It was not enough to wring commitments out of their men; those men had to be made to take inner responsibility for their actions.

尽管背景截然不同，但受访的兄弟会拒绝在入会仪式中安排公民活动，其原因与中国共产党放弃巨额奖金而选择力度较小的激励措施如出一辙：他们希望成员们对自己的所作所为负责。不允许任何借口，不允许任何逃避。一个经历了严酷入会仪式的成员，不能被允许相信自己是出于慈善目的。一个在政治文章中夹杂了一些反美言论的囚犯，也不能被允许将其归咎于丰厚的奖励。不，兄弟会和中国共产党都是在玩真的。仅仅让成员们做出承诺是不够的；他们必须对自己的行为承担内在的责任。

Given the Chinese Communist government's affinity for the politicalessay contest as a commitment device, it should come as no surprise that a wave of such contests appeared in the aftermath of the 1989 massacre in Tiananmen Square, where pro-democracy protesters were gunned down by government soldiers. In Beijing alone, nine state-run newspapers and television stations sponsored essay competitions on the "quelling of the counterrevolutionary rebellion." Still acting in accord with its long-standing and insightful de-emphasis of rewards for public commitments, the Beijing government left the contest prizes unspecified.

鉴于中国共产党政府一贯热衷于将政治征文比赛作为一种激励民众承诺的手段，1989年天安门广场大屠杀后，此类比赛如雨后春笋般涌现也就不足为奇了。当时，支持民主的抗议者遭到政府军的枪杀。仅在北京，就有九家官方报纸和电视台举办了以“镇压反革命叛乱”为主题的征文比赛。北京政府一贯秉持着不以奖励来激励民众的原则，并未明确比赛的奖项设置。

Social scientists have determined that we accept inner responsibility for a behavior when we think we have chosen to perform it in the absence of strong outside pressures. A large reward is one such external pressure. It may get us to perform a certain action, but it won't get us to accept inner responsibility for the act. Consequently, we won't feel committed to it. The same is true of a strong threat; it may motivate immediate compliance, but it is unlikely to produce long-term commitment.

社会科学家已经证实，当我们认为自己是在没有受到强烈外部压力的情况下选择做出某种行为时，我们才会承担起该行为的内在责任。丰厚的奖励就是一种外部压力。它或许能促使我们采取某种行动，但却无法让我们承担起该行为的内在责任。因此，我们不会对此感到投入。强烈的威胁也是如此；它或许能促使我们立即服从，但不太可能产生长期的承诺。

All this has important implications for rearing children. It suggests that we should never heavily bribe or threaten our children to do the things we want them truly to believe in. Such pressures will probably produce temporary compliance with our wishes. However, if we want more than just that, if we want the children to believe in the correctness of what they have done, if we want them to continue to perform the desired behavior when we are not present to apply those outside pressures, then we must somehow arrange for them to accept inner responsibility for the actions we want them to take. An experiment by Jonathan Freedman gives us some hints about what to do and what not to do in this regard.

所有这些都对养育子女有着重要的启示。它表明，我们绝不应该用重金贿赂或威胁的方式强迫孩子去做我们希望他们真正相信的事情。这样的压力或许能让他们暂时顺从我们的意愿。然而，如果我们想要的不仅仅是暂时的顺从，如果我们希望孩子相信自己所做事情的正确性，如果我们希望他们在我们不在场施加外部压力时也能继续保持这种行为，那么我们就必须想办法让他们对我们希望他们采取的行动承担内在的责任。乔纳森·弗里德曼的一项实验为我们在这方面提供了一些启示。

Freedman wanted to see if he could prevent second- to fourth-grade boys from playing with a fascinating toy, just because he had said that it was wrong to do so some six weeks earlier. Anyone familiar with seven-to-nine-year-old boys must realize the enormity of the task. But Freedman had a plan. If he could first get the boys to convince themselves that it was wrong to play with the forbidden toy, perhaps that belief would keep them from playing with it thereafter. The difficult thing was making the boys believe that it was wrong to amuse themselves with the toy—an extremely expensive, battery-controlled robot.

弗里德曼想看看，他能否阻止二到四年级的男孩们玩一款令人着迷的玩具，仅仅因为他大约六周前说过玩这个玩具是不对的。任何了解七到九岁男孩的人都会明白这项任务有多么艰巨。但弗里德曼早有计划。如果他能先让男孩们相信玩这个禁忌玩具是错的，或许这种信念就能让他们从此不再玩它。难点在于如何让男孩们相信玩这个玩具——一个极其昂贵的电池控制机器人——是错误的。

Freedman knew it would be easy enough to have a boy obey temporarily. All he had to do was threaten the boy with severe consequences should he be caught playing with the toy. As long as he was nearby to deal out stiff punishment, Freedman figured that few boys would risk operating the robot. He was right. After showing a boy an array of five toys and warning him, "It is wrong to play with the robot. If you play with the robot, I'll be very angry and will have to do something about it," Freedman left the room for a few minutes. During that time, the boy was observed secretly through a one-way mirror. Freedman tried this threat procedure on twenty-two different boys, and twenty-one of them never touched the robot while he was gone.

弗里德曼知道，让男孩暂时服从很容易。他只需要威胁男孩，如果被发现玩玩具，就会有严重的后果。只要他在附近，随时可以施以严厉的惩罚，弗里德曼认为很少有男孩会冒险操作机器人。他的想法是对的。弗里德曼向一个男孩展示了五种玩具，并警告他：“玩机器人是不对的。如果你玩机器人，我会非常生气，不得不采取行动。”说完，弗里德曼离开了房间几分钟。在这段时间里，有人通过单向镜秘密观察男孩。弗里德曼用这种方法对二十二个男孩进行了测试，其中二十一个男孩在他离开期间都没有碰过机器人。

So a strong threat was successful while the boys thought they might be caught and punished. But Freedman had already guessed that. He was really interested in the effectiveness of the threat in guiding the boys' behavior later on, when he was no longer around. To find out what would happen then, he sent a young woman back to the boys' school about six weeks after he had been there. She took the boys out of the class one at a time to participate in an experiment. Without ever mentioning any connection with Freedman, she escorted each boy back to the room with the five toys and gave him a drawing test. While she was scoring the test, she told the boy that he was free to play with any toy in the room. Of course, almost all the boys played with a toy. The interesting result was that, of the boys playing with a toy, 77 percent chose to play with the robot that had been forbidden to them earlier. Freedman's severe threat, which had been so successful six weeks before, was almost totally unsuccessful when he was no longer able to back it up with punishment.

因此，在男孩们担心被抓到并受到惩罚的时候，强烈的威胁奏效了。但弗里德曼早已预料到这一点。他真正感兴趣的是，当他离开后，这种威胁对引导男孩们的行为是否有效。为了弄清楚之后会发生什么，在他离开大约六周后，他派了一位年轻女子回到男孩们的学校。她一次带一个男孩离开教室，让他们参与一项实验。她没有提及与弗里德曼的任何关系，而是把每个男孩带到放着五个玩具的房间，并让他们进行绘画测试。在她批改试卷时，她告诉男孩们，他们可以随意玩房间里的任何玩具。当然，几乎所有男孩都玩了玩具。有趣的是，在这些玩玩具的男孩中，77%的人选择了玩之前被禁止的机器人。弗里德曼六周前如此成功的严厉威胁，在他无法再用惩罚来强化之后，几乎完全失效了。

But Freedman wasn't finished yet. He changed his procedure slightly with a second sample of boys. These boys, too, were initially shown the array of five toys by Freedman and warned not to play with the robot while he was briefly out of the room because "It is wrong to play with the robot." But this time, Freedman provided no strong threat to frighten a boy into obedience. He simply left the room and observed through the one-way mirror to see if his instruction against playing with the forbidden toy was enough. It was. Just as with the other sample, only one of the twenty-two boys touched the robot during the short time Freedman was gone.

但弗里德曼的实验并未就此结束。他稍稍调整了实验步骤，对第二组男孩进行了测试。这些男孩也像弗里德曼一样，先被展示了五件玩具，并被警告在他短暂离开房间期间不要玩机器人，因为“玩机器人是不对的”。但这一次，弗里德曼没有使用强烈的威胁来吓唬男孩，而是直接离开房间，透过单向镜观察，看看禁止玩机器人的警告是否有效。结果证明，警告确实有效。和之前的实验一样，在弗里德曼短暂离开的这段时间里，22个男孩中只有一个碰了机器人。

The real difference between the two samples of boys came six weeks later, when they had a chance to play with the toys while Freedman was no longer around. An astonishing thing happened with the boys who had earlier been given no strong threat against playing with the robot: When given the freedom to play with any toy they wished, most avoided the robot, even though it was by far the most attractive of the five toys available (the others were a cheap plastic submarine, a child's baseball glove without a ball, an unloaded toy rifle, and a toy tractor). When these boys played with one of the five toys, only 33 percent chose the robot.

两组男孩之间的真正区别出现在六周后，当时弗里德曼不在场，他们有机会玩这些玩具。令人惊讶的是，之前没有被强烈警告不要玩机器人的男孩们，在被允许自由选择任何玩具时，大多数都避开了机器人，尽管它是五种玩具中最具吸引力的（其他玩具分别是廉价塑料潜艇、没有球的儿童棒球手套、空枪玩具步枪和玩具拖拉机）。当这些男孩在五种玩具中选择一种时，只有33%的人选择了机器人。

Something dramatic had happened to both groups of boys. For the first group, it was the severe threat they heard from Freedman to back up his statement that playing with the robot was "wrong." It had been quite effective at first when Freedman could catch them should they violate his rule. Later, though, when he was no longer present to observe the boys' behavior, his threat was impotent and his rule was, consequently, ignored. It seems clear that the threat had not taught the boys that operating the robot was wrong, only that it was unwise to do so when the possibility of punishment existed.

两组男孩都经历了一些戏剧性的事情。第一组男孩的遭遇是弗里德曼严厉的威胁，他声称玩机器人是“错误的”。起初，弗里德曼的警告确实很有效，因为他可以随时发现他们违反规则。然而，后来，当他不在场监督男孩们的行为时，他的威胁就失去了效力，他的规则也因此被忽视了。显然，弗里德曼的威胁并没有让男孩们明白操作机器人是错误的，而只是让他们意识到，在可能受到惩罚的情况下，这样做是不明智的。

For the other boys, the dramatic event had come from the inside, not the outside. Freedman had instructed them, too, that playing with the robot was wrong, but he had added no threat of punishment should they disobey him. There were two important results. First, Freedman's instruction alone was enough to prevent the boys from operating the robot while he was briefly out of the room. Second, the boys took personal responsibility for their choice to stay away from the robot during that time. They decided that they hadn't played with it because they didn't want to. After all, there were no strong punishments associated with the toy to explain their behavior otherwise. Thus, weeks later, when Freedman was nowhere around, they still ignored the robot because they had been changed inside to believe that they did not want to play with it.

对其他男孩来说，这场戏剧性的事件并非源于外部环境，而是源于内心。弗里德曼也曾告诫他们玩机器人是不对的，但他并没有威胁他们如果不听话会受到惩罚。这产生了两个重要的结果。首先，弗里德曼的告诫本身就足以阻止男孩们在他短暂离开房间期间操作机器人。其次，男孩们为自己在那段时间远离机器人的行为承担了责任。他们认定自己不玩机器人是因为他们不想玩。毕竟，玩具本身并没有什么严厉的惩罚可以解释他们的这种行为。因此，几周后，当弗里德曼不在场时，他们仍然对机器人不予理睬，因为他们的内心已经被改变，相信自己不想玩机器人。

Adults facing the child-rearing experience can take a cue from the Freedman study. Suppose a couple wants to impress upon their daughter that lying is wrong. A strong, clear threat ("It's bad to lie, honey; so if I catch you at it, I'll cut your tongue out") might well be effective when the parents are present or when the girl thinks she can be discovered. But it will not achieve the larger goal of convincing her that she does not want to lie because she thinks it's wrong. To do that, a much subtler approach is required. A reason must be given that is just strong enough to get her to be truthful most of the time but is not so strong that she sees it as the obvious reason for her truthfulness. It's a tricky business, because exactly what this barely sufficient reason will be changes from child to child. For one little girl, a simple appeal may be enough ("It's bad to lie, honey; so I hope you won't do it"); for another child, it may be necessary to add a somewhat stronger reason ("... because if you do, I'll be disappointed in you"); for a third child, a mild form of warning may be required as well (".and I'll probably have to do something I don't want to do"). Wise parents will know which kind of reason will work on their own children. The important thing is to use a reason that will initially produce the desired behavior and will, at the same time, allow a child to take personal responsibility for that behavior. Thus, the less detectable outside pressure such a reason contains, the better. Selecting just the right reason is not an easy task for parents. But the effort should pay off. It is likely to mean the difference between short-lived compliance and long-term commitment.

面临育儿挑战的成年人可以从弗里德曼的研究中汲取一些经验。假设一对夫妇想让女儿明白说谎是不对的。当父母在场或女儿认为自己可能会被发现时，一个强硬而明确的威胁（“宝贝，说谎不好；所以如果我发现你说谎，我就割掉你的舌头”）或许会很有效。但这并不能达到更深层次的目的，即让她相信自己不想说谎是因为她认为说谎是错的。要做到这一点，需要一种更巧妙的方法。必须给出一个足够有力的理由，让她大部分时间都说真话，但又不能太有力，以至于她认为这是她说真话的显而易见的理由。这很棘手，因为这个恰到好处的理由因人而异。对一个小女孩来说，一个简单的劝告可能就足够了（“宝贝，说谎不好；所以我希望你不要说谎”）；对于另一个孩子，可能需要补充一个更强有力的理由（“……因为如果你那样做，我会对你失望的”）；对于第三个孩子，可能还需要一个温和的警告（“而且我可能不得不做一些我不想做的事情”）。明智的父母会知道哪种理由对自己的孩子有效。重要的是，要使用一个既能促使孩子做出期望的行为，又能让孩子对自己的行为承担责任的理由。因此，理由中越少包含明显的外部压力，效果就越好。选择合适的理由对父母来说并非易事，但付出终会有回报。这很可能决定孩子是短暂的顺从还是长久的坚持。

For a pair of reasons we have already talked about, compliance professionals love commitments that produce inner change. First, that change is not just specific to the situation where it first occurred; it covers a whole range of related situations, too. Second, the effects of the change are lasting. So, once a man has been induced to take action that shifts his self-image to that of, let's say, a public-spirited citizen, he is likely to be public-spirited in a variety of other circumstances where his compliance may also be desired, and he is likely to continue his public-spirited behavior for as long as his new self-image holds.

出于我们之前讨论过的两个原因，合规专业人士喜欢那些能带来内在改变的承诺。首先，这种改变并非仅限于最初发生的情境，它还能涵盖一系列相关的情境。其次，这种改变的影响是持久的。因此，一旦一个人被引导采取行动，使其自我认知转变为（比如说）一个具有公共精神的公民，那么在其他各种需要他遵守规定的情境中，他很可能也会表现出这种公共精神，并且只要这种新的自我认知保持不变，他就会继续保持这种公共精神的行为。

There is yet another attraction in commitments that lead to inner change—they grow their own legs. There is no need for the compliance professional to undertake a costly and continuing effort to reinforce the change; the pressure for consistency will take care of all that. After our friend comes to view himself as a public-spirited citizen, he will automatically begin to see things differently. He will convince himself that it is the correct way to be. He will begin to pay attention to facts he hadn't noticed before about the value of community service. He will make himself available to hear arguments he hadn't heard before favoring civic action. And he will find such arguments more persuasive than before. In general, because of the need to be consistent within his system of beliefs, he will assure himself that his choice to take public-spirited action was right. What is important about this process of generating additional reasons to justify the commitment is that the reasons are new. Thus, even if the original reason for the civic-minded behavior was taken away, these newly discovered reasons might be enough by themselves to support his perception that he had behaved correctly.

促成内在改变的承诺还有另一个吸引人的地方——它们会自行发展壮大。合规专业人员无需投入大量成本和持续精力来巩固这种改变；对一致性的压力会自然而然地促成这一切。当我们的朋友开始将自己视为一位热心公益的公民后，他自然而然地会以不同的视角看待事物。他会说服自己，这是正确的行事方式。他会开始关注以前从未注意到的关于社区服务价值的事实。他会愿意倾听以前从未听过的、支持公民行动的论点。而且他会发现这些论点比以前更有说服力。总而言之，由于需要在自己的信念体系内保持一致，他会确信自己选择采取热心公益的行动是正确的。在这个过程中，产生更多理由来证明承诺的合理性，关键在于这些理由是全新的。因此，即使最初的公民行为的原因被剥夺，这些新发现的原因本身也可能足以支持他认为自己的行为是正确的看法。

The advantage to an unscrupulous compliance professional is tremendous. Because we build new struts to undergird choices we have committed ourselves to, an exploitative individual can offer us an inducement for making such a choice, and after the decision has been made, can remove that inducement, knowing that our decision will probably stand on its own newly created legs. New-car dealers frequently try to benefit from this process through a trick they call "throwing a lowball." I first encountered the tactic while posing as a sales trainee at a local Chevrolet dealership. After a week of basic instruction, I was allowed to watch the regular salesmen perform. One practice that caught my attention right away was the lowball.

对不择手段的合规专业人士来说，这种做法的优势是巨大的。因为我们会为自己做出的选择构建新的支撑结构，所以别有用心的人可以利用这种优势诱导我们做出选择，然后在我们做出决定后，撤回这种诱导，因为他们知道，我们的决定很可能凭借新构建的支撑结构就能站得住脚。新车经销商经常试图利用这种机制，他们称之为“低价抛售”。我第一次遇到这种伎俩是在当地一家雪佛兰经销店假扮销售实习生的时候。经过一周的基础培训后，我被允许观摩正式销售人员的销售工作。其中一种做法立刻引起了我的注意，那就是低价抛售。

For certain customers, a very good price is offered on a car, perhaps as much as four hundred dollars below competitors' prices. The good deal, however, is not genuine; the dealer never intends it to go through. Its only purpose is to cause a prospect to decide to buy one of the dealership's cars. Once the decision is made, a number of activities develop the customer's sense of personal commitment to the car—a raft of purchase forms are filled out, extensive financing terms are arranged, sometimes the customer is encouraged to drive the car for a day before signing the contract "so you can get the feel of it and show it around in the neighborhood and at work." During this time, the dealer knows, customers automatically develop a range of new reasons to support the choice they have now made.

对于某些客户，经销商会提供一个非常优惠的价格，可能比竞争对手的价格低四百美元之多。然而，这种所谓的“优惠”并非真心实意；经销商根本就没打算真的成交。其唯一目的在于促使潜在客户决定购买本店的车辆。一旦客户做出决定，经销商便会采取一系列措施来增强客户对车辆的认同感——填写大量的购车表格，安排复杂的融资方案，有时甚至鼓励客户在签署合同前试驾一天，“以便您感受一下车辆的性能，并在附近和工作场所进行演示”。经销商深知，在此期间，客户会自然而然地找到各种新的理由来支持他们已做出的选择。

Then something happens. Occasionally an "error" in the calculations is discovered—maybe the salesman forgot to add in the cost of the air conditioner, and if the buyer still requires air conditioning, four hundred dollars must be added to the price. To keep from being suspected of gouging by the customer, some dealers let the bank handling the financing find the mistake. At other times, the deal is disallowed at the last moment when the salesman checks with his boss, who cancels it because "We'd be losing money." For only another four hundred dollars the car can be had, which, in the context of a multithousand-dollar deal, doesn't seem too steep since, as the salesman emphasizes, the cost is equal to competitors' and "This is the car you chose, right?" Another, even more insidious form of lowballing occurs when the salesman makes an inflated trade-in offer on the prospect's old car as part of the buy/trade package. The customer recognizes the offer as overly generous and jumps at the deal. Later, before the contract is signed, the used-car manager says that the salesman's estimate was four hundred dollars too high and reduces the trade-in allowance to its actual, blue-book level. The customer, realizing that the reduced offer is the fair one, accepts it as appropriate and sometimes feels guilty about trying to take advantage of the salesman's high estimate. I once witnessed a woman provide an embarrassed apology to a salesman who had used the last version of lowballing on her—this while she was signing a new-car contract giving him a huge commission. He looked hurt but managed a forgiving smile.

然后，事情就发生了。有时，会发现计算中存在“错误”——比如销售员忘记把空调的费用算进去，如果买家仍然需要空调，就得在价格上加400美元。为了避免被顾客怀疑宰客，一些经销商会让负责贷款的银行发现这个错误。还有的时候，销售员会在最后一刻向老板确认，老板会以“我们会赔钱”为由取消交易。只需再加400美元，这辆车就能到手。在几千美元的交易中，这似乎并不算太贵，因为正如销售员强调的那样，价格和竞争对手一样，“这可是您选的车，对吧？”另一种更阴险的低价策略是，销售员在买车/置换套餐中，对顾客的旧车提出一个过高的置换价格。顾客意识到这个价格过于诱人，便欣然接受了。后来，在合同签署之前，二手车经理说销售员的估价高了四百美元，并将旧车置换补贴降至实际的蓝皮书价格。顾客意识到降价后的报价才是合理的，便接受了，有时还会因为试图占销售员高估价的便宜而感到内疚。我曾亲眼目睹一位女士尴尬地向一位销售员道歉，这位销售员之前对她使用了压价策略——而当时她正在签署一份新车合同，这意味着他能拿到一大笔佣金。他看起来很受伤，但还是勉强挤出一丝宽容的微笑。

No matter which variety of lowballing is used, the sequence is the same: An advantage is offered that induces a favorable purchase decision; then, sometime after the decision has been made but before the bargain is sealed, the original purchase advantage is deftly removed. It seems almost incredible that a customer would buy a car under these circumstances. Yet it works—not on everybody, of course, but it is effective enough to be a staple compliance procedure in many, many car showrooms. Automobile dealers have come to understand the ability of a personal commitment to build its own support system, a support system of new justifications for the commitment. Often these justifications provide so many strong legs for the decision to stand on that when the dealer pulls away only one leg, the original one, there is no collapse. The loss can be shrugged off by the customer who is consoled, even made happy, by the array of other good reasons favoring the choice. It never occurs to the buyer that those additional reasons might never have existed had the choice not been made in the first place.

无论采用哪种低价策略，流程都一样：先提供某种优势，诱使顾客做出购买决定；然后，在顾客做出决定之后、交易完成之前，巧妙地取消最初的优惠。在这种情况下，顾客竟然会买车，这听起来简直不可思议。然而，这招确实有效——当然，并非对每个人都有效，但它的效力足以使其成为许多汽车展厅的必备手段。汽车经销商已经意识到，个人承诺能够建立起自身的支撑体系，一个由新的理由组成的支撑体系。这些理由往往为顾客的决定提供了诸多强有力的支撑，以至于当经销商撤回其中一条支撑——最初的那条——时，顾客也不会感到崩溃。顾客会因为其他诸多支持其选择的理由而感到安慰，甚至欣喜。买家从未想过，如果当初没有做出这个选择，这些额外的理由或许根本不会存在。

The impressive thing about the lowball tactic is its ability to make a person feel pleased with a poor choice. Those who have only poor choices to offer us, then, are especially fond of the technique. We can find them throwing lowballs in business, social, and personal situations. For instance, there's my neighbor Tim, a true lowball aficionado. Recall that he's the one who, by promising to change his ways, got his girlfriend, Sara, to cancel her impending marriage to another and to take him back. Since her decision for Tim, Sara has become more devoted to him than ever, even though he has not fulfilled his promises. She explains this by saying that she has allowed herself to see all sorts of positive qualities in Tim she had never recognized before.

低价策略最令人印象深刻之处在于，它能让人对自己的糟糕选择感到满意。因此，那些只会提供糟糕选择的人尤其钟爱这种技巧。我们可以在商业、社交和个人场合看到他们使用低价策略。例如，我的邻居蒂姆就是个不折不扣的低价高手。想想看，他曾承诺改过自新，以此说服女友萨拉取消了与他人的婚约，重新回到他身边。自从萨拉为了蒂姆做出这个决定后，她比以往任何时候都更加忠于他，尽管蒂姆并没有兑现承诺。她解释说，这是因为她开始看到蒂姆身上以前从未发现的各种优点。

I know full well that Sara is a lowball victim. Just as sure as I had watched buyers fall for the give-it-and-take-it-away-later strategy in the car showroom, I watched her fall for the same trick with Tim. For his part, Tim remains the guy he has always been. But because the new attractions Sara has discovered (or created) in him are quite real for her, she now seems satisfied with the same arrangement that was unacceptable before her enormous commitment. The decision to choose Tim, poor as it may have been objectively, has grown its own supports and appears to have made Sara genuinely happy. I have never mentioned to Sara what I know about lowballing. The reason for my silence is not that I think her better off in the dark on the issue. As a general guiding principle, more information is always better than less information. It's just that, if I said a word, I am confident she would hate me for it.

我非常清楚萨拉是低价谈判的受害者。就像我亲眼目睹买家在汽车展厅里落入“先给再说”的陷阱一样，我也亲眼目睹她对蒂姆上当受骗。蒂姆还是老样子。但因为萨拉在他身上发现了（或者说是自己创造了）的新吸引力，而且这种吸引力对她来说是真真切切的，所以她现在似乎对之前她无法接受的这种安排感到满意。选择蒂姆这个决定，尽管客观上可能并不明智，但却逐渐获得了支持，而且似乎真的让萨拉感到快乐。我从未跟萨拉提起过我所知道的低价谈判之事。我保持沉默的原因并非是我认为对她一无所知更好。一般来说，信息越多越好。只是，如果我说了半句，我确信她会因此恨我。

Depending on the motives of the person wishing to use them, any of the compliance techniques discussed in this book can be employed for good or for ill. It should not be surprising, then, that the lowball tactic can be used for more socially beneficial purposes than selling new cars or reestablishing relationships with former lovers. One research project done in Iowa, for example, shows how the lowball procedure can influence homeowners to conserve energy. 1 The project, headed by Dr. Michael Pallak, began at the start of the Iowa winter when residents who heated their homes with natural gas were contacted by an interviewer. The interviewer gave them some energy-conservation tips and asked them to try to save fuel in the future. Although they all agreed to try, when the researchers examined the utility records of these families after a month and again at winter's end, it was clear that no real savings had occurred. The residents who had promised to make a conservation attempt used just as much natural gas as a random sample of their neighbors who had not been contacted by an interviewer. Just good intentions coupled with information about saving fuel, then, were not enough to change habits.

根据使用者的动机，本书讨论的任何一种顺从技巧都可能被用于行善或作恶。因此，低价策略可以用于比推销新车或与前任复合更有益于社会的目的，也就不足为奇了。例如，爱荷华州的一项研究表明，低价策略可以促使房主节约能源。 1 该项目由迈克尔·帕拉克博士领导，在爱荷华州冬季伊始启动。研究人员联系了使用天然气取暖的居民，并向他们提供了一些节能建议，希望他们今后尽量节约燃料。尽管所有居民都同意尝试，但一个月后以及冬季结束时，研究人员再次检查了这些家庭的公用事业记录，结果发现并没有真正节省能源。那些承诺节约能源的居民使用的天然气量与随机抽取的、未被研究人员联系的邻居一样多。因此，仅仅有良好的意愿和节约燃料的信息并不足以改变人们的习惯。

Even before the project began, Pallak and his research team had recognized that something more would be needed to shift long-standing energy patterns. So they tried a slightly different procedure on a comparable sample of Iowa natural-gas users. These people, too, were contacted by an interviewer, who provided energy-saving hints and asked them to conserve. But for these families, the interviewer offered something else: Those residents agreeing to save energy would have their names publicized in newspaper articles as public-spirited, fuel-conserving citizens. The effect was immediate. One month later, when the utility companies checked their meters, the homeowners in this sample had saved an average of 422 cubic feet of natural gas apiece. The chance to have their names in the paper had motivated these residents to substantial conservation efforts for a period of a month.

早在项目启动之前，帕拉克和他的研究团队就意识到，要改变长期以来的能源使用模式，还需要采取更多措施。因此，他们对爱荷华州的一组天然气用户进行了略有不同的调查。这些用户也接受了访谈，访谈员向他们提供节能建议并鼓励他们节约能源。但对于这些家庭，访谈员还提供了一项额外的奖励：同意节约能源的居民的名字将刊登在报纸上，作为具有公共精神、节约能源的公民。效果立竿见影。一个月后，当公用事业公司检查他们的燃气表时，发现这组样本中的居民平均每户节约了422立方英尺的天然气。有机会在报纸上露面激励了这些居民在一个月的时间里积极采取节约措施。

Then the rug was pulled out. The researchers extracted the reason that had initially caused these people to save fuel. Each family that had been promised publicity received a letter saying it would not be possible to publicize their names after all.

然而，真相却被揭穿了。研究人员挖出了这些人最初节约燃料的真正原因。每个原本被承诺会公开姓名的家庭都收到了一封信，信中告知他们，最终无法公开他们的姓名。

At the end of the winter, the research team examined the effect that letter had had on the natural-gas usage of the families. Did they return to their old, wasteful habits when the chance to be in the newspaper was removed? Hardly. For each of the remaining winter months, they actually conserved more fuel than they had during the time they thought they would be publicly celebrated for it! In terms of percentage of energy savings, they had managed a 12.2 percent first-month gas savings because they expected to see themselves lauded in the paper. But after the letter arrived informing them to the contrary, they did not return to their previous energy-use levels; instead, they increased their savings to a 15.5 percent level for the rest of the winter.

冬季结束时，研究团队调查了那封信对这些家庭天然气使用情况的影响。当上报纸的机会消失后，他们是否又恢复了以往浪费的习惯？答案是否定的。在接下来的几个月里，他们实际上比之前预期会因此受到表扬时更加节约能源！就节能百分比而言，由于期待在报纸上看到自己的身影，他们在第一个月实现了12.2%的天然气节约。但收到那封告知他们结果并非如此的信后，他们并没有恢复到之前的能源消耗水平；相反，在接下来的整个冬季，他们的节能率达到了15.5%。

Although we can never be completely sure of such things, one explanation for their persistent behavior presents itself immediately. These people had been lowballed into a conservation commitment through a promise of newspaper publicity. Once made, that commitment started generating its own support: The homeowners began acquiring new energy habits, began feeling good about their public-spirited efforts, began convincing themselves of the vital need to reduce American dependence on foreign fuel, began appreciating the monetary savings in their utility bills, began feeling proud of their capacity for self-denial, and, most important, began viewing themselves as conservation-minded. With all these new reasons present to justify the commitment to use less energy, it is no wonder that the commitment remained firm even after the original reason, newspaper publicity, had been kicked away.

尽管我们永远无法完全确定此类事情，但他们持续节能行为的一个解释却显而易见。这些人最初是被报纸宣传的承诺所蒙蔽，才做出节能承诺的。一旦做出承诺，它便开始产生自身的支持：房主们开始养成新的节能习惯，开始为自己的公益行为感到自豪，开始相信减少美国对外国燃料依赖的必要性，开始体会到水电费的节省，开始为自己的克己能力感到骄傲，最重要的是，开始将自己视为具有节能意识的人。有了这些新的理由来证明减少能源消耗的合理性，即使最初的报纸宣传承诺不再，他们仍然坚定不移也就不足为奇了。

But strangely enough, when the publicity factor was no longer a possibility, these families did not merely maintain their fuel-saving effort, they heightened it. Any of a number of interpretations could be offered for that still stronger effort, but I have a favorite. In a way, the opportunity to receive newspaper publicity had prevented the homeowners from fully owning their commitment to conservation. Of all the reasons supporting the decision to try to save fuel, it was the only one that had come from the outside; it was the only one preventing the homeowners from thinking that they were conserving gas because they believed in it. So when the letter arrived canceling the publicity agreement, it removed the only impediment to these residents' images of themselves as fully concerned, energy-conscious citizens. This unqualified, new self-image then pushed them to even greater heights of conservation. Whether or not such an explanation is correct, a repeat study done by Pallak indicates that this hidden benefit of the lowball tactic is no fluke.

但奇怪的是，当宣传机会不再可能时，这些家庭不仅没有停止节约能源，反而加大了力度。对于这种更强烈的节约行为，可以提出多种解释，但我最喜欢其中一种。某种程度上，报纸宣传的机会反而让这些房主无法真正认同自己节约能源的承诺。在所有支持他们节约能源的理由中，只有报纸宣传是来自外部的；也只有它阻止了房主们认为自己节约燃气是出于真心。因此，当取消宣传协议的信件到来时，它消除了这些居民心中唯一阻碍他们成为真正关心能源、具有环保意识的公民的障碍。这种全新的、毫无保留的自我认知促使他们更加努力地节约能源。无论这种解释是否正确，帕拉克进行的一项重复研究表明，低价策略带来的这种隐藏好处并非偶然。

The experiment was done in summer on Iowans whose homes were cooled by central air-conditioning. Those homeowners who were promised newspaper publicity decreased their electricity use by 27.8 percent during July, as compared to similar homeowners who were not promised any coverage or who were not contacted at all. At the end of July, a letter was sent canceling the publicity promise. Rather than reverting to their old habits, the lowballed residents increased their August energy savings to a stunning 41.6 percent. Much like Sara, they appeared to have become committed to a choice through an initial inducement and were still more dedicated to it after the inducement had been removed.

这项实验在夏季进行，对象是爱荷华州使用中央空调的居民。那些被承诺会在报纸上刊登广告的居民，在7月份的用电量比那些没有被承诺任何报道或根本没被联系的居民减少了27.8%。7月底，主办方寄出一封信，取消了之前的宣传承诺。然而，这些被取消宣传承诺的居民并没有恢复之前的用电习惯，反而将8月份的节能幅度提高到了惊人的41.6%。就像萨拉一样，他们似乎是因为最初的激励而做出了某种选择，即使激励取消后，他们仍然更加坚持这种选择。

HOW TO SAY NO

如何说“不”

"Consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds." Or, at least, so goes a frequently heard quotation attributed to Ralph Waldo Emerson. But what a very odd thing to say. Looking around, it is obvious that, quite contrary to what Emerson seems to have suggested, internal consistency is a hallmark of logic and intellectual strength, while its lack characterizes the intellectually scattered and limited among us. What, then, could a thinker of Emerson's caliber have meant when he assigned the trait of consistency to the small-minded? I was sufficiently intrigued to go back to the original source of his statement, the essay "Self-Reliance," where it was clear that the problem lay not in Emerson, but in the popular version of what he had said. Actually he wrote, "A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds." For some obscure reason, a central distinction had been lost as the years eroded the accurate version of his statement to mean something entirely different and, upon close inspection, entirely silly.

“循规蹈矩是心胸狭隘者的怪癖。”至少，这句常被人们挂在嘴边的名言出自拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生之口。但这话听起来实在匪夷所思。环顾四周，我们便会发现，与爱默生似乎暗示的截然相反，内在的一致性恰恰是逻辑和智力强大的标志，而缺乏内在一致性则恰恰是那些思维散漫、思维局限之人的特征。那么，像爱默生这样一位思想家，为何会将“循规蹈矩”这一特质与心胸狭隘之人联系起来呢？我对此十分好奇，于是追溯到他这句话的原始出处——《论自助》一文。在那里，我发现问题不在于爱默生本人，而在于人们对这句话的流行解读。实际上，他写的是：“愚蠢的循规蹈矩是心胸狭隘者的怪癖。”不知何故，随着岁月的流逝，他这句话的准确含义逐渐被扭曲，最终变成了完全不同、甚至荒谬至极的东西。

That distinction should not be lost on us, however, because it is vital to the only effective defense I know against the weapons of influence embodied in the combined principles of commitment and consistency. Although consistency is generally good, even vital, there is a foolish, rigid variety to be shunned. It is this tendency to be automatically and unthinkingly consistent that Emerson referred to. And it is this tendency that we must be wary of, for it lays us open to the maneuvers of those who want to exploit the mechanical commitment --> consistency sequence for profit.

然而，我们不应忽视这一区别，因为它对于我所知的唯一有效防御手段至关重要，这种防御手段旨在抵御以承诺和一致性原则相结合为核心的影响武器。虽然一致性通常是好的，甚至是至关重要的，但有一种愚蠢而僵化的一致性应该避免。爱默生所指的正是这种机械地、不假思索地保持一致的倾向。我们必须警惕这种倾向，因为它使我们容易受到那些企图利用机械的承诺→一致性序列来牟利的人的摆布。

But since automatic consistency is so useful in allowing us an economical and appropriate way of behaving most of the time, we can't decide merely to eliminate it from our lives altogether. The results would be disastrous. If, rather than whirring along in accordance with our prior decisions and deeds, we stopped to think through the merits of every new action before performing it, we would never have time to accomplish anything significant. We need even that dangerous, mechanical brand of consistency. The only way out of the dilemma is to know when such consistency is likely to lead to a poor choice. There are certain signals—two separate kinds of signals, in fact—to tip us off. We register each type in a different part of our bodies.

但是，由于自动一致性在大多数情况下能帮助我们以经济且恰当的方式行事，因此我们不能简单地将其从生活中彻底剔除。否则后果不堪设想。如果我们不再按照以往的决定和行为机械地行事，而是在每次行动前停下来仔细思考其利弊，我们将永远没有时间完成任何有意义的事情。我们甚至需要这种危险的、机械式的一致性。摆脱困境的唯一方法是了解这种一致性何时可能导致糟糕的选择。实际上，有两种不同的信号可以提醒我们。我们身体的不同部位会感知到这两种信号。

The first sort of signal is easy to recognize. It occurs right in the pit of our stomachs when we realize we are trapped into complying with a request we know we don't want to perform. It has happened to me a hundred times. An especially memorable instance, though, took place on a summer evening well before I began to study compliance tactics. I answered my doorbell to find a stunning young woman dressed in shorts and a revealing halter top. I noticed, nonetheless, that she was carrying a clipboard and was asking me to participate in a survey. Wanting to make a favorable impression, I agreed and, I do admit, stretched the truth in my interview answers so as to present myself in the most positive light. Our conversation went as follows:

第一种信号很容易识别。当我们意识到自己被迫服从一个明知自己不想做的请求时，这种信号就会在我们内心深处涌现。这种情况我经历过无数次。不过，有一次特别难忘的经历发生在一个夏日的傍晚，那时我还没有开始研究服从技巧。我去开门，发现一位穿着短裤和露背吊带背心的漂亮年轻女子站在门口。但我注意到，她手里拿着一个写字板，邀请我参与一项调查。为了给她留下好印象，我答应了，而且我承认，为了尽可能展现自己最好的一面，我在回答问题时夸大了事实。我们的对话如下：

STUNNING YOUNG WOMAN: Hello, I'm doing a survey on the entertainment habits of city residents, and I wonder if you could answer a few questions for me.

一位惊艳的年轻女子：您好，我正在进行一项关于城市居民娱乐习惯的调查，不知道您是否可以回答我几个问题。

CIALDINI: Do come in.

西奥迪尼：请进。

SYW: Thank you. I'll just sit right here and begin. How many times per week would you say that you go out to dinner?

SYW：谢谢。我就坐在这里开始。您每周大概会外出就餐几次？

C: Oh, probably three, maybe four times a week. Whenever I can, really; I love fine restaurants.

C：哦，大概一周三四次吧。只要有时间就去；我喜欢高级餐厅。

SYW: How nice. And do you usually order wine with your dinner?

SYW：真好。你通常会在晚餐时点葡萄酒吗？

C: Only if it's imported.

C：只有进口的才行。

SYW: I see. What about movies? Do you go to the movies much?

SYW：我明白了。那电影呢？你经常去看电影吗？

C: The cinema? I can't get enough of good films. I especially like the sophisticated kind with the words on the bottom of the screen. How about you? Do you like to see films?

C：电影院？我百看不厌。我尤其喜欢那种屏幕下方有字幕的精致电影。你呢？你喜欢看电影吗？

SYW: Uh...yes, I do. But let's get back to the interview. Do you go to many concerts?

SYW：呃……是的，我经常去。不过我们还是回到采访上来吧。你经常去看演唱会吗？

C: Definitely. The symphonic stuff mostly, of course; but I do enjoy a quality pop group as well.

C：当然。主要是交响乐，不过我也很喜欢一些优秀的流行乐队。

SYW (writing rapidly): Great! Just one more question. What about touring performances by theatrical or ballet companies? Do you see them when they're in town?

SYW（快速书写）：太好了！最后一个问题。戏剧团或芭蕾舞团的巡回演出呢？他们会来我们城市演出吗？

C: Ah, the ballet—the movement, the grace, the form—I love it. Mark me down as loving the ballet. See it every chance I get.

C：啊，芭蕾——它的动作、优雅的姿态、优美的身形——我太爱它了。我绝对热爱芭蕾。只要有机会，我都会去看。

SYW: Fine. Just let me recheck my figures here for a moment, Mr. Cialdini.

SYW：好的。西奥迪尼先生，请允许我再核对一下数据。

C: Actually, it's Dr. Cialdini. But that sounds so formal; why don't you call me Bob?

C：其实，我是西奥迪尼博士。但这听起来太正式了；你为什么不叫我鲍勃呢？

SYW: All right, Bob. From the information you've already given me, I'm pleased to say that you could save up to twelve hundred dollars a year by joining Clubamerica! A small membership fee entitles you to discounts on most of the activities you've mentioned. Surely someone as socially vigorous as yourself would want to take advantage of the tremendous savings our company can offer on all the things you've already told me you do.

SYW：好的，鲍勃。根据你之前提供的信息，我很高兴地告诉你，加入美国俱乐部（Clubamerica）每年最多可以节省一千二百美元！只需缴纳少量会员费，你就可以享受你提到的大部分活动的折扣。像你这样热爱社交的人，肯定很乐意利用我们公司提供的巨大优惠，让你在之前提到的所有活动上都能省钱。

C (trapped like a rat): Well...uh...I...uh...I guess so.

C（像老鼠一样被困住了）：嗯……呃……我……呃……我想是的。

I remember quite well feeling my stomach tighten as I stammered my agreement. It was a clear call to my brain, "Hey, you're being taken here!" But I couldn't see a way out. I had been cornered by my own words. To decline her offer at that point would have meant facing a pair of distasteful alternatives: If I tried to back out by protesting that I was not actually the man-about-town I had claimed to be during the interview, I would come off a liar; but trying to refuse without that protest would make me come off a fool for not wanting to save twelve hundred dollars. So I bought the entertainment package, even though I knew I had been set up so that the need to be consistent with what I had already said would snare me.

我清楚地记得，当我结结巴巴地答应时，胃里一阵紧缩。那感觉就像我的大脑在发出警告：“嘿，你上当了！”但我却找不到出路。我被自己的话逼到了墙角。如果当时拒绝她的提议，就意味着要面对两个令人不快的选择：如果我反悔，声称自己并非面试时口中的那种风流倜傥的社交名流，那我就成了个骗子；但如果不反悔就拒绝，又会显得我像个傻瓜，竟然舍不得省下那一千二百美元。所以我买了那份娱乐套餐，尽管我知道自己已经中了圈套，为了维持之前说的话，我最终还是落入了陷阱。

No more, though. I listen to my stomach these days. And I have discovered a way to handle people who try to use the consistency principle on me. I just tell them exactly what they are doing. It works beautifully. Most of the time, they don't understand me; they just become sufficiently confused to want to leave me alone. I think they suspect lunacy in anyone who responds to their requests by explaining what Ralph Waldo Emerson meant in distinguishing between consistency and foolish consistency. Usually they have already begun edging away by the time I have mentioned "hobgoblins of the mind" and are gone long before I have described the click, whirr character of commitment and consistency. Occasionally, though, they realize that I am on to their game. I always know when that happens—it's as clear as the egg on their faces. They invariably become flustered, bumble through a hasty exit line, and go for the door.

不过，现在不会了。这些日子我听从自己的直觉。而且，我发现了一个对付那些试图用“一致性原则”来对付我的人的办法。我直接告诉他们，他们到底在干什么。这招非常管用。大多数时候，他们根本不理解我的意思；他们只是感到困惑，然后就想赶紧离开。我想，他们肯定觉得那些回应他们要求，并解释拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生如何区分“一致性”和“愚蠢的一致性”的人是疯子。通常，当我提到“思维的妖魔鬼怪”时，他们就已经开始溜走了，在我描述承诺和一致性的“咔哒”声和“嗡嗡”声之前，他们早就走开了。不过，偶尔他们也会意识到我识破了他们的伎俩。我总是能一眼看穿——就像他们脸上的尴尬表情一样清晰可见。他们总是会慌慌张张地从队伍里溜走，然后夺门而出。

This tactic has become the perfect counterattack for me. Whenever my stomach tells me I would be a sucker to comply with a request merely because doing so would be consistent with some prior commitment I was tricked into, I relay that message to the requester. I don't try to deny the importance of consistency; I just point out the absurdity of foolish consistency. Whether, in response, the requester shrinks away guiltily or retreats in bewilderment, I am content. I have won; an exploiter has lost.

这招对我来说简直是完美的反击。每当我感觉自己像个傻瓜一样，仅仅因为答应对方的要求就能维持之前被骗做出的承诺，我就会把这种感觉转告给对方。我并不否认前后一致的重要性，我只是指出这种愚蠢的“前后一致”有多么荒谬。无论对方是愧疚地退缩，还是茫然地退缩，我都心满意足。我赢了，骗子输了。

I sometimes think about how it would be if that stunning young woman of years ago were to try to sell me an entertainment-club membership now. I have it all worked out. The entire interaction would be the same, except for the end:

我有时会想，如果多年前那位惊艳的年轻女子现在想向我推销娱乐俱乐部的会员资格，会是什么样子。我已经想好了。整个过程都会一样，除了结尾：

SYW:. . .Surely someone as socially vigorous as yourself would want to take advantage of the tremendous savings our company can offer on all the things you've already told me you do.

SYW：……像您这样社交活跃的人，肯定会想利用我们公司在您之前告诉我的所有活动上提供的巨大优惠。

C (with great self-assurance): Quite wrong. You see, I recognize what has gone on here. I know that your story about doing a survey was just a pretext for getting people to tell you how often they go out and that, under those circumstances, there is a natural tendency to exaggerate. I also realize that your bosses selected you for this job because of your physical attractiveness and told you to wear clothes showing a lot of your resilient body tissue because a pretty, scantily clad woman is likely to get men to brag about what swingers they are in order to impress her. So I'm not interested in your entertainment club because of what Emerson said about foolish consistency and hobgoblins of the mind.

C（自信满满）：大错特错。你看，我看穿了这一切。我知道你所谓的做调查只是个幌子，目的是想套取人们的外出频率，在这种情况下，人们自然会倾向于夸大其词。我也明白，你的老板之所以选中你这份工作，是因为你长得漂亮，还让你穿暴露的衣服，因为漂亮又衣着暴露的女人更容易让男人吹嘘自己有多放荡不羁，以此来博取她的好感。所以，我对你的娱乐俱乐部一点兴趣都没有，就像爱默生说的，愚蠢的坚持和心灵的恶魔。

SYW (staring blankly): Huh?

SYW（茫然地盯着）：嗯？

C: Look. What I told you during your fake survey doesn't matter. I refuse to allow myself to be locked into a mechanical sequence of commitment and consistency when I know it's wrongheaded. No click, whirr for me.

C：听着。我在你那份虚假调查问卷里说的话根本不重要。我拒绝让自己陷入那种机械式的承诺和坚持模式中，因为我知道那是错的。对我来说，不需要任何形式的“咔哒”声或“嗡嗡”声。

SYW: Huh?

SYW：嗯？

C: Okay, let me put it this way: (1) It would be stupid of me to spend money on something I don't want. (2) I have it on excellent author-ity, direct from my stomach, that I don't want your entertainment plan. (3) Therefore, if you still believe that I will buy it, you probably also still believe in the Tooth Fairy. Surely, someone as intelligent as yourself would be able to understand that.

C：好吧，我这么说吧：（1）花钱买自己不想要的东西，那太傻了。（2）我发自内心地、绝对肯定地说，我不需要你的娱乐套餐。（3）所以，如果你还觉得我会买，那你大概也还相信牙仙子吧。像你这么聪明的人，肯定能明白这一点。

SYW (trapped like a stunning young rat): Well... uh... I... uh... I guess so.

SYW（像一只被困住的漂亮小老鼠一样）：嗯……呃……我……呃……我想是的。

Stomachs are not especially perceptive or subtle organs. Only when it is obvious that we are about to be conned are they likely to register and transmit that message. At other times, when it is not clear that we are being taken, our stomachs may never catch on. Under those circumstances we have to look elsewhere for a clue. The situation of my neighbor Sara provides a good illustration. She made an important commitment to Tim by canceling her prior marriage plans. That commitment has grown its own supports, so that even though the original reasons for the commitment are gone, she remains in harmony with it. She has convinced herself with newly formed reasons that she did the right thing, so she stays with Tim. It is not difficult to see why there would be no tightening in Sara's stomach as a result. Stomachs tell us when we are doing something we think is wrong for us. Sara thinks no such thing. To her mind, she has chosen correctly and is behaving consistently with that choice.

胃并不是特别敏感或细腻的器官。只有当我们明显意识到自己即将被骗时，它才有可能感知并传递这一信息。其他时候，当我们并不明显意识到自己被骗时，我们的胃可能永远不会有所察觉。在这种情况下，我们必须从其他方面寻找线索。我的邻居萨拉的情况就是一个很好的例子。她取消了之前的结婚计划，对蒂姆做出了一个重要的承诺。这个承诺已经发展出自己的支撑，即使最初做出承诺的理由已经消失，她仍然对此感到满意。她用新形成的理由说服自己，她做的是正确的，所以她留在了蒂姆身边。不难理解为什么萨拉的胃不会因此而感到不安。胃会在我们做我们认为对自己不利的事情时发出信号。萨拉并不这么认为。在她看来，她做出了正确的选择，并且她的行为也与这个选择相符。

Yet, unless I badly miss my guess, there is a part of Sara that recognizes her choice as a mistake and her current living arrangement as a brand of foolish consistency. Where, exactly, that part of Sara is located we can't be sure. But our language does give it a name: heart of hearts. It is, by definition, the one place where we cannot fool ourselves. It is the place where none of our justifications, none of our rationalizations penetrate. Sara has the truth there, although, right now, she can't hear its signal clearly through the noise and static of the new support apparatus she has erected.

然而，除非我猜得完全错误，否则萨拉内心深处一定明白，她现在的选择是个错误，而她目前的生活方式则是一种愚蠢的坚持。我们无法确定萨拉内心深处的这一部分究竟位于何处。但我们的语言赋予了它一个名字：内心深处。顾名思义，它是我们无法自欺欺人的地方。在那里，我们所有的辩解和理由都无法触及。萨拉的内心深处藏着真相，尽管此刻，她无法透过自己搭建起来的这套新体系的喧嚣和干扰，清晰地听到真相的信号。

If Sara has erred in her choice of Tim, how long could she go without clearly recognizing it, without having a massive heart of hearts attack? There is no telling. One thing is certain, however: As time passes, the various alternatives to Tim are disappearing. She had better determine soon whether she is making a mistake.

如果萨拉当初选择蒂姆是个错误，她究竟要多久才能意识到这一点，才会突然感到心惊胆战？谁也说不准。但有一点可以肯定：随着时间的流逝，除了蒂姆之外的其他选择正在逐渐消失。她最好尽快弄清楚自己是否做错了。

Easier said than done, of course. She must answer an extremely intricate question: "Knowing what I now know, if I could go back in time, would I make the same choice?" The problem lies in the "Knowing what I now know" part of the question. Just what does she now know, accurately, about Tim? How much of what she thinks of him is the result of a desperate attempt to justify the commitment she made? She claims that since her decision to take him back, he cares for her more, is trying hard to stop his excessive drinking, has learned to make a wonderful omelet, etc. Having tasted a couple of his omelets, I have my doubts. The important issue, though, is whether she believes these things, not just intellectually—we can play such mind games on ourselves—but in her heart of hearts.

当然，说起来容易做起来难。她必须回答一个极其复杂的问题：“如果我能回到过去，以我现在的认知，我还会做出同样的选择吗？”问题就出在“以我现在的认知”这部分。她现在究竟对蒂姆了解多少？她对他的看法有多少是出于一种绝望的自我安慰，想要为自己当初的决定辩解？她声称，自从她决定和他复合后，他更加关心她了，正在努力戒酒，还学会了做美味的煎蛋卷等等。尝过他做的几个煎蛋卷之后，我对此表示怀疑。然而，关键在于，她是否真的相信这些，不仅仅是理智上的——我们常常会自欺欺人——而是发自内心的。

There may be a little device Sara can use to find out how much of her current satisfaction with Tim is real and how much is foolish consistency. Accumulating psychological evidence indicates that we experience our feelings toward something a split second before we can intellectu-alize about it. My suspicion is that the message sent by the heart of hearts is a pure, basic feeling. Therefore, if we train ourselves to be attentive, we should register it ever so slightly before our cognitive apparatus engages. According to this approach, were Sara to ask herself the crucial "Would I make the same choice again?" question, she would be well advised to look for and trust the first flash of feeling she experienced in response. It would likely be the signal from her heart of hearts, slipping through undistorted just before the means by which she could kid herself flooded in.

萨拉或许可以用某种小工具来分辨她目前对蒂姆的满意程度有多少是真心的，又有多少只是愚蠢的妥协。越来越多的心理学证据表明，我们对某件事物的感受会在我们能够理性思考之前瞬间产生。我怀疑，这种发自内心的信息是一种纯粹而基本的感受。因此，如果我们训练自己保持觉察，就能在认知机制启动之前，极其细微地感知到它。按照这种思路，如果萨拉问自己那个关键问题：“我会再次做出同样的选择吗？”，那么她最好去寻找并相信自己最初感受到的那种感觉。这很可能就是她内心深处的信号，在她用来欺骗自己的各种手段涌入之前，未经任何扭曲地溜了出来。

I have begun using the same device myself whenever I even suspect I might be acting in a foolishly consistent manner. One time, for instance, I had stopped at the self-service pump of a filling station advertising a price per gallon a couple of cents below the rate of other stations in the area. But with pump nozzle in hand, I noticed that the price listed on the pump was two cents higher than the display sign price. When I mentioned the difference to a passing attendant, who I later learned was the owner, he mumbled uncon-vincingly that the rates had changed a few days ago but there hadn't been time to correct the display. I tried to decide what to do. Some reasons for staying came to mind—"I really do need gasoline badly." "This pump is available, and I am in sort of a hurry." "I think I remember that my car runs better on this brand of g as ."

每当我怀疑自己可能做出愚蠢而又始终如一的行为时，我都会使用同样的装置。例如，有一次，我停在一家加油站的自助加油机前，广告上说这家加油站的汽油价格比附近其他加油站低几美分。但当我拿起油枪时，我注意到油枪上显示的价格比广告牌上的价格高出两美分。我把这个差价告诉了一位路过的服务员（后来我才知道他是老板），他含糊其辞地说价格几天前就变了，但还没来得及更新显示屏。我努力想决定该怎么办。一些留下的理由浮现在脑海里——“我真的急需汽油。”“这个油枪空着，而且我有点赶时间。”“我记得我的车用这个牌子的汽油跑得更好。”

I needed to determine whether those reasons were genuine or mere justifications for my decision to stop there. So I asked myself the crucial question, "Knowing what I know about the real price of this gasoline, if I could go back in time, would I make the same choice again?" Concentrating on the first burst of impression I sensed, the answer was clear and unqualified. I would have driven right past. I wouldn't even have slowed down. I knew then that without the price advantage, those other reasons would not have brought me there. They hadn't created the decision; the decision had created them.

我需要判断那些理由是真心实意，还是仅仅为了替我停车找借口。于是我问了自己一个关键问题：“如果我能回到过去，了解了汽油的真实价格，我还会做出同样的选择吗？” 我专注于最初的感受，答案清晰而明确。我会直接开过去，甚至都不会减速。我当时就明白，如果没有价格优势，其他那些理由根本不会让我停在这里。不是它们促成了我的决定，而是我的决定造就了它们。

That settled, there was another decision to be faced, though. Since I was already there holding the hose, wouldn't it be better to use it than to suffer the inconvenience of going elsewhere to pay the same price? Fortunately, the station attendant-owner came over and helped me make up my mind. He asked why I wasn't pumping any gas. I told him I didn't like the price discrepancy, and he said with a snarl, "Listen, nobody's gonna tell me how to run my business. If you think I'm cheating you, just put that hose down right now and get off my property as fast as you can do it, bud." Already certain he was a cheat, I was happy to act consistently with my belief and his wishes. I dropped the hose on the spot... and drove over it on my way to the closest exit. Sometimes consistency can be a marvelously rewarding thing.

事情解决了，但我还得面对另一个抉择。既然我已经拿着油管了，与其费劲跑到别的地方去付同样的价钱，不如直接用它加油，岂不是更好？幸好，加油站的老板兼服务员走了过来，帮我做了决定。他问我为什么不加油。我告诉他，我不满意价格差异，他却咆哮道：“听着，没人能教我怎么经营生意。你要是觉得我坑你，就立刻把油管放下，赶紧滚出我的地盘，小子。” 我早就认定他是个骗子，所以很乐意按照自己的想法和他的意思行事。我当场扔掉了油管……然后开车从它上面碾过去，驶向最近的出口。有时候，坚持原则真的会带来意想不到的好处。

READER'S REPORT

读者报告

From a Woman Living in Portland, Oregon

来自一位居住在俄勒冈州波特兰市的女士

"I was walking through downtown Portland on my way to a lunch appointment when a young, attractive man stopped me with a friendly smile and a powerful line: 'Excuse me, I'm involved in a contest and I need a good-looking woman like yourself to help me win.' I was truly skeptical, since I know there are many more attractive women than myself running around; however, I was caught off guard and was curious to find out what he wanted. He explained that he would receive points for a contest by getting total strangers to give him a kiss. Now I consider myself a fairly level-headed person who shouldn't have believed his line, but he was quite persistent, and since I was almost late for my lunch appointment, I thought, 'What the heck, I'll give the guy a kiss and get out of here.' So I did something totally against my common sense and pecked this total stranger on the cheek in the middle of downtown Portland!

“那天我正走在波特兰市中心，准备去赴午餐约会。突然，一个年轻帅气的男人拦住了我，脸上带着友好的微笑，说道：‘打扰一下，我正在参加一个比赛，需要像你这样漂亮的女士帮我赢得比赛。’我当时真的有点怀疑，因为我知道比我漂亮的女人多了去了；不过，我还是被他的话惊到了，很好奇他到底想干什么。他解释说，他可以通过让陌生人亲吻他来获得比赛积分。我自认为是个相当理智的人，不应该相信他的话，但他非常坚持，而且我午餐约会快要迟到了，所以我想：‘管他呢，就亲他一下然后赶紧走吧。’于是，我做了件完全违背常理的事，在波特兰市中心亲了这个陌生人的脸颊！”

"I thought that would be the end of it, but I soon learned that it was just the beginning. Much to my distress, he followed the kiss with the line 'You are a great kisser, but the real contest I am involved in is to sell magazine subscriptions. You must be an active person. Would any of these magazines interest you?' At this point I should have slugged the guy and walked away; but somehow, because I had complied with his initial request, I felt a need to be consistent, and I complied with his second request. Yes, much to my own disbelief, I actually subscribed to SKI magazine (which I occasionally enjoy reading, but had no intention of subscribing to), gave him a five-dollar initial-subscription fee and left as quickly as possible, feeling quite frustrated with what I had just done and not understanding why I had done it.

我以为事情就此结束了，但很快我就发现这仅仅是个开始。更让我恼火的是，他吻完我之后竟然说：“你的吻技真棒，但我真正想参加的是推销杂志订阅的比赛。你肯定是个很活跃的人。这些杂志里有没有你感兴趣的？” 当时我真应该揍他一顿然后走人；但不知怎么的，因为我答应了他第一个要求，就觉得应该前后一致，于是又答应了他的第二个要求。没错，我自己都难以置信，我竟然真的订阅了《SKI》杂志（我偶尔会看看，但根本没打算订阅），给了他五美元的订阅费，然后赶紧溜走了。我对自己刚才的所作所为感到非常懊恼，也不明白自己为什么会这么做。

"Although it still pains me to think about it, in reflecting on the incident after reading your book, I've now figured out what happened. The reason this tactic worked so effectively is because once small commitments have been made (in this case, giving a kiss), people tend to add justifications to support the commitment and then are willing to commit themselves further. In this situation, I justified complying with the second request because it was consistent with my initial action. If I had only listened to my 'stomach signs,' I could have saved myself a lot of humiliation."

“虽然现在想起来仍然让我感到痛苦，但在读了你的书之后，我反思了这件事，现在明白了事情的来龙去脉。这种策略之所以如此有效，是因为一旦人们做出了小的承诺（比如，亲吻），他们往往会找各种理由来支持自己的承诺，然后就愿意做出更大的承诺。在这种情况下，我之所以答应第二个要求，是因为它与我最初的行为一致。如果我当时听从了内心的直觉，就能避免很多尴尬。”

By extracting a kiss, the salesman exploited the consistency principle in two ways. First, by the time he asked for her aid in the magazine contest, his prospect had already gone on record—with that kiss—as agreeing to help him win a contest. Second, it seems only natural (i.e., congruent) that if a woman feels positively enough toward a man to kiss him, she should feel positively toward helping him out.

通过索取一个吻，这位推销员巧妙地利用了一致性原则，体现在两个方面。首先，当他请求她帮忙参加杂志比赛时，这位潜在客户已经通过那个吻表明了她愿意帮助他赢得比赛。其次，如果一个女人对一个男人有好感到愿意亲吻他，那么她也应该乐于帮助他，这似乎是顺理成章的（即符合逻辑的）。

# ↩

Chapter 4 - SOCIAL PROOF

第四章——社会认同

Truths Are Us

真理即我们

Where all think alike, no one thinks very much.
当所有人都想法一致时，就没有人真正思考过。
— W ALTER L IPPMANN
——沃尔特·利普曼

I DON'T KNOW ANYONE WHO LIKES CANNED LAUGHTER. IN FACT, when I surveyed the people who came into my office one day—several students, two telephone repairmen, a number of university professors, and the janitor—the reaction was invariably critical. Television, with its incessant system of laugh tracks and technically augmented mirth, received the most heat. The people I questioned hated canned laughter. They called it stupid, phony, and obvious. Although my sample was small, I would bet that it closely reflects the negative feelings of most of the American public toward laugh tracks.

我认识的人里没有一个喜欢罐头笑声的。事实上，有一天我调查了来我办公室的人——几个学生、两个电话维修工、几位大学教授和清洁工——他们的反应无一例外都是批评。电视节目，尤其是那些充斥着罐头笑声和技术增强效果的节目，受到的抨击最多。我调查的这些人讨厌罐头笑声。他们说它愚蠢、虚假、拙劣。虽然我的样本量很小，但我敢肯定，它能很好地反映大多数美国公众对罐头笑声的负面看法。

Why, then, is canned laughter so popular with television executives? They have won their exalted positions and splendid salaries by knowing how to give the public what it wants. Yet they religiously employ the laugh tracks that their audiences find distasteful. And they do so over the objections of many of their most talented artists. It is not uncommon for acclaimed directors, writers, or actors to demand the elimination of canned responses from the television projects they undertake. These demands are only sometimes successful, and when they are, it is not without a battle.

那么，为什么罐头笑声如此受电视高管青睐呢？他们之所以能身居高位、收入丰厚，正是因为他们懂得如何迎合观众的喜好。然而，他们却执意使用观众反感的罐头笑声，而且不顾众多才华横溢的艺术家们的反对。知名导演、编剧或演员要求在他们参与的电视项目中取消罐头笑声的情况并不少见。这些要求并非总能成功，即便成功，也往往是一场艰苦的斗争。

What could it be about canned laughter that is so attractive to television executives? Why would these shrewd and tested businessmen champion a practice that their potential watchers find disagreeable and their most creative talents find personally insulting? The answer is at once simple and intriguing: They know what the research says. Experiments have found that the use of canned merriment causes an audience to laugh longer and more often when humorous material is presented and to rate the material as funnier. In addition, some evidence indicates that canned laughter is most effective for poor jokes.

电视高管们为何如此钟情于罐头笑声？这些精明老练的商人为何会支持这种做法，而他们的潜在观众却对此感到反感，甚至连他们最具创造力的人才也觉得受到了侮辱？答案既简单又耐人寻味：他们了解研究结果。实验发现，使用罐头笑声能让观众在观看幽默内容时笑得更久、更频繁，并且觉得内容更有趣。此外，一些证据表明，罐头笑声对那些不太好笑的笑话尤其有效。

In the light of these data, the actions of television executives make perfect sense. The introduction of laugh tracks into their comic programming will increase the humorous and appreciative responses of an audience, even—and especially—when the material is of poor quality. Is it any surprise, then, that television, glutted as it is with artless situ-ation-comedy attempts, should be saturated with canned laughter? Those executives know precisely what they are doing.

鉴于这些数据，电视高管们的做法完全合情合理。在喜剧节目中加入罐头笑声，即使——尤其是在——节目质量低劣的情况下，也能提升观众的幽默感和欣赏度。那么，充斥着大量拙劣情景喜剧的电视节目充斥着罐头笑声也就不足为奇了。这些高管们非常清楚自己在做什么。

But with the mystery of the widespread use of laugh tracks solved, we are left with a more perplexing question: Why does canned laughter work on us the way it does? It is no longer the television executives who appear peculiar; they are acting logically and in their own interests. Instead, it is the behavior of the audience, of you and me, that seems strange. Why should we laugh more at comedy material afloat in a sea of mechanically fabricated merriment? And why should we think that comic flotsam funnier? The executives aren't really fooling us. Anyone can recognize dubbed laughter. It is so blatant, so clearly counterfeit, that there could be no confusing it with the real thing. We know full well that the hilarity we hear is irrelevant to the humorous quality of the joke it follows, that it is created not spontaneously by a genuine audience, but artificially by a technician at a control board. Yet, transparent forgery that it is, it works on us!

但随着罐头笑声广泛使用的谜团解开，我们面临着一个更令人困惑的问题：为什么罐头笑声对我们如此有效？电视高管们不再显得古怪；他们的行为合情合理，也符合自身利益。相反，真正奇怪的是观众——你我——的行为。为什么我们会对漂浮在机械制造的欢乐海洋中的喜剧素材笑得更多？为什么我们会觉得这些喜剧碎片更有趣？高管们其实骗不了我们。任何人都能识别出配音笑声。它如此明目张胆，如此明显地是伪造的，以至于根本无法与真实的笑声混淆。我们非常清楚，我们听到的笑声与它后面的笑话的幽默程度毫无关系，它并非由真正的观众自发产生，而是由控制室里的技术人员人为制造的。然而，尽管它如此拙劣，却依然对我们有效！

To discover why canned laughter is so effective, we first need to understand the nature of yet another potent weapon of influence: the principle of social proof. It states that one means we use to determine what is correct is to find out what other people think is correct. The principle applies especially to the way we decide what constitutes correct behavior. We view a behavior as more correct in a given situation to the degree that we see others performing it. Whether the question is what to do with an empty popcorn box in a movie theater, how fast to drive on a certain stretch of highway, or how to eat the chicken at a dinner party, the actions of those around us will be important in defining the answer.

要探究罐头笑声为何如此有效，我们首先需要了解另一种强大的影响力武器：社会认同原则。该原则指出，我们判断正确与否的方法之一，就是了解其他人认为什么是正确的。这一原则尤其适用于我们判断何为正确行为的方式。在特定情境下，我们看到其他人采取某种行为的程度越高，我们就越认为这种行为是正确的。无论是如何处理电影院里空的爆米花盒、在某段高速公路上应该开多快，还是在晚宴上如何吃鸡肉，我们周围人的行为都会对最终答案的确定产生重要影响。

The tendency to see an action as more appropriate when others are doing it normally works quite well. As a rule, we will make fewer mistakes by acting in accord with social evidence than contrary to it. Usually, when a lot of people are doing something, it is the right thing to do. This feature of the principle of social proof is simultaneously its major strength and its major weakness. Like the other weapons of influence, it provides a convenient shortcut for determining how to behave but, at the same time, makes one who uses the shortcut vulnerable to the attacks of profiteers who lie in wait along its path.

人们往往倾向于认为，当其他人都在做某件事时，这件事本身也更合适，这种倾向通常很有效。一般来说，我们遵循社会经验行事比违背社会经验行事犯错更少。通常情况下，当很多人都在做某件事时，这件事就是正确的。社会认同原则的这一特点既是它的主要优势，也是它的主要弱点。与其他影响力工具一样，它为判断行为方式提供了一条便捷的捷径，但同时也使使用这条捷径的人容易受到那些伺机而动的投机者的攻击。

In the case of canned laughter, the problem comes when we begin responding to social proof in such a mindless and reflexive fashion that we can be fooled by partial or fake evidence. Our folly is not that we use others' laughter to help decide what is humorous and when mirth is appropriate; that is in keeping with the well-founded principle of social proof. The folly is that we do so in response to patently fraudulent laughter. Somehow, one disembodied feature of humor—a sound—works like the essence of humor. The example from Chapter 1 of the turkey and the polecat is instructive here. Remember that because the particular "cheep-cheep" of turkey chicks is normally associated with newborn turkeys, their mothers will display or withhold maternal care solely on the basis of that sound? And remember how, consequently, it was possible to trick a female turkey into mothering a stuffed polecat as long as the replica played the recorded "cheep-cheep" of a baby turkey? The simulated chick sound was enough to start the female's mothering tape whirring.

就罐头笑声而言，问题在于我们开始以一种盲目且下意识的方式回应社会认同，以至于会被片面或虚假的证据所蒙蔽。我们的愚蠢之处不在于我们利用他人的笑声来判断什么是幽默以及何时应该发笑；这符合社会认同这一根深蒂固的原则。真正的愚蠢之处在于，我们竟然会用这种做法来回应那些明显是虚假的笑声。不知何故，幽默中一个脱离具体事物的特征——声音——似乎成了幽默的本质。第一章中火鸡和白鼬的例子就很有启发性。还记得吗？因为小火鸡特有的“唧唧”声通常与新生火鸡联系在一起，所以它们的母亲会仅仅根据这种声音来决定是否给予母爱。因此，你还记得吗？只要播放录制好的小火鸡“唧唧”的叫声，就能诱骗雌火鸡去哺育一只填充的白鼬。模拟的小鸡叫声足以让雌火鸡开始发出哺育的信号。

The lesson of the turkey and the polecat illustrates uncomfortably well the relationship between the average viewer and the laugh-track-playing television executive. We have become so accustomed to taking the humorous reactions of others as evidence of what deserves laughter that we, too, can be made to respond to the sound and not to the substance of the real thing. Much as a "cheep-cheep" noise removed from the reality of a chick can stimulate a female turkey to mother, so can a recorded "ha-ha" removed from the reality of a genuine audience stimulate us to laugh. The television executives are exploiting our preference for shortcuts, our tendency to react automatically on the basis of partial evidence. They know that their tapes will cue our tapes. Click, whirr.

火鸡和白鼬的故事令人不安地揭示了普通观众与播放罐头笑声的电视高管之间的关系。我们已经习惯于将他人的幽默反应作为判断笑点是否值得发笑的证据，以至于我们自己也会被声音而非内容本身所左右。正如脱离雏鸡真实声音的“啾啾”声可以刺激雌火鸡产仔一样，脱离真实观众的录制“哈哈”声也能让我们发笑。电视高管们正是利用了我们喜欢走捷径的习惯，以及我们基于片面信息就自动做出反应的倾向。他们知道，他们的录像带会引导我们的反应。咔哒，嗡嗡。

Television executives are hardly alone in their use of social evidence for profit. Our tendency to assume that an action is more correct if others are doing it is exploited in a variety of settings. Bartenders often "salt" their tip jars with a few dollar bills at the beginning of the evening to simulate tips left by prior customers and thereby to give the impression that tipping with folding money is proper barroom behavior. Church ushers sometimes salt collection baskets for the same reason and with the same positive effect on proceeds. Evangelical preachers are known to seed their audience with "ringers," who are rehearsed to come forward at a specified time to give witness and donations. For example, an Arizona State University research team that infiltrated the Billy Graham organization reported on such advance preparations prior to one of his Crusade visits. "By the time Graham arrives in town and makes his altar call, an army of six thousand wait with instructions on when to come forth at varying intervals to create the impression of a spontaneous mass outpouring." 2

利用社会证据牟利的并非只有电视高管。我们往往会认为，如果其他人都在做某件事，那么这件事就更正确，这种倾向在各种场合都被利用。酒吧招待员经常在晚上开始时往小费罐里放几张美元钞票，模拟之前顾客留下的小费，从而给人一种印象：用折叠的钞票给小费才是酒吧里应有的行为。教堂招待员有时也会出于同样的原因在奉献篮里放些钱，同样能提高捐款额。众所周知，福音派牧师会在听众中安排“炮灰”，这些人经过排练，会在特定时间上前作见证并募捐。例如，亚利桑那州立大学的一个研究小组渗透到葛培理的组织中，并在葛培理的一次布道会之前就发现了这种预先安排。 “当葛培理抵达镇上并开始呼召信徒时，六千名信徒早已等候在那里，他们事先接到指示，分批依次上前，以营造出自发群众涌现的景象。”

Advertisers love to inform us when a product is the "fastest-growing" or "largest-selling" because they don't have to convince us directly that the product is good, they need only say that many others think so, which seems proof enough. The producers of charity telethons devote inordinate amounts of time to the incessant listing of viewers who have already pledged contributions. The message being communicated to the holdouts is clear: "Look at all the people who have decided to give. It must be the correct thing to do." At the height of the disco craze, certain discotheque owners manufactured a brand of visible social proof for their clubs' quality by creating long waiting lines outside when there was plenty of room inside. Salesmen are taught to spice their pitches with numerous accounts of individuals who have purchased the product. Sales and motivation consultant Cavett Robert captures the principle nicely in his advice to sales trainees: "Since 95 percent of the people are imitators and only 5 percent initiators, people are persuaded more by the actions of others than by any proof we can offer."
