但菲利普斯的洞见还有第二个宝贵之处。它不仅能解释现有的事实，还能预测以前从未发现的新事实。例如，如果自杀事件曝光后异常频繁的坠机事故确实是模仿而非意外造成的，那么这些事故的致命性应该更高。也就是说，试图自杀的人很可能会精心安排（比如踩油门而不是刹车，让飞机机头向下而不是向上），使撞击尽可能致命。其结果应该是迅速而确定的死亡。菲利普斯查阅记录以验证这一预测时发现，如果商业客机的致命坠机事故发生在头版自杀报道一周后，那么平均死亡人数是发生在自杀报道一周前的三倍多。类似的现象也可以在交通统计数据中找到，有证据表明，自杀报道后发生的交通事故的致命性更高。在头版刊登自杀新闻后发生的致命车祸中，受害者的死亡速度比正常情况快四倍。

Still another fascinating prediction flows from Phillips's idea. If the increase in wrecks following suicide stories truly represents a set of copycat deaths, then the imitators should be most likely to copy the suicides of people who are similar to them. The principle of social proof states that we use information about how others have behaved to help us determine proper conduct for ourselves. But as the dropped-wallet experiment showed, we are most influenced in this fashion by the actions of others like us.

菲利普斯的观点还引出了另一个引人入胜的预测。如果自杀事件后车祸数量的增加确实代表了一系列模仿自杀，那么模仿者最有可能效仿与自己相似的人的自杀行为。社会认同原则指出，我们会利用他人的行为信息来帮助我们判断自身的行为是否恰当。但正如“丢钱包实验”所表明的那样，我们最容易受到与自己相似的人的行为的影响。

Therefore, Phillips reasoned, if the principle of social proof is behind the phenomenon, there should be some clear similarity between the victim of the highly publicized suicide and those who cause subsequent wrecks. Realizing that the clearest test of this possibility would come from the records of automobile crashes involving a single car and a lone driver, Phillips compared the age of the suicide-story victim with the ages of the lone drivers killed in single-car crashes immediately after the story appeared in print. Once again the predictions were strikingly accurate: When the newspaper detailed the suicide of a young person, it was young drivers who then piled their cars into trees, poles, and embankments with fatal results; but when the news story concerned an older person's suicide, older drivers died in such crashes.

因此，菲利普斯推断，如果社会认同原则是这一现象背后的驱动力，那么备受瞩目的自杀事件的受害者与随后引发车祸的肇事者之间应该存在某种明显的相似之处。菲利普斯意识到，检验这种可能性的最直接方法是查阅涉及单车和单人驾驶的交通事故记录，于是他将自杀事件受害者的年龄与该报道刊登后不久发生的单车事故中丧生的单人驾驶者的年龄进行了比较。结果再次惊人地准确：当报纸详细报道一名年轻人的自杀事件时，随后发生致命车祸的往往是年轻驾驶员，他们的车辆撞向树木、电线杆或路堤；而当新闻报道涉及一名老年人的自杀事件时，死于此类车祸的往往是老年驾驶员。

This last statistic is the crusher for me. I am left wholly convinced and, simultaneously, wholly amazed by it. Evidently, the principle of social proof is so wide-ranging and powerful that its domain extends to the fundamental decision for life or death. Professor Phillips's findings have persuaded me of a distressing tendency for suicide publicity to motivate certain people who are similar to the victim to kill them-selves—because they now find the idea of suicide more legitimate. Truly frightening are the data indicating that many innocent people die in the bargain. A glance at the graphs documenting the undeniable increase in traffic and air fatalities following publicized suicides, especially those involving murder, is enough to cause concern for one's own safety. I have been sufficiently affected by these statistics to begin to take note of front-page suicide stories and to change my behavior in the period after their appearance. I try to be especially cautious behind the wheel of my car. I am reluctant to take extended trips requiring a lot of air travel. If I must fly during such a period, I purchase substantially more flight insurance than I normally would. Dr. Phillips has done us a service by demonstrating that the odds for survival when we travel change measurably for a time following the publication of certain kinds of front-page suicide stories. It would seem only prudent to play those odds.

最后这条统计数据让我彻底崩溃。它让我完全信服，同时也让我感到无比震惊。显然，社会认同原则的影响范围如此广泛、力量如此强大，甚至延伸到了生死攸关的根本抉择。菲利普斯教授的研究结果让我确信，自杀事件的公开报道会诱使一些与死者相似的人自杀——因为他们觉得自杀的想法变得更加合理。更令人恐惧的是，数据显示，许多无辜的人也因此丧命。只需看看那些图表，就能发现，在公开报道自杀事件（尤其是涉及谋杀的自杀事件）之后，交通事故和空难死亡人数无疑会大幅增加，这足以让人担忧自身安全。这些统计数据深深触动了我，让我开始关注报纸头版上的自杀报道，并在报道刊登后的一段时间内改变自己的行为。我开车时格外小心，也尽量避免需要频繁乘坐飞机的长途旅行。如果我必须在这段时间乘坐飞机，我会购买比平时多得多的航空保险。菲利普斯博士的研究表明，在某些类型的自杀新闻刊登在报纸头版之后的一段时间内，我们旅行时的生存几率会发生显著变化，这对我们大有裨益。因此，谨慎行事似乎是理所当然的。

As if the frightening features of Phillips's suicide data weren't enough, his subsequent research brings more cause for alarm: Homicides in this country have a stimulated, copycat character after highly publicized acts of violence. Heavyweight championship prize fights that receive coverage on network evening news appear to produce measurable increases in the U.S. homicide rate. This analysis of heavyweight championship fights (between 1973 and 1978) is perhaps most compelling in its demonstration of the remarkably specific nature of the imitative aggression that is generated. When such a match was lost by a black fighter, the homicide rate during the following ten days rose significantly for young black male victims but not young white males. On the other hand, when a white fighter lost a match, it was young white men but not young black men who were killed more frequently in the next ten days. When these results are combined with the parallel findings in Phillips's suicide data, it is clear that widely publicized aggression has the nasty tendency to spread to similar victims, no matter whether the aggression is inflicted on the self or on another.

菲利普斯的自杀数据已经令人震惊，而他随后的研究更是加剧了这种担忧：在美国，备受瞩目的暴力事件之后，凶杀案往往会受到刺激，并出现模仿犯罪的现象。那些在晚间新闻电视网播出的重量级拳击冠军赛似乎会导致美国凶杀率显著上升。这项对1973年至1978年间重量级拳击冠军赛的分析，或许最引人注目之处在于它揭示了这种模仿性攻击行为的显著特征。当黑人拳击手输掉比赛后，接下来十天内，年轻黑人男性受害者的凶杀率显著上升，而年轻白人男性受害者的凶杀率则没有上升。另一方面，当白人拳击手输掉比赛后，接下来十天内被杀害的主要是年轻白人男性，而不是年轻黑人男性。将这些结果与菲利普斯自杀数据中的平行发现结合起来，可以清楚地看出，广为人知的攻击行为具有蔓延到类似受害者的恶劣倾向，无论这种攻击行为是针对自身还是针对他人。

Work like Dr. Phillips's helps us appreciate the awesome influence of the behavior of similar others. Once the enormity of that force is recognized, it becomes possible to understand perhaps the most spectacular act of compliance of our time—the mass suicide at Jonestown, Guyana. Certain crucial features of that event deserve review.

菲利普斯博士等人的研究有助于我们理解相似人群行为的巨大影响力。一旦认识到这种力量的强大，我们或许就能理解我们这个时代最令人震惊的集体服从行为——圭亚那琼斯镇的集体自杀。该事件的某些关键特征值得我们重新审视。

The People's Temple was a cultlike organization that began in San Francisco and drew its recruits from the poor of that city. In 1977, the Reverend Jim Jones—who was the group's undisputed political, social, and spiritual leader—moved the bulk of the membership with him to a jungle settlement in Guyana, South America. There, the People's Temple existed in relative obscurity until November 18, 1978, when four men of a fact-finding party led by Congressman Leo J. Ryan were murdered as they tried to leave Jonestown by plane. Convinced that he would be arrested and implicated in the killings and that the demise of the People's Temple would result, Jones sought to control the end of the Temple in his own way. He gathered the entire community around him and issued a call for each person's death in a unified act of self-destruction.

人民圣殿教是一个类似邪教的组织，起源于旧金山，其成员主要来自该市的贫民。1977年，该组织无可争议的政治、社会和精神领袖吉姆·琼斯牧师带领大部分成员迁往南美洲圭亚那丛林中的一个定居点。在那里，人民圣殿教一直相对隐秘地存在着，直到1978年11月18日，由国会议员利奥·J·瑞安率领的调查小组的四名成员在试图乘飞机离开琼斯镇时被谋杀。琼斯确信自己会被逮捕并牵连其中，人民圣殿教也将因此覆灭，于是他试图以自己的方式掌控圣殿教的终结。他召集了整个社群，号召所有人集体自杀，以一场统一的自我毁灭行动结束生命。

The first response was that of a young woman who calmly approached the now famous vat of strawberry-flavored poison, administered one dose to her baby, one to herself, and then sat down in a field, where she and her child died in convulsions within four minutes. Others followed steadily in turn. Although a handful of Jonestowners escaped rather than comply and a few others are reported to have resisted, the survivors claim that the great majority of the 910 people who died did so in an orderly, willful fashion.

第一个响应者是一位年轻女子，她冷静地走向那桶如今闻名遐迩的草莓味毒药，先给她的婴儿服下一剂，自己也服下一剂，然后坐在田野里，她和孩子在四分钟内抽搐而死。其他人也陆续效仿。虽然有少数琼斯镇居民选择逃跑而不是服从，也有报道称少数人进行了抵抗，但幸存者声称，910名死者中的绝大多数都是有条不紊、心甘情愿地死去的。

News of the event shocked us. The broadcast media and the papers provided a barrage of reports, updates, and analyses. For days, our conversations were full of the topic: "How many have they found dead now?" "A guy who escaped says they were drinking the poison like they were hypnotized or something." "What were they doing down in South America, anyway?" "It's so hard to believe. What caused it?"

事件的消息让我们震惊不已。广播媒体和报纸铺天盖地地报道、更新和分析。接下来的几天，我们每天都在谈论这个话题：“现在找到多少具尸体了？”“一个幸存者说，他们喝毒药的时候就像被催眠了一样。”“他们到底去南美洲干什么？”“这太难以置信了。到底是什么原因造成的？”

Yes, "What caused it?"—the critical question. How are we to account for this most astounding of compliant acts? Various explanations have been offered. Some have focused on the charisma of Jim Jones, a man whose style allowed him to be loved like a savior, trusted like a father, and treated like an emperor. Other explanations have pointed to the kind of people who were attracted to the People's Temple. They were mostly poor and uneducated individuals who were willing to give up their freedoms of thought and action for the safety of a place where all decisions would be made for them. Still other explanations have emphasized the quasi-religious nature of the People's Temple, in which unquestioned faith in the cult's leader was assigned highest priority.

是的，“是什么导致了这一切？”——这才是关键问题。我们该如何解释这种令人震惊的顺从行为？人们提出了各种各样的解释。一些人将重点放在吉姆·琼斯的个人魅力上，他以救世主般的形象被爱戴，以父亲般的信任被信赖，以皇帝般的地位被尊崇。另一些人则将目光投向了人民圣殿教的信徒群体。他们大多是贫穷且缺乏教育的人，为了在一个所有决定都由他人代为做出的地方寻求安全，他们甘愿放弃思想和行动的自由。还有一些人则强调了人民圣殿教的准宗教性质，在这个教派中，对教主的绝对信仰被置于首位。

No doubt each of these features of Jonestown has merit in explaining what happened there. But I do not find them sufficient. After all, the world abounds with cults populated by dependent people who are led by a charismatic figure. What's more, there has never been a shortage of this combination of circumstances in the past. Yet virtually nowhere do we find evidence of an event even approximating the Jonestown incident among such groups. There must be something else that was critical.

毫无疑问，琼斯镇事件的这些特征都有助于解释那里发生的事情。但我认为它们还不够充分。毕竟，世界上充斥着由魅力非凡的领袖领导、信徒高度依赖的邪教组织。而且，历史上这类情况并不少见。然而，我们几乎找不到任何证据表明，在这些组织中发生过哪怕是与琼斯镇事件类似的事件。必然还有其他关键因素。

One especially revealing question gives us a clue: "If the community had remained in San Francisco, would Rev. Jim Jones's suicide command have been obeyed?" A highly speculative question to be sure, but the expert most familiar with the People's Temple has no doubt about the answer. Dr. Louis Jolyon West, chairman of psychiatry and biobehavi-oral sciences at UCLA and director of its neuropsychiatric unit, is an authority on cults who had observed the People's Temple for eight years prior to the Jonestown deaths. When interviewed in the immediate aftermath, he made what strikes me as an inordinately instructive statement: "This wouldn't have happened in California. But they lived in total alienation from the rest of the world in a jungle situation in a hostile country."

一个尤其发人深省的问题为我们提供了一条线索：“如果人民圣殿教留在旧金山，吉姆·琼斯牧师的自杀命令会被执行吗？”这无疑是一个极具推测性的问题，但最了解人民圣殿教的专家对此毫不怀疑。路易斯·乔利恩·韦斯特博士是加州大学洛杉矶分校精神病学和生物行为口腔科学系主任，也是该校神经精神病学部门的主任，他是邪教研究领域的权威，在琼斯镇惨案发生前，他已经观察人民圣殿教长达八年之久。在惨案发生后不久接受采访时，他发表了一番在我看来极具启发性的言论：“这种事不会发生在加州。但他们生活在一个充满敌意的国家，与世隔绝，身处丛林之中。”

Although lost in the welter of commentary following the tragedy, Dr. West's observation, together with what we know about the principle of social proof, seems to me quite important to a satisfactory understanding of the compliant suicides. To my mind, the single act in the history of the People's Temple that most contrib-uted to the members' mindless compliance that day occurred a year earlier with the relocation of the Temple to a jungled country of unfamiliar customs and strange people. If we are to believe the stories of Jim Jones's malevolent genius, he realized fully the massive psychological impact such a move would have on his followers. All at once, they found themselves in a place they knew nothing about. South America, and the rain forests of Guyana, especially, were unlike anything they had experienced in San Francisco.

尽管在悲剧发生后铺天盖地的评论中，韦斯特博士的观察被淹没了，但我认为，结合我们对社会认同原则的了解，对于充分理解这些顺从的自杀者至关重要。在我看来，人民圣殿教历史上导致成员们在那天盲目服从的最主要因素，发生在一年前，当时圣殿教迁往了一个风俗陌生、人民异乡的丛林地带。如果我们相信吉姆·琼斯那邪恶的天才，他完全意识到此举会对他的追随者造成巨大的心理冲击。他们突然发现自己身处一个完全陌生的地方。南美洲，尤其是圭亚那的热带雨林，与他们在旧金山的经历截然不同。

The country—both physical and social—into which they were dropped must have seemed dreadfully uncertain.

他们被空投到的这个国家——无论是自然环境还是社会环境——对他们来说一定充满了可怕的不确定性。

Ah, uncertainty—the right-hand man of the principle of social proof. We have already seen that when people are uncertain, they look to the actions of others to guide their own actions. In the alien, Guyanese environment, then, Temple members were very ready to follow the lead of others. But as we have also seen, it is others of a special kind whose behavior will be most unquestioningly followed—similar others. And therein lies the awful beauty of the Reverend Jim Jones's relocation strategy. In a country like Guyana, there were no similar others for a Jonestown resident but the people of Jonestown itself.

啊，不确定性——社会认同原则的得力助手。我们已经看到，当人们感到迷茫时，他们会观察他人的行为来指导自己的行动。因此，在陌生的圭亚那环境中，圣殿教成员非常乐意效仿他人。但正如我们也看到的，最容易被盲目效仿的，是与自己相似的人。而这正是吉姆·琼斯牧师搬迁策略的可怕之处。在圭亚那这样的国家，对于琼斯镇的居民来说，除了琼斯镇的居民之外，没有其他与自己相似的群体。

What was right for a member of the community was determined to a disproportionate degree by what other community members—influ-enced heavily by Jones—did and believed. When viewed in this light, the terrible orderliness, the lack of panic, the sense of calm with which these people moved to the vat of poison and to their deaths, seems more comprehensible. They hadn't been hypnotized by Jones; they had been convinced—partly by him but, more important, also by the principle of social proof—that suicide was correct conduct. The uncertainty they surely felt upon first hearing the death command must have caused them to look to those around them for a definition of the appropriate response. It is particularly worth noting that they found two impressive pieces of social evidence, each pointing in the same direction.

对于社区成员而言，何为正确之举在很大程度上取决于其他成员——深受琼斯影响——的行为和信念。从这个角度来看，这些人走向毒药桶、走向死亡时所表现出的那种可怕的秩序感、缺乏恐慌和冷静，似乎就更容易理解了。他们并非被琼斯催眠；他们是被说服了——部分是受琼斯的影响，但更重要的是，也是受社会认同原则的影响——自杀才是正确的行为。他们最初听到处死命令时，必然感到茫然，这促使他们向周围的人寻求恰当的回应。尤其值得注意的是，他们找到了两份令人印象深刻的社会证据，而且都指向同一个方向。

The first was the initial set of their compatriots, who quickly and willingly took the poison drafts. There will always be a few such fanatically obedient individuals in any strong-leader-dominated group. Whether, in this instance, they had been specially instructed beforehand to serve as examples or whether they were just naturally the most compliant with Jones's wishes is difficult to know. No matter; the psychological effect of the actions of those individuals must have been potent. If the suicides of similar others in news stories can influence total strangers to kill themselves, imagine how enormously more compelling such an act would be when performed without hesitation by one's neighbors in a place like Jonestown.

第一批是他们的同伴，他们迅速而自愿地服下了毒药。在任何由强势领导者主导的群体中，总会有一些狂热服从者。至于他们是否事先被特别指示以儆效尤，或者只是天性使然，最顺从琼斯的意愿，我们不得而知。但无论如何，这些人的行为必定产生了巨大的心理影响。如果新闻报道中类似案例的自杀就能影响陌生人自杀，那么想象一下，在像琼斯镇这样的地方，如果邻居毫不犹豫地效仿，这种行为的影响力该有多么巨大。

The second source of social evidence came from the reactions of the crowd itself. Given the conditions, I suspect that what occurred was a large-scale instance of the pluralistic ignorance phenomenon that frequently infects onlookers at emergencies. Each Jonestowner looked to the actions of surrounding individuals to assess the situation and—finding seeming calm because everyone else, too, was surreptitiously assessing rather than reacting—"learned" that patient turn taking was the correct behavior. Such misinterpreted but nonetheless convincing social evidence would be expected to result precisely in the ghastly composure of the assemblage that waited in the tropics of Guyana for businesslike death.

第二个社会证据来源是人群自身的反应。鉴于当时的状况，我怀疑所发生的一切是大规模的多元无知现象，这种现象经常在紧急情况下影响旁观者。琼斯镇的每个居民都观察周围人的行为来评估形势，并且——由于其他人也都在暗中评估而非做出反应，所以表面上看起来很平静——“学会”了耐心地轮流行动才是正确的行为。这种被误解但却令人信服的社会证据，理应导致这群人在圭亚那的热带地区静静等待死亡的可怕镇定。

From my own perspective, most attempts to analyze the Jonestown incident have focused too much on the personal qualities of Jim Jones. Although he was without question a man of rare dynamism, the power he wielded strikes me as coming less from his remarkable personal style than from his understanding of fundamental psychological principles. His real genius as a leader was his realization of the limitations of individual leadership. No leader can hope to persuade, regularly and single-handedly, all the members of the group. A forceful leader can reasonably expect, however, to persuade some sizable proportion of group members. Then the raw information that a substantial number of group members has been convinced can, by itself, convince the rest. Thus the most influential leaders are those who know how to arrange group conditions to allow the principle of social proof to work maximally in their favor.

在我看来，大多数对琼斯镇事件的分析都过于关注吉姆·琼斯的个人特质。尽管他无疑是个极具魄力的人，但我认为他所拥有的权力与其说是源于他非凡的个人风格，不如说是源于他对基本心理学原理的理解。他作为领导者的真正过人之处在于他认识到个人领导的局限性。任何领导者都无法指望凭借一己之力持续地、单枪匹马地说服所有成员。然而，一个强有力的领导者完全可以预期说服相当一部分成员。然后，相当一部分成员已被说服这一信息本身就足以说服其余成员。因此，最具影响力的领导者是那些懂得如何营造群体环境，从而最大限度地发挥社会认同原则优势的人。

It is in this that Jones appears to have been inspired. His masterstroke was the decision to move the People's Temple community from its roots in urban San Francisco to the remoteness of equatorial South America, where the conditions of uncertainty and exclusive similarity would make the principle of social proof operate for him as perhaps nowhere else. There, a settlement of a thousand people, much too large to be held in persistent sway by the force of one man's personality, could be changed from a following into a herd. As slaughterhouse operators have long known, the mentality of a herd makes it easy to manage. Simply get some members moving in the desired direction and the others—re-sponding not so much to the lead animal as to those immediately surrounding them—will peacefully and mechanically go along. The powers of the amazing Reverend Jim Jones, then, are probably best understood not in terms of his dramatic personal style, but in his profound knowledge of the art of social jujitsu.

琼斯似乎正是从这一点中汲取了灵感。他的妙招是将人民圣殿教的社群从其位于旧金山的繁华都市迁至赤道南美洲的偏远地区。在那里，不确定性和高度相似性使得社会认同原则对他而言发挥了前所未有的作用。在那里，一个拥有上千人的社群——规模之大，单凭一个人的个人魅力难以维系——可以从一群追随者转变为一群乌合之众。正如屠宰场经营者早已熟知的那样，群体的思维模式使其易于管理。只需让一部分成员朝着既定的方向前进，其余成员——与其说是响应领头羊，不如说是响应周围的同伴——就会平静而机械地跟随。因此，要理解这位神奇的吉姆·琼斯牧师的强大力量，或许并非在于他戏剧化的个人风格，而在于他对社会柔术的深刻理解。

HOW TO SAY NO

如何说“不”

This chapter began with an account of the relatively harmless practice of laugh tracking and has moved on to stories of murder and suicide—all explained by the principle of social proof. How can we expect to defend ourselves against a weapon of influence that pervades such a vast range of behavior? The difficulty is compounded by the realization that most of the time, we don't want to guard against the information that social proof provides. The evidence it offers about how we should act is usually valid and valuable. With it we can cruise confidently through a myriad of decisions without personally having to investigate the detailed pros and cons of each.

本章以相对无害的笑声追踪技术开篇，随后探讨了谋杀和自杀案例——所有这些都可以用社会认同原则来解释。面对这种渗透到如此广泛行为领域的强大影响力，我们该如何自保？更棘手的是，我们大多数时候并不想防范社会认同提供的信息。它提供的关于我们应该如何行动的证据通常是有效且有价值的。有了它，我们就能自信地做出无数决定，而无需亲自去调查每个决定的利弊。

In this sense, the principle of social proof equips us with a wonderful kind of automatic-pilot device not unlike that aboard most aircraft.

从这个意义上讲，社会认同原则为我们提供了一种奇妙的自动驾驶装置，与大多数飞机上的自动驾驶装置非常相似。

Yet there are occasional but real problems with automatic pilots. Those problems appear whenever the flight information locked into the control mechanism is wrong. In these instances, we will be taken off course. Depending on the size of the error, the consequences can be severe. But, because the automatic pilot afforded by the principle of social proof is more often an ally than an enemy, we can't be expected to want simply to disconnect it. Thus we are faced with a classic problem: how to make use of a piece of equipment that simultaneously benefits and imperils our welfare.

然而，自动驾驶系统偶尔也会出现一些实际存在的问题。这些问题会在控制系统中存储的飞行信息出现错误时出现。在这种情况下，我们会偏离航线。根据错误的大小，后果可能十分严重。但是，由于基于社会认同原则的自动驾驶系统通常是我们的盟友而非敌人，我们不能指望我们会想要直接将其断开。因此，我们面临着一个经典的难题：如何利用这件既能造福我们又能危害我们福祉的设备。

Fortunately, there is a way out of the dilemma. Because the disadvantages of automatic pilots arise principally when incorrect data have been put into the control system, our best defense against these disadvantages is to recognize when the data are in error. If we can become sensitive to situations where the social-proof automatic pilot is working with inaccurate information, we can disengage the mechanism and grasp the controls when we need to.

幸运的是，我们有办法摆脱这种困境。自动驾驶系统的缺点主要体现在控制系统输入了错误数据时，因此，应对这些缺点的最佳方法就是识别数据错误。如果我们能够敏锐地察觉到自动驾驶系统在处理不准确信息时的表现，我们就可以在必要时解除该机制，重新掌控飞机。

There are two types of situation in which incorrect data cause the principle of social proof to give us poor counsel. The first occurs when the social evidence has been purposely falsified. Invariably these situations are manufactured by exploiters intent on creating the impression —reality be damned—that a multitude is performing the way the exploiters want us to perform. The canned laughter of TV comedy shows, which we have already discussed, is one variety of faked data of this sort. But there is a great deal more; and much of the fakery is strikingly obvious.

有两种情况会导致错误数据使社会认同原则失效。第一种情况是社会证据被故意篡改。这种情况通常是由别有用心的人制造的，他们不顾现实，试图营造一种假象：大多数人都在按照他们的意愿行事。我们之前讨论过的电视喜剧节目中的罐头笑声就是这种伪造数据的一种。但伪造的数据远不止这些；而且很多伪造行为都显而易见。

For instance, canned responses are not unique to the electronic media or even to the electronic age. In fact, the heavy-handed exploitation of the principle of social proof can be traced through the history of one of our most venerable art forms: grand opera. This is the phenomenon called claquing, said to have been begun in 1820 by a pair of Paris opera-house habitués named Sauton and Porcher. The men were more than operagoers, though. They were businessmen whose product was applause.

例如，千篇一律的回应并非电子媒体或电子时代独有。事实上，对社会认同原则的滥用可以追溯到我们最古老的艺术形式之一：歌剧。这种现象被称为“拍手叫好”（claquing），据说起源于1820年，由两位巴黎歌剧院的常客索顿（Sauton）和波歇尔（Porcher）发起。然而，这两人不仅仅是歌剧观众，他们是商人，他们的产品就是掌声。

Organizing under the title L'Assurance des Succès Dramatiques, they leased themselves and their employees to singers and opera managers who wished to be assured of an appreciative audience response. So effective were they in stimulating genuine audience reaction with their rigged reactions that before long claques (usually consisting of a leader —chef de claque —and several individual claqueurs) had become an established and persistent tradition throughout the world of opera. As music historian Robert Sabin notes, "By 1830 the claque was a full-bloom institution, collecting by day, applauding by night, all in the honest open.... But it is altogether probable that neither Sauton, nor his ally Porcher, had a notion of the extent to which their scheme of paid applause would be adopted and applied wherever opera is sung."

他们以“戏剧成功保证”（L'Assurance des Succès Dramatiques）的名义组织起来，将自己和员工出租给那些希望确保获得观众好评的歌手和歌剧经理。他们通过人为操控的掌声来刺激观众的真实反应，效果显著，以至于不久之后，由一名领头人（chef de claque）和几名普通鼓掌者组成的“鼓掌团”（claque）便成为歌剧界一项根深蒂固的传统。正如音乐史学家罗伯特·萨宾所指出的那样，“到1830年，鼓掌团已发展成为一种成熟的制度，白天收取费用，晚上鼓掌，一切都公开透明……但索顿和他的盟友波歇尔很可能都没有预料到，他们这种付费鼓掌的模式会被如此广泛地采用，并应用于所有歌剧演出场所。”

As claquing grew and developed, its practitioners offered an array of styles and strengths. In the same way that laugh-track producers can hire individuals who excel in titters, chuckles, or belly laughs, the claques spawned their own specialists—the pleureuse, chosen for her ability to weep on cue; the bisseur, who called "bis" (repeat) and "encore" in ecstatic tones; and in direct kinship with today's laugh-track performer, the rieur , selected for the infectious quality of his laugh.

随着笑声表演的兴起和发展，表演者们展现出各具特色的风格和技能。就像罐头笑声制作人会聘请擅长轻笑、咯咯笑或开怀大笑的演员一样，笑声表演者也涌现出自己的专家——哭泣女（pleureuse），因其能按要求哭泣而被选中；吹口哨的（bisseur），以欣喜若狂的语气喊着“bis”（重复）和“encore”（安可）；以及与如今的罐头笑声表演者有着直接联系的，笑声感染力极强的（rieur）。

For our purposes, though, the most instructive parallel to modern forms of canned response is the conspicuous character of the fakery. No special need was seen to disguise or vary the claque, who often sat in the same seats, performance after performance, year after year, led by a chef de claque two decades into his position. Even the monetary transactions were not hidden from the public. Indeed, one hundred years after the birth of claquing, a reader of the London Musical Times could scan the advertised rates of the Italian claqueurs. Whether in the world of Rigoletto or Gilligan's Island, then, audiences have been successfully manipulated by those who use social evidence, even when that evidence has been openly falsified.

然而，就我们的目的而言，与现代罐头式回应形式最能说明问题的相似之处在于，这种造假行为的显眼特征。观众席上的“捧场者”（claque）似乎无需刻意伪装或更换，他们往往年复一年、一场接一场地坐在相同的位置上，由一位担任“捧场者”长达二十年的领队带领。就连金钱交易也毫不隐瞒。事实上，在“捧场者”这一现象诞生一百年后，《伦敦音乐时报》的读者仍然可以查阅到意大利捧场者的广告价格。因此，无论是在《弄臣》的世界里，还是在《吉利根岛》的世界里，那些利用社会证据的人都成功地操纵了观众，即便这些证据已被公开伪造。

Wild enthusiasm—A special sum to be arranged

热情高涨——一笔待定款项

FIGURE 4-5 Advertised Rates of the Italian Claque

图 4-5 意大利克拉克瓷器的广告价格

From "ordinary applause" to "wild enthusiasm," claqueurs offered their services in an audaciously public fashion—in this case, in a newspaper read by many of the audience members they fully expected to influence. Claque, whirr.

从“普通的掌声”到“狂热的热情”，拉票员们以一种大胆公开的方式招揽生意——在这种情况下，他们是在一份报纸上刊登广告，他们完全希望能够影响到许多听众。拉票员，嗡嗡作响。

What Sauton and Porcher realized about the mechanical way that we abide by the principle of social proof is understood as well by a variety of today's exploiters. They see no need to hide the manufactured nature of the social evidence they provide—witness the amateurish quality of the average TV laugh track. They seem almost smug in the recognition of our predicament: Either we must allow them to fool us or we must abandon the precious automatic pilots that make us so vulnerable to their tricks. But in their certainty that they have us trapped, such exploiters have made a crucial mistake. The laxity with which they construct phony social evidence gives us a way to fight back.

索顿和波切尔意识到我们机械地遵循社会认同原则，而当今许多剥削者也深谙此道。他们毫不掩饰自己提供的社会证据的虚假本质——看看电视上那些业余的罐头笑声就知道了。他们似乎沾沾自喜地意识到我们的困境：要么我们任由他们愚弄，要么我们就得放弃那些让我们如此容易上当受骗的“自动驾驶”机制。然而，这些剥削者自以为已经将我们牢牢控制，却犯了一个致命的错误。他们炮制虚假社会证据的松懈，反而给了我们反击的机会。

Because automatic pilots can be engaged and disengaged at will, we can cruise along trusting in the course steered by the principle of social proof until we recognize that a piece of inaccurate data is being used. Then we can take the controls, make the necessary correction for the misinformation, and reset the automatic pilot. The transparency of the rigged social proof we get these days provides us with exactly the cue we need for knowing when to perform this simple maneuver. With no more cost than a bit of vigilance for plainly counterfeit social evidence, then, we can protect ourselves nicely.

由于自动驾驶系统可以随时启用和禁用，我们可以依靠社会认同原则的指引一路前行，直到发现使用了不准确的数据。这时，我们可以接管控制权，纠正错误信息，并重置自动驾驶系统。如今，人为操纵的社会认同如此透明，恰恰为我们提供了何时进行这一简单操作所需的线索。因此，我们只需稍加警惕，留意那些明显伪造的社会证据，就能有效地保护自己。

Let's take an example. A bit earlier, we noted the proliferation of av-erage-person-on-the-street ads, in which a number of ordinary people speak glowingly of a product, often without knowing that their words are being recorded. As would be expected according to the principle of social proof, these testimonials from "average people like you and me" make for quite effective advertising campaigns. They have always included one relatively subtle kind of distortion: We hear only from those who like the product; as a result, we get an understandably biased picture of the amount of social support for it. More recently, though, a cruder and more unethical sort of falsification has been introduced. Commercial producers often don't bother to get genuine testimonials. They merely hire actors to play the roles of average people testifying in an unrehearsed fashion to an interviewer. It is amazing how baldfaced these "unrehearsed interview" commercials can be. The situations are obviously staged, the participants are clearly actors, and the dialogue is unmistakably prewritten.

我们举个例子。之前我们提到过，街头路人广告泛滥成灾，许多普通人热情洋溢地谈论某个产品，而他们往往并不知道自己的话被录了下来。正如社会认同原则所预期的那样，这些来自“像你我一样的普通人”的证言确实能带来相当有效的广告效果。它们一直都包含一种相对隐蔽的扭曲：我们听到的只是那些喜欢该产品的人的评价；因此，我们对该产品的社会支持度的认知必然存在偏差。然而，最近出现了一种更粗暴、更不道德的造假手段。商业广告制作人往往懒得去收集真实的证言，他们只是雇佣演员扮演普通人，让他们未经排练地接受采访。这些“未经排练的采访”广告的拙劣程度令人瞠目结舌。这些情境显然是事先安排好的，参与者显然是演员，对话也毫无疑问是预先写好的。

Dave Barry

戴夫·巴里

Knight Ridder News Service

骑士里德新闻服务

Recently I was watching TV, and a commercial came on, and the announcer, in a tone of voice usually reserved for major developments in the Persian Gulf, said, "Now consumers can ask Angela Lansbury their questions about Bufferin!"

最近我在看电视，突然插播了一条广告，播音员用一种通常只有在波斯湾发生重大事件时才会使用的语气说道：“现在消费者可以向安吉拉·兰斯伯瑞询问有关 Bufferin 的问题了！”

As a normal human, the natural reaction to this announcement is: "Huh?" Meaning: "What does Angela Lansbury have to do with Bufferin?" But this commercial featured several consumers who had apparently been stopped at random on the street, and every one of them had a question for Angela Lansbury about Bufferin. Basically, what they asked was, "Miss Lansbury, is Bufferin a good product that I should purchase, or what?"

作为普通人，听到这个广告的第一反应可能是：“啊？”意思是：“安吉拉·兰斯伯瑞跟百洁布有什么关系？”但这则广告里，几位消费者似乎是在街上被随机拦下，每个人都向安吉拉·兰斯伯瑞提出了一个关于百洁布的问题。基本上，他们问的是：“兰斯伯瑞小姐，百洁布到底好不好用，值得买吗？”

These consumers seemed very earnest. It was as if they had been going around for months wringing their hands and saying, "I have a question about Bufferin! If only I could ask Angela Lansbury!"

这些消费者看起来非常认真。就好像他们几个月来一直在焦急地四处奔走，焦急地说：“我有个关于 Bufferin 的问题！要是能问问安吉拉·兰斯伯瑞就好了！”

What we are seeing here is yet another example of a worsening problem that has been swept under the rug for too long in this nation: The invasion of Consumers From Mars. The look like humans, but they don't act like humans, and they are taking over.

我们现在看到的，是这个国家长期以来一直被掩盖的、日益恶化的问题的又一个例证：来自火星的消费者入侵。他们外表像人类，但行为举止却不像人类，而且他们正在接管一切。

图 4-6 街上的普通火星人

Apparently I am not alone in noticing the number of blatantly phony "unrehearsed "

显然，注意到大量明显虚假的“未经彩排”表演的人并非只有我一人。

testimonial ads these days. Humorist Dave Barry has registered their prevalence too

如今，证言广告层出不穷。幽默作家戴夫·巴里也注意到了这种广告的盛行。

and has labeled their inhabitants Consumers From Mars, which is a term I like

并将他们的居民称为“火星消费者”，我很喜欢这个称呼。

and have even begun using myself. It helps remind me that, as regards my buying

我自己也开始用了。它提醒我，就我的购买而言，

habits, I should be sure to ignore the tastes of these individuals who, after all, come

习惯方面，我应该尽量忽略这些人的喜好，毕竟，他们是……

from another planet than me.

他来自另一个星球。

(KNIGHT RIDDER NEWS SERVICE)

（骑士新闻社）

I know that whenever I encounter an influence attempt of this sort, it sets off in me a kind of alarm with a clear directive: Attention! Attention! Bad social proof in this situation. Temporarily disconnect automatic pilot. It's so easy to do. We need only make a conscious decision to be alert to counterfeit social evidence, and the smug overconfidence of the exploiters will play directly into our hands. We can relax until their manifest fakery is spotted, at which time we can pounce.

我知道，每当我遇到这类试图影响他人的行为时，我的内心都会响起一种警报，并收到一条明确的指令：注意！注意！这种情况下的社交认同是错误的。暂时关闭自动驾驶模式。这很容易做到。我们只需要有意识地决定对伪造的社交证据保持警惕，那些利用他人的人的自鸣得意就会正中我们的下怀。我们可以放松警惕，直到他们的拙劣伎俩被识破，然后我们就可以出手反击。

And we should pounce with a vengeance. I am speaking here of more than simply ignoring the misinformation, although this defensive tactic is certainly called for. I am speaking of aggressive counterattack. Whenever possible we ought to sting those responsible for the rigging of social evidence. We should purchase no products featured in phony "unrehearsed interview" commercials. Moreover, each manufacturer of the items should receive a letter explaining our response and recommending that they discontinue use of the advertising agency that produced so deceptive a presentation of their product.

我们应该采取强硬措施予以反击。我指的不仅仅是无视虚假信息，尽管这种防御策略固然必要。我指的是积极的反击。我们应该尽可能地打击那些操纵社会证据的人。我们不应该购买任何在虚假的“未经彩排的采访”广告中出现的商品。此外，我们应该给每家此类商品的生产商写一封信，解释我们的应对措施，并建议他们停止与制作如此具有欺骗性产品宣传的广告公司合作。

Of course, we don't always want to trust the actions of others to direct our conduct—especially in a situation important enough to warrant our personal investigation of the pros and cons, or in which we are ex-perts—but we do want to be able to count on others' behavior as a source of valid information in a large array of settings. If, in such settings, we find that we cannot trust the information to be valid because someone has tampered with the evidence, we ought to be ready to strike back. In such instances, I personally feel driven by more than the aversion to being duped. I bristle at the thought of being pushed into an unacceptable corner by those who would undermine one of my hedges against the decisional overload of modern life. And I get a genuine sense of righteousness by lashing out when they try. If you are like me, so should you.

当然，我们并非总是希望依赖他人的行为来指导自己的决策——尤其是在需要我们亲自权衡利弊的重要情况下，或者在我们自身是专家的情况下——但我们确实希望在各种情况下都能将他人的行为视为有效信息的来源。如果在这些情况下，我们发现信息的真实性无法保证，因为有人篡改了证据，我们就应该做好反击的准备。在这种情况下，我个人感到的动力不仅仅是害怕被欺骗。我一想到有人会试图破坏我应对现代生活决策过载的防御机制，就感到愤怒，仿佛自己被逼到了绝境。当他们试图这样做时，我的反击会让我感到一种真正的正义感。如果你也和我一样，你也应该如此。

In addition to the times when social evidence is deliberately faked, there is another time when the principle of social proof will regularly steer us wrong. In such an instance, an innocent, natural error will produce snowballing social proof that pushes us to the incorrect decision. The pluralist ignorance phenomenon, in which everyone at an emergency sees no cause for alarm, is one example of this process. The best illustration I know, however, comes from a story of one of my students, who was a highway patrolman.

除了故意伪造社会证据的情况之外，还有一种情况是社会认同原则会经常误导我们。在这种情况下，一个无意的、自然的错误会产生滚雪球式的社会认同，最终导致我们做出错误的决定。多元无知现象就是一个例子，在这种现象中，所有人在紧急情况下都认为无需担忧。然而，我所知的最佳例证来自我的一位学生的故事，他曾是一名公路巡警。

After a class session in which the subject of discussion was the principle of social proof, he stayed to talk with me. He said that he now understood the cause of a type of traffic accident that had always puzzled him before. The accident typically occurred on the city freeway during rush hour, when cars in all lanes were moving steadily but slowly. Events leading to the accident would start when a pair of cars, one behind the other, would simultaneously begin signaling an intention to get out of the lane they were in and into the next. Within seconds, a long line of drivers to the rear of the first two would follow suit, thinking that something—a stalled car or a construction barrier—was blocking the lane ahead. It would be in this crush to cram into the available spaces of the next lane that a collision frequently happened.

在一次关于社会认同原理的课堂讨论结束后，他留下来和我聊天。他说他现在明白了一种一直困扰他的交通事故的成因了。这种事故通常发生在高峰时段的城市高速公路上，那时所有车道的车辆都在缓慢但平稳地行驶。事故的起因是，前后两辆车同时打转向灯，表示要驶出当前车道，进入相邻车道。几秒钟之内，后面一长串的司机也会跟着做，他们以为前面的车道被什么东西挡住了——比如抛锚的车辆或施工路障。正是在这种争先恐后地挤进相邻车道的拥挤过程中，碰撞事故经常发生。

The odd thing about it all, according to the patrolman, was that very often there had been no obstruction to be avoided in the first place, and by the time of the accident, this should have been obvious to anyone who looked. He said he had more than once witnessed such accidents when there was a visibly clear road in front of the ill-fated lane switchers.

据巡警说，最奇怪的是，很多时候根本没有需要避让的障碍物，到了事故发生的时候，任何稍加留意的人都应该能清楚地看到这一点。他说，他不止一次目睹过类似的事故，当时那些不幸变道的人面前明明是一条畅通无阻的道路。

The patrolman's account provides certain insights into the way we respond to social proof. First, we seem to assume that if a lot of people are doing the same thing, they must know something we don't. Especially when we are uncertain, we are willing to place an enormous amount of trust in the collective knowledge of the crowd. Second, quite frequently the crowd is mistaken because they are not acting on the basis of any superior information but are reacting, themselves, to the principle of social proof.

巡警的叙述揭示了我们如何应对社会认同的一些问题。首先，我们似乎会认为，如果很多人都在做同样的事情，那他们肯定知道一些我们不知道的事情。尤其是在我们感到不确定的时候，我们更愿意对群体的集体智慧寄予厚望。其次，群体经常会犯错，因为他们的行动并非基于任何更权威的信息，而是出于自身对社会认同原则的反应。

So if a pair of freeway drivers decided by coincidence to change lanes at the identical moment, the next two drivers might well do the same, assuming that the forward drivers had spotted an obstruction. The resulting social evidence confronting drivers behind this group would be potent—four successive cars, all with their turn signals flashing, trying to angle into the next lane. More signal lights would go on. The social proof would be undeniable by then. For drivers to the rear, there could be no question about the correctness of switching lanes: "All those guys ahead must know something." So intent would they be upon working themselves into the next lane that, without even checking the true condition of the road before them, the drivers would begin a line-long flank assault. Crash.

因此，如果两名高速公路司机碰巧同时决定变道，那么后面的两名司机很可能也会效仿，因为他们认为前面的司机发现了障碍物。这样一来，后面的司机就会看到强烈的社会证据——四辆车依次闪着转向灯，试图斜着变入相邻车道。更多的转向灯会亮起。到那时，这种社会证据将无可辩驳。对于后面的司机来说，变道的正确性毋庸置疑：“前面那些人肯定知道些什么。”他们会一心想变入相邻车道，甚至不去查看前方路况，就开始从侧面发起长龙式的进攻。结果就是撞车。

There is a lesson here: An automatic-pilot device, like social proof, should never be trusted fully; even when no saboteur has fed bad information into the mechanism, it can sometimes go haywire by itself. We need to check the machine from time to time to be sure that it hasn't worked itself out of sync with the other sources of evidence in the situation—the objective facts, our prior experiences, our own judgments. Fortunately, this precaution requires neither much effort nor much time. A quick glance around is all that is needed. And this little precaution is well worth it. The consequences of single-minded reliance on social evidence can be frightening.

这里蕴含着一个教训：像社会认同这样的自动驾驶机制永远不应被完全信任；即使没有人故意向其输入错误信息，它有时也会自行失灵。我们需要时不时地检查一下这台机器，确保它没有与其他证据来源——客观事实、我们过往的经验以及我们自身的判断——脱节。幸运的是，这种预防措施既不需要花费太多精力，也不需要花费太多时间。只需快速环顾四周即可。而这种小小的预防措施却非常值得。一味依赖社会认同的后果可能不堪设想。

This aspect of the social proof phenomenon always reminds me of the way certain Indian tribes—the Blackfeet, Cree, Snake, and Crow—used to hunt the North American buffalo. There are two features of buffalo that make them especially susceptible to erroneous social evidence. First, their eyes are set in their heads so that it is easier for them to see to the side than to the front. Second, when they run, as in a stampede, it is with their heads down low so they cannot see above the herd. As a result, the Indians realized, it was possible to kill tremendous numbers of buffalo by starting a herd running toward a cliff. The animals, responding to the thundering social proof around them—and never looking up to see what lay ahead—did the rest. One astonished observer to such a hunt described the deadly outcome of the buffalo's obsessive trust in collective knowledge.

社会认同现象的这一方面总是让我想起某些印第安部落——黑脚族、克里族、斯内克族和克罗族——过去猎杀北美野牛的方式。野牛有两个特点使它们特别容易受到错误的社会认同的影响。首先，它们的眼睛长在头部，因此更容易看到侧面而不是前方。其次，当它们奔跑时，比如在牛群奔腾时，它们的头会低垂，所以看不到牛群上方的情况。因此，印第安人发现，只要让一群野牛朝着悬崖奔跑，就能杀死大量的野牛。这些动物会响应周围震耳欲聋的社会认同——从不抬头看前方的情况——完成剩下的事情。一位目睹过这种狩猎的观察者震惊地描述了野牛对集体智慧的盲目信任所造成的致命后果。

In this way, it was possible to decoy a herd toward a precipice, and cause it to plunge over en masse, the leaders being thrust overby their followers and all the rest following of their own free will.
这样，就可以诱使一群动物走向悬崖，使它们集体坠落，领头的动物被它们的追随者推下去，其余的动物则出于自愿跟随下去。

Certainly, a flier whose plane is locked onto automatic pilot would be wise to glance occasionally at the instrument panel and out the window. In the same way, we need to look up and around periodically whenever we are locked onto the evidence of the crowd. Without this simple safeguard against misguided social proof, our prospects might well run parallel to those of the freeway lane switchers and the North American buffalo: Crash.

当然，如果飞机开启自动驾驶模式，飞行员最好时不时地瞥一眼仪表盘和窗外。同样，当我们过于关注人群的言行举止时，也需要时不时地抬头看看周围。如果没有这种简单的防范措施，避免被误导性的社会认同所左右，我们的命运很可能与高速公路上的随意变道者和北美野牛一样：坠毁。

READER'S REPORT

读者报告

From a Former Racetrack Employee

一位前赛马场员工的自述

"I became aware of one method of faking social evidence to one's advantage while working at a racetrack. In order to lower the odds and make more money, some bettors are able to sway the public to bet on bad horses.

“我在赛马场工作时，发现了一种利用伪造社会证据来谋取私利的方法。为了降低赔率、赚取更多利润，一些赌徒会设法影响公众，让他们押注于劣马。”

"Odds at a racetrack are based on where the money is being bet. The more money on a horse, the lower (better) the odds. Many people who play the horses have surprisingly little knowledge of racing or betting strategy. Thus, especially when they don't know much about the horses in a particular race, a lot of times they'll simply bet the favorite. Because tote boards are displayed with up-to-the-minute odds, the public can always tell who the current favorite is. The system that a high roller can use to alter the odds is actually quite simple. The guy has in mind a horse he feels has a good chance of winning. Next he chooses a horse that has long odds (say, 15 to 1) and doesn't have a realistic chance to win. The minute the mutual windows open, the guy puts down a hundred dollars on the inferior horse, creating an instant favorite whose odds on the board drop to about 2 to 1.

赛马场的赔率取决于投注金额的分布。投注金额越大，赔率就越低（越好）。许多赛马爱好者对赛马或投注策略的了解少得惊人。因此，尤其是在对特定比赛中的马匹不太了解的情况下，他们往往会直接投注热门马匹。由于投注板上会实时显示赔率，公众总能知道当前的热门马匹是谁。豪赌客用来操纵赔率的方法其实很简单。他心中已经有了一匹他认为很有可能获胜的马。接下来，他选择一匹赔率很高（比如15比1）且获胜几率很小的马。一旦投注窗口打开，他就在这匹赔率较低的马身上下注一百美元，从而瞬间将其变成热门马，赔率降至2比1左右。

"Now the elements of social proof begin to work. People who are uncertain of how to bet the race look to the tote board to see which horse the early bettors have decided is a favorite, and they follow. A snowballing effect now occurs as other people continue to bet the favorite. At this point, the high roller can go back to the window and bet heavily on his true favorite, which will have better odds now because the 'new favorite' has pushed down the board. If the guy wins, the initial hundred-dollar investment will have been worth it many times over. "I've seen this happen myself. I remember one time a person put down a hundred dollars on a prerace 10-to-1 shot, making it the early favorite. The rumors started circulating around the track—people knew something. Next thing you know, everyone (me included) was betting on this horse. It ended up running last and had a bad leg. Many people lost a lot of money. Somebody came out ahead though. We'll never know who. But he is the one with all the money. He understood the theory of social proof."

“现在，社会认同效应开始发挥作用了。那些不确定如何下注的人会查看赔率板，看看早期下注者都把哪匹马列为热门，然后他们也跟着下注。随着其他人继续下注热门马，这就产生了滚雪球效应。这时，豪赌客就可以回到投注窗口，重注自己真正心仪的马匹，因为“新热门”的赔率下降了，这匹马的赔率现在更高了。如果他赢了，最初那一百美元的投资就会获得数倍的回报。“我亲眼见过这种情况。我记得有一次，有人在一匹赛前赔率为10比1的冷门马匹上下了100美元，使它成为早期热门。赛场上开始流传各种消息——人们都知道些什么。接下来，几乎所有人都在下注这匹马（包括我）。结果它跑得垫底，而且腿伤了。很多人损失惨重。不过，有人从中获利。我们永远不会知道是谁。但他是那个拥有所有钱的人。”他理解社会认同理论。

Once again we can see that social proof is most powerful for those who feel unfamiliar or unsure in a specific situation and who, consequently, must look outside of themselves for evidence of how best to behave there.

我们再次看到，社会认同对于那些在特定情况下感到不熟悉或不确定的人来说最为有效，因此，他们必须向外寻求证据，才能知道在这种情况下如何最好地行事。

# ↩

Chapter 5 - LIKING

第五章——喜欢

The Friendly Thief

友善的小偷

The main work of a trial attorney is to make a jury like his client.
出庭律师的主要工作是让陪审团喜欢他的委托人。
— C LARENCE D ARROW
——克拉伦斯·达罗

FEW PEOPLE WOULD BE SURPRISED TO LEARN THAT, AS A RULE, we most prefer to say yes to the requests of someone we know and like. What might be startling to note, however, is that this simple rule is used in hundreds of ways by total strangers to get us to comply with their requests.

很少有人会惊讶地发现，通常情况下，我们更倾向于答应认识且喜欢的人的请求。然而，令人惊讶的是，完全陌生的人会用数百种方式利用这条简单的规则来让我们答应他们的请求。

The clearest illustration I know of the professional exploitation of the liking rule is the Tupperware party, which I consider the quintessential American compliance setting. Anybody familiar with the workings of a Tupperware party will recognize the use of the various weapons of influence we have examined so far: reciprocity (to start, games are played and prizes won by the partygoers; anyone who doesn't win a prize gets to reach into a grab bag for hers so that everyone has received a gift before the buying begins), commitment (each participant is urged to describe publicly the uses and benefits she has found in the Tupper-ware she already owns), and social proof (once the buying begins, each purchase builds the idea that other, similar people want the product; therefore, it must be good).

我所知的对“喜好法则”进行专业利用的最清晰例证就是特百惠派对，我认为这是美国式顺从行为的典型案例。任何熟悉特百惠派对运作方式的人都会认出其中运用了我们目前为止探讨过的各种影响力手段：互惠（派对开始时会玩游戏并颁发奖品；任何没有中奖的人都可以从礼品袋中挑选自己的奖品，这样每个人在开始购买之前都能收到一份礼物）、承诺（鼓励每位参与者公开描述她已拥有的特百惠产品的用途和好处）以及社会认同（一旦开始购买，每一次购买都会强化这样一种观念：其他类似的人也想要这款产品；因此，它一定很好）。

All the major weapons of influence are present to help things along, but the real power of the Tupperware party comes from a particular arrangement that trades on the liking rule. Despite the entertaining and persuasive salesmanship of the Tupperware demonstrator, the true request to purchase the product does not come from this stranger; it comes from a friend to every woman in the room. Oh, the Tupperware representative may physically ask for each partygoer's order, all right, but the more psychologically compelling requester is a housewife sitting off to the side, smiling, chatting, and serving refreshments. She is the party hostess, who has called her friends together for the demonstration in her home and who, everyone knows, makes a profit from each piece sold at her party.

所有主要的营销手段都已到位，但特百惠派对真正的威力却源于一种特殊的安排，即利用“好感法则”。尽管特百惠的演示员风趣幽默、极具说服力，但真正促成购买的并非这位陌生人，而是房间里每位女性的“朋友”。当然，特百惠的代表或许会亲自询问每位宾客的订单，但真正更具心理说服力的，是一位坐在一旁，面带微笑、与人聊天、并准备茶点的家庭主妇。她就是派对的女主人，邀请朋友们到家中参加产品演示，而人人都知道，派对上每售出一件产品，她都能从中获利。

Simple. By providing the hostess with a percentage of the take, the Tupperware Home Parties Corporation arranges for its customers to buy from and for a friend rather than an unknown salesperson. In this way, the attraction, the warmth, the security, and the obligation of friendship are brought to bear on the sales setting. Consumer researchers Frenzer and Davis, who have examined the social ties between the hostess and the partygoers in home-party sales settings, have affirmed the power of the company's approach: The strength of that social bond is twice as likely to determine product purchase as is preference for the product itself. The results have been remarkable. It was recently estimated that Tupperware sales exceed $2.5 million a day!

很简单。特百惠家庭聚会公司通过向女主人支付一定比例的销售额，让顾客从朋友那里购买产品，而不是从陌生的销售员那里购买。这样一来，友谊的吸引力、温暖、安全感和义务感就融入了销售场景。消费者研究员弗伦泽和戴维斯研究了家庭聚会销售场景中女主人和参加者之间的社交关系，证实了该公司这种模式的有效性：这种社交关系的强度对产品购买的影响是产品本身偏好的两倍。结果令人瞩目。据最近估计，特百惠的日销售额超过250万美元！

What is interesting is that the customers appear to be fully aware of the liking and friendship pressures embodied in the Tupperware party. Some don't seem to mind; others do, but don't seem to know how to avoid them. One woman I spoke with described her reactions with more than a bit of frustration in her voice:

有趣的是，顾客们似乎完全意识到特百惠聚会中蕴含的讨好和交友压力。有些人似乎并不介意；有些人介意，但似乎不知道如何避免。我采访的一位女士在描述她的反应时，语气中带着明显的无奈：

It's gotten to the point now where I hate to be invited to Tupperware parties. I've got all the containers I need; and if I wanted any more, I could buy another brand cheaper in the store. But when a friend calls up, I feel like I have to go. And when I get there, I feel like I have to buy something. What can I do? It's for one of my friends.
现在我已经到了讨厌被邀请参加特百惠聚会的地步了。我需要的保鲜盒都够用了；如果想要更多，我可以去商店买其他更便宜的牌子。但当朋友打电话来的时候，我感觉自己不得不去。到了那里，我又感觉自己不得不买点东西。我能怎么办呢？这是帮朋友买的。

With so irresistible an ally as the friendship principle operating, it is little wonder that the company has abandoned retail sales outlets and has pushed the home party concept until a Tupperware party now starts somewhere every 2.7 seconds. But, of course, all sorts of other compliance professionals recognize the pressure to say yes to someone we know and like. Take, for instance, the growing number of charity organizations that recruit volunteers to canvass for donations close to their own homes. They understand perfectly how much more difficult it is for us to turn down a charity request when it comes from a friend or a neighbor.

有了友谊原则这样强大的助力，难怪该公司放弃了零售门店，转而大力推广家庭聚会模式，如今每2.7秒就有一场特百惠聚会在某个地方拉开帷幕。当然，其他各种合规专业人士也意识到，面对熟人或邻居的请求，我们往往难以拒绝。例如，越来越多的慈善机构招募志愿者在自家附近募捐。他们深知，当慈善请求来自朋友或邻居时，我们拒绝起来有多么困难。

Other compliance professionals have found that the friend doesn't even have to be present to be effective; often, just the mention of the friend's name is enough. The Shaklee Corporation, which specializes in door-to-door sales of various home-related products, advises its salespeople to use the "endless chain" method for finding new customers. Once a customer admits to liking a product, he or she can be pressed for the names of friends who would also appreciate learning about it. The individuals on that list can then be approached for sales and a list of their friends, who can serve as sources for still other potential customers, and so on in an endless chain.

其他合规专家发现，朋友甚至不必在场就能起到作用；通常，仅仅提及朋友的名字就足够了。专门从事各种家居用品上门销售的嘉康利公司建议其销售人员使用“无限链”法寻找新客户。一旦客户表示喜欢某个产品，就可以询问他们有哪些朋友也想了解该产品。然后，可以联系名单上的这些人进行销售，并获取他们的朋友名单，这些朋友又可以成为其他潜在客户的来源，如此循环往复，形成一个无限链。

The key to the success of this method is that each new prospect is visited by a salesperson armed with the name of a friend "who suggested I call on you." Turning the salesperson away under those circumstances is difficult; it's almost like rejecting the friend. The Shaklee sales manual insists that employees use this system without fail: "It would be impossible to overestimate its value. Phoning or calling on a prospect and being able to say that Mr. So-and-so, a friend of his, felt he would benefit by giving you a few moments of his time is virtually as good as a sale 50 percent made before you enter."

这种方法成功的关键在于，每位新客户都会由一位销售人员拜访，而这位销售人员会事先告知客户某位朋友的姓名，并表示“他建议我来拜访您”。在这种情况下拒绝销售人员几乎是不可能的，这几乎等同于拒绝这位朋友。嘉康利销售手册坚持要求员工必须使用这套系统：“它的价值怎么强调都不为过。打电话或拜访客户，并告诉客户某某先生，他的朋友觉得抽出几分钟时间与您交流会对您有所帮助，这几乎相当于在您进门之前就已经完成了50%的销售。”

The widespread use by compliance practitioners of the liking bond between friends tells us much about the power of the liking rule to produce assent. In fact, we find that such professionals seek to benefit from the rule even when already formed friendships are not present for them to employ. Under these circumstances, the professionals' compliance strategy is quite direct: They first get us to like them.

合规从业者广泛利用朋友间的好感关系，这充分说明了好感规则在获取认同方面的强大力量。事实上，我们发现，即使没有现成的友谊可供利用，这些专业人士也会试图从中获益。在这种情况下，他们的合规策略非常直接：首先，他们要赢得我们的好感。

There is a man in Detroit, Joe Girard, who specialized in using the liking rule to sell Chevrolets. He became wealthy in the process, making more than two hundred thousand dollars a year. With such a salary, we might guess that he was a high-level GM executive or perhaps the owner of a Chevrolet dealership. But no. He made his money as a salesman on the showroom floor. At what he did, he was phenomenal. For twelve years straight, he won the title as the "number one car salesman"; he averaged more than five cars and trucks sold every day he worked; and he has been called the world's "greatest car salesman" by the Guinness Book of World Records.

在底特律，有一位名叫乔·吉拉德的销售员，他擅长运用“喜好法则”推销雪佛兰汽车。他因此积累了巨额财富，年收入超过二十万美元。如此丰厚的收入，我们或许会以为他是通用汽车的高管，或者是一家雪佛兰经销店的老板。然而并非如此。他靠在展厅里做销售员赚到了这些钱。他的销售业绩堪称惊人。他连续十二年蝉联“最佳汽车销售员”的称号；平均每天售出五辆以上的汽车和卡车；吉尼斯世界纪录更是将他誉为“世界最伟大的汽车销售员”。

For all his success, the formula he employed was surprisingly simple. It consisted of offering people just two things: a fair price and someone they liked to buy from. "And that's it," he claimed in an interview. "Finding the salesman they like, plus the price; put them both together, and you get a deal."

尽管他取得了巨大的成功，但他采用的模式却出奇地简单。这套模式只包含两点：合理的价格和他们喜欢的销售人员。“就是这样，”他在一次采访中说道，“找到他们喜欢的销售人员，再加上合理的价格；把这两点结合起来，你就达成了一笔交易。”

Fine. The Joe Girard formula tells us how vital the liking rule is to his business, but it doesn't tell us nearly enough. For one thing, it doesn't tell us why customers liked him more than some other salesperson who offered a fair price. There is a crucial—and fascinating—general question that Joe's formula leaves unanswered: What are the factors that cause one person to like another person? If we knew that answer, we would be a long way toward understanding how people such as Joe can so successfully arrange to have us like them and, conversely, how we might successfully arrange to have others like us. Fortunately, social scientists have been asking the question for decades. Their accumulated evidence has allowed them to identify a number of factors that reliably cause liking. And, as we will see, each is cleverly used by compliance professionals to urge us along the road to "yes."

很好。乔·吉拉德公式告诉我们，好感法则对他的生意有多么重要，但这还远远不够。首先，它没有解释为什么顾客更喜欢他，而不是其他报价合理的销售员。乔的公式遗漏了一个至关重要且引人入胜的普遍性问题：是什么因素导致一个人喜欢另一个人？如果我们知道答案，就能更好地理解像乔这样的人是如何成功地让我们喜欢他们的，反之亦然，我们又该如何成功地让别人喜欢我们。幸运的是，社会科学家们几十年来一直在研究这个问题。他们积累的证据使他们能够识别出许多可靠的影响好感的因素。而且，正如我们将看到的，合规专家巧妙地利用了这些因素，引导我们走向“同意”的道路。

Physical Attractiveness

外貌吸引力

Although it is generally acknowledged that good-looking people have an advantage in social interaction, recent findings indicate that we may have sorely underestimated the size and reach of that advantage. There seems to be a click, whirr response to attractive people. Like all click, whirr reactions, it happens automatically, without forethought. The response itself falls into a category that social scientists call "halo effects." A halo effect occurs when one positive characteristic of a person dominates the way that person is viewed by others. And the evidence is now clear that physical attractiveness is often such a characteristic.

虽然人们普遍认为外貌出众的人在社交互动中具有优势，但最近的研究表明，我们可能严重低估了这种优势的规模和影响范围。人们似乎会对长相吸引人的人产生一种“心动”的反应。就像所有“心动”反应一样，这种反应是自动发生的，无需事先思考。这种反应本身属于社会科学家所说的“光环效应”。光环效应指的是，一个人的某个积极特征主导了他人对其的看法。而现在的证据表明，外貌吸引力往往就是这样一种特征。

Research has shown that we automatically assign to good-looking individuals such favorable traits as talent, kindness, honesty, and intelligence. Furthermore, we make these judgments without being aware that physical attractiveness plays a role in the process. Certain of the consequences of this unconscious assumption that "good-looking equals good" scare me. For example, a study of the Canadian federal elections found that attractive candidates received more than two and a half times as many votes as unattractive candidates. Despite such evidence of favoritism toward handsome politicians, follow-up research demonstrated that voters do not realize their bias. In fact, 73 percent of Canadian voters surveyed denied in the strongest possible terms that their votes had been influenced by physical appearance; only 14 percent even allowed for the possibility of such influence. A similar effect has been found in hiring situations. In one study, good grooming of applicants in a simulated employment interview accounted for more favorable hiring decisions than did job qualifications—this, even though the interviewers claimed that appearance played a small role in their choices.

研究表明，我们往往会不自觉地将才华、善良、诚实和智慧等优良品质赋予外表出众的人。此外，我们在做出这些判断时，并未意识到外貌吸引力在其中发挥了作用。这种“长得好看就等于好”的无意识假设所带来的某些后果令我感到担忧。例如，一项针对加拿大联邦选举的研究发现，外貌出众的候选人获得的选票是相貌平平的候选人的两倍半以上。尽管有证据表明选民偏爱英俊的政治人物，但后续研究表明，选民并未意识到这种偏见。事实上，73%的受访加拿大选民以最强烈的措辞否认他们的投票受到外貌的影响；只有14%的人甚至认为这种可能性存在。类似的现象也出现在招聘中。一项研究发现，在模拟面试中，应聘者良好的仪容仪表比工作资格更能促成录用决定——尽管面试官声称外貌在他们的选择中只起到了很小的作用。

Equally unsettling research indicates that our judicial process is similarly susceptible to the influences of body dimensions and bone structure. Good-looking people are likely to receive highly favorable treatment in the legal system. For example, in a Pennsylvania study, researchers rated the physical attractiveness of seventy-four separate male defendants at the start of their criminal trials. When, much later, the researchers checked court records for the results of these cases, they found that the handsome men had received significantly lighter sentences. In fact, the attractive defendants were twice as likely to avoid jail as the unattractive ones. In another study—this one on the damages awarded in a staged negligence trial—a defendant who was better-looking than his victim was assessed an average amount of $5,623; but when the victim was the more attractive of the two, the average compensation was $10,051. What's more, both male and female jurors exhibited the attractiveness-based favoritism.

同样令人不安的研究表明，我们的司法程序也同样容易受到体型和骨骼结构的影响。相貌出众的人在法律体系中往往能获得极大的优待。例如，宾夕法尼亚州的一项研究在74名男性被告的刑事审判开始时，对他们的外貌吸引力进行了评分。多年后，当研究人员查阅这些案件的法庭记录时，发现那些相貌英俊的被告所受的刑罚明显更轻。事实上，相貌出众的被告免于牢狱之灾的可能性是相貌平平的被告的两倍。在另一项关于模拟过失诉讼中赔偿金额的研究中，一名相貌优于受害者的被告平均被判赔偿5623美元；而当受害者相貌优于被告时，平均赔偿金额则高达10051美元。更令人担忧的是，男性和女性陪审员都表现出了这种基于外貌的偏袒行为。

Other experiments have demonstrated that attractive people are more likely to obtain help when in need and are more persuasive in changing the opinions of an audience. Here, too, both sexes respond in the same way. In the helping study, for instance, the better-looking men and women received aid more often, even from members of their own sex. A major exception to this rule might be expected to occur, of course, if the attractive person is viewed as a direct competitor, especially a romantic rival. Short of this qualification, though, it is apparent that good-looking people enjoy an enormous social advantage in our culture. They are better liked, more persuasive, more frequently helped, and seen as possessing better personality traits and intellectual capacities. And it appears that the social benefits of good looks begin to accumulate quite early. Research on elementary-school children shows that adults view aggressive acts as less naughty when performed by an attractive child and that teachers presume good-looking children to be more intelligent than their less-attractive classmates. 5

其他实验表明，外貌出众的人在需要帮助时更容易获得帮助，也更善于说服他人改变观点。在这方面，男女的反应也相同。例如，在助人研究中，相貌出众的男性和女性更常获得帮助，甚至来自同性。当然，如果外貌出众的人被视为直接竞争对手，尤其是情敌，那么这条规则可能会出现重大例外。但撇开这一限制条件不谈，外貌出众的人在我们的文化中显然享有巨大的社会优势。他们更受欢迎，更有说服力，更容易获得帮助，并且被认为拥有更好的性格特质和智力。而且，外貌带来的社会优势似乎很早就开始积累。对小学生的研究表明，成年人认为外貌出众的孩子做出的攻击性行为不那么恶劣，老师也倾向于认为外貌出众的孩子比相貌平平的同学更聪明。

It is hardly any wonder, then, that the halo of physical attractiveness is regularly exploited by compliance professionals. Because we like attractive people and because we tend to comply with those we like, it makes sense that sales training programs include grooming hints, that fashionable clothiers select their floor staffs from among the good-looking candidates, and that con men are handsome and con women pretty.

因此，外貌吸引力的光环经常被合规人员利用也就不足为奇了。因为我们喜欢外表出众的人，也因为我们倾向于服从自己喜欢的人，所以销售培训课程包含仪容仪表方面的建议，时尚服装店从外形靓丽的候选人中挑选店员，以及骗子通常英俊潇洒、女骗子漂亮动人，这些都符合逻辑。

Similarity

相似

But what if physical appearance is not much at issue? After all, most people possess average looks. Are there other factors that can be used to produce liking? As both researchers and compliance professionals know, there are several, and one of the most influential is similarity.

但如果外貌并非主要因素呢？毕竟，大多数人的外貌都比较普通。那么，除了外貌之外，还有其他因素可以影响好感度吗？研究人员和合规专业人士都知道，这样的因素有很多，其中最具影响力的因素之一就是相似性。

We like people who are similar to us. This fact seems to hold true whether the similarity is in the area of opinions, personality traits, background, or life-style. Consequently, those who wish to be liked in order to increase our compliance can accomplish that purpose by appearing similar to us in any of a wide variety of ways.

我们喜欢与自己相似的人。无论这种相似体现在观点、性格特征、背景还是生活方式上，这一事实似乎都成立。因此，那些希望博得我们好感、从而提高我们顺从度的人，可以通过各种各样的方式让自己看起来与我们相似，以此达到目的。

Dress is a good example. Several studies have demonstrated that we are more likely to help those who dress like us. In one study, done in the early 1970s when young people tended to dress either in "hippie" or "straight" fashion, experimenters donned hippie or straight attire and asked college students on campus for a dime to make a phone call. When the experimenter was dressed in the same way as the student, the request was granted in more than two thirds of the instances; but when the student and requester were dissimilarly dressed, the dime was provided less than half the time. Another experiment shows how automatic our positive response to similar others can be. Marchers in an antiwar demonstration were found to be not only more likely to sign the petition of a similarly dressed requester, but also to do so without bothering to read it first. Click, whirr.

着装就是一个很好的例子。多项研究表明，我们更倾向于帮助那些穿着与我们相似的人。一项在20世纪70年代初进行的研究中，当时年轻人的着装风格大致分为“嬉皮士”和“传统”两类。实验人员分别穿上嬉皮士或传统服饰，向校园里的大学生借一角钱打电话。当实验人员的着装与学生相同时，超过三分之二的学生会答应借钱；但当学生和实验人员的着装不同时，借钱的概率就不到一半了。另一项实验则表明，我们对与自己相似的人的积极反应是多么的自动。在一次反战示威游行中，人们发现，与自己着装相似的请求者，其请愿书上的签名不仅更容易被接受，而且他们甚至无需事先阅读就签名了。咔哒，嗡嗡。

Another way requesters can manipulate similarity to increase liking and compliance is to claim that they have backgrounds and interests similar to ours. Car salesmen, for example, are trained to look for evidence of such things while examining the customer's trade-in. If there is camping gear in the trunk, the salesman might mention, later on, how he loves to get away from the city whenever he can; if there are golf balls on the back seat, he might remark that he hopes the rain will hold off until he can play the eighteen holes he has scheduled for later in the day; if he notices that the car was purchased out of state, he might ask where the customer is from and report—with surprise—that he (or his wife) was born there, too.

请求者还可以通过操纵相似度来提升好感度和顺从度，比如声称自己与我们有着相似的背景和兴趣。例如，汽车销售员就接受过专门训练，会在检查顾客的旧车时寻找这类蛛丝马迹。如果后备箱里有露营装备，销售员之后可能会提到自己多么喜欢尽可能地远离城市喧嚣；如果后座上有高尔夫球，他可能会说希望雨能停，这样他就可以打完当天晚些时候安排的十八洞；如果他注意到这辆车是在外州买的，他可能会问顾客是哪里人，然后惊讶地表示自己（或妻子）也出生在那里。

As trivial as these similarities may seem, they appear to work. One researcher who examined the sales records of insurance companies found that customers were more likely to buy insurance when the salesperson was like them in such areas as age, religion, politics, and cigarette-smoking habits. Because even small similarities can be effective in producing a positive response to another and because a veneer of similarity can be so easily manufactured, I would advise special caution in the presence of requesters who claim to be "just like you." Indeed, it would be wise these days to be careful around salespeople who just seem to be just like you. Many sales training programs now urge trainees to "mirror and match" the customer's body posture, mood, and verbal style, as similarities along each of these dimensions have been shown to lead to positive results. 7

这些相似之处看似微不足道，但似乎确实有效。一位研究人员分析了保险公司的销售记录，发现如果销售人员在年龄、宗教信仰、政治观点和吸烟习惯等方面与客户相似，客户购买保险的可能性就会更高。由于即使是微小的相似之处也能有效地促使他人产生积极的反应，而且这种相似性很容易人为制造，因此我建议在面对声称“和你一模一样”的推销员时要格外谨慎。事实上，如今与那些看起来和你一模一样的销售人员保持警惕是明智之举。许多销售培训项目现在都鼓励学员“模仿”客户的肢体语言、情绪和说话方式，因为研究表明，在这些方面保持相似性能够带来积极的销售结果。

Compliments

赞美

Actor McLean Stevenson once described how his wife tricked him into marriage: "She said she liked me." Although designed for a laugh, the remark is as much instructive as humorous. The information that someone fancies us can be a bewitchingly effective device for producing return liking and willing compliance. So, often in terms of flattery or simple claims of affinity, we hear positive estimation from people who want something from us.

演员麦克莱恩·史蒂文森曾描述过他妻子是如何哄骗他结婚的：“她说她喜欢我。” 这句话虽然是为了博君一笑，却也颇具启发意义。得知有人对我们有好感，往往能起到一种极具诱惑力的作用，让人心甘情愿地喜欢上我们，并心甘情愿地顺从我们。因此，我们常常会听到一些奉承之词或简单的示好之语，而这些话往往出自那些想从我们身上得到些什么的人之口。

Remember Joe Girard, the world's "greatest car salesman," who says the secret of his success was getting customers to like him? He did something that, on the face of it, seems foolish and costly. Each month he sent every one of his more than thirteen thousand former customers a holiday greeting card containing a personal message. The holiday greeting changed from month to month (Happy New Year or Happy Thanksgiving, etc.), but the message printed on the face of the card never varied. It read, "I like you." As Joe explained it, "There's nothing else on the card. Nothin' but my name. I'm just telling 'em that I like 'em."

还记得乔·吉拉德吗？这位号称“世界最伟大的汽车销售员”的成功秘诀是让顾客喜欢他。他做了一件乍看之下既愚蠢又费钱的事。每个月，他都会给超过一万三千名老顾客寄送一张节日贺卡，贺卡里写着一句真挚的祝福。节日祝福每月都不一样（比如新年快乐、感恩节快乐等等），但贺卡上的文字却始终如一：“我喜欢你。”正如乔解释的那样：“贺卡上什么都没有，只有我的名字。我只是想告诉他们，我喜欢他们。”

"I like you." It came in the mail every year, twelve times a year, like clockwork. "I like you," on a printed card that went off to thirteen thousand other people, too. Could a statement of liking so impersonal, so obviously designed to sell cars, really work? Joe Girard thinks so; and a man as successful as he was at what he did deserves our attention. Joe understands an important fact about human nature: We are phenomenal suckers for flattery. Although there are limits to our gullibility—especially when we can be sure that the flatterer is trying to manipulate us—we tend, as a rule, to believe praise and to like those who provide it, oftentimes when it is clearly false.

“我喜欢你。”每年，我都会收到这样一封信，一年十二次，准时如约而至。“我喜欢你”，印在一张卡片上，这张卡片也寄给了其他一万三千人。这样一句冷冰冰的“喜欢”，如此明显是为了推销汽车而设计的，真的有效吗？乔·吉拉德认为有效；而像他这样在汽车行业取得如此成就的人，值得我们关注。乔深谙人性中的一个重要事实：我们极易被奉承所蒙蔽。虽然我们的轻信也是有限度的——尤其当我们确信奉承者试图操纵我们时——但我们通常倾向于相信赞美，并喜欢那些给予我们赞美的人，即便这些赞美往往是虚假的。

An experiment done on men in North Carolina shows how helpless we can be in the face of praise. The men in the study received comments about themselves from another person who needed a favor from them. Some of the men got only positive comments, some got only negative comments, and some got a mixture of good and bad. There were three interesting findings. First, the evaluator who provided only praise was liked best by the men. Second, this was the case even though the men fully realized that the flatterer stood to gain from their liking him. Finally, unlike the other types of comments, pure praise did not have to be accurate to work. Positive comments produced just as much liking for the flatterer when they were untrue as when they were true.

北卡罗来纳州一项针对男性进行的实验表明，面对赞美，我们可能会有多么无助。研究中的男性会收到一位需要他们帮忙的人对他们的评价。有些男性只收到正面评价，有些只收到负面评价，还有一些则好坏参半。研究得出了三个有趣的结论。首先，只给予赞美的评价者最受男性欢迎。其次，即使男性完全意识到奉承者会从他们的好感中获益，情况依然如此。最后，与其他类型的评价不同，纯粹的赞美并不需要准确就能奏效。无论赞美是否属实，都能让男性同样喜欢上奉承者。

Apparently we have such an automatically positive reaction to compliments that we can fall victim to someone who uses them in an obvious attempt to win our favor. Click, whirr. When seen in this light, the expense of printing and mailing well over 150,000 "I like you" cards each year seems neither as foolish nor as costly as before.

显然，我们对赞美之词有着一种与生俱来的积极反应，以至于很容易落入那些明显试图用赞美来博取我们好感的人的圈套。咔哒，嗡嗡。从这个角度来看，每年印刷和邮寄超过15万张“我喜欢你”卡片的费用，似乎既不像以前那么愚蠢，也不像以前那么昂贵了。

# ↩

Contact and Cooperation

联系与合作

For the most part, we like things that are familiar to us. 9 To prove the point to yourself, try a little experiment. Get the negative of an old photograph that shows a front view of your face and have it developed into a pair of pictures—one that shows you as you actually look and one that shows a reverse image (so that the right and left sides of your face are interchanged). Now decide which version of your face you like better and ask a good friend to make the choice, too. If you are at all like a group of Milwaukee women on whom this procedure was tried, you should notice something odd: Your friend will prefer the true print, but you will prefer the reverse image. Why? Because you both will be responding favorably to the more familiar face—your friend to the one the world sees, and you to the transposed one you find in the mirror every day.

大多数情况下，我们都喜欢熟悉的事物。为了验证这一点，不妨做个小实验。找一张旧照片的底片，照片内容是你正面的脸，然后冲洗成两张照片——一张是你原本的样子，另一张是镜像的（左右脸互换）。现在，决定你更喜欢哪一张，并请一位好朋友也做出同样的选择。如果你和之前在密尔沃基接受过这项实验的几位女性一样，你会发现一件奇怪的事情：你的朋友会更喜欢原图，而你会更喜欢镜像的那张。为什么呢？因为你们都会对更熟悉的面孔产生好感——你的朋友喜欢的是世人所见的那张，而你则喜欢的是每天在镜子里看到的那个镜像。

Because of its effect on liking, familiarity plays a role in decisions about all sorts of things, including the politicians we elect. It appears that in an election booth voters often choose a candidate merely because the name seems familiar. In one controversial Ohio election a few years ago, a man given little chance of winning the state attorney-general race swept to victory when, shortly before the election, he changed his name to Brown—a family name of much Ohio political tradition.

由于熟悉感会影响好感度，因此它在各种决策中都扮演着重要角色，包括我们选举的政治人物。在投票站，选民似乎常常仅仅因为候选人的名字听起来熟悉就选择他。几年前，在俄亥俄州一场备受争议的选举中，一位原本被认为几乎没有胜算的州检察长候选人，在选举前不久将自己的名字改为布朗（Brown）——一个在俄亥俄州政治传统中颇具影响力的家族姓氏——后，最终横扫对手，赢得了选举。

How could such a thing happen? The answer lies partially in the unconscious way that familiarity affects liking. Often we don't realize that our attitude toward something has been influenced by the number of times we have been exposed to it in the past. For example, in one experiment, the faces of several individuals were flashed on a screen so quickly that later on, the subjects who were exposed to the faces in this manner couldn't recall having seen any of them before. Yet, the more frequently a person's face was flashed on the screen, the more these subjects came to like that person when they met in a subsequent interaction. And because greater liking leads to greater social influence, these subjects were also more persuaded by the opinion statements of the individuals whose faces had appeared on the screen most frequently.

这种现象怎么会发生呢？部分原因在于熟悉感会潜移默化地影响喜好。我们常常意识不到，我们对某事物的态度会受到过去接触次数的影响。例如，在一项实验中，几张人脸快速闪现在屏幕上，以至于后来，以这种方式接触过这些面孔的受试者都想不起来之前见过他们中的任何一张。然而，一个人的面孔在屏幕上出现的次数越多，这些受试者在之后的互动中就越喜欢这个人。而且，由于更高的好感度会带来更大的社会影响力，这些受试者也更容易被那些在屏幕上出现次数最多的人的观点所说服。

On the basis of evidence that we are more favorable toward the things we have had contact with, some people have recommended a "contact" approach to improving race relations. They argue that simply by providing individuals of different ethnic background with more exposure to one another as equals, those individuals will naturally come to like each other better. However, when scientists have examined school integration—the area offering the single best test of the contact approach—they have discovered quite the opposite pattern. School desegregation is more likely to increase prejudice between blacks and whites than to decrease it.

基于我们往往对接触过的事物抱有好感这一现象，一些人提倡采用“接触式”方法来改善种族关系。他们认为，只要让不同种族背景的人们有更多平等接触的机会，他们自然会彼此产生好感。然而，科学家们在研究学校融合——这是检验“接触式”方法的最佳领域——时，却发现了截然相反的现象。学校取消种族隔离更有可能加剧黑人和白人之间的偏见，而不是减少这种偏见。

Let's stay with the issue of school desegregation for a while. However well intentioned the proponents of interracial harmony through simple contact, their approach is unlikely to bear fruit because the argument on which it is based is terribly misinformed. First of all, the school setting is no melting pot where children interact as readily with members of other ethnic groups as they do with their own. Years after formal school integration, there is little social integration. The students clot together ethnically, separating themselves for the most part from other groups. Second, even if there were much more interethnic interaction, research shows that becoming familiar with something through repeated contact doesn't necessarily cause greater liking. In fact, continued exposure to a person or object under unpleasant conditions such as frustration, conflict, or competition leads to less liking. And the typical American classroom fosters precisely these unpleasant conditions.

让我们先继续讨论学校种族融合的问题。尽管那些主张通过简单的接触来促进种族和谐的人出发点是好的，但他们的方法不太可能奏效，因为他们所依据的论点存在严重的误解。首先，学校并非一个文化熔炉，孩子们不会像与同族人那样轻松地与其他族裔群体互动。即使在正式的学校融合多年之后，社会融合仍然微乎其微。学生们仍然会按族裔聚集在一起，在很大程度上与其他群体隔离开来。其次，即使族裔间的互动显著增加，研究表明，通过反复接触熟悉某事物并不一定会增加喜爱之情。事实上，在诸如挫折、冲突或竞争等不愉快的环境下持续接触某人或某物，反而会导致喜爱程度的降低。而典型的美国课堂恰恰助长了这些不愉快的氛围。

Consider the illuminating report of a psychologist, Elliot Aronson, called in to consult with school authorities on problems in the Austin, Texas, schools. His description of how he found education proceeding in the standard classroom could apply to nearly any public school in the United States:

不妨看看心理学家埃利奥特·阿伦森（Elliot Aronson）的一份颇具启发性的报告。他受邀为德克萨斯州奥斯汀市的学校提供咨询，以解决当地存在的问题。他对标准课堂教学情况的描述几乎适用于美国任何一所公立学校：

In general, here is how it works: The teacher stands in front of the class and asks a question. Six to ten children strain in their seats and wave their hands in the teacher's face, eager to be called on and show how smart they are. Several others sit quietly with eyes averted, trying to become invisible, When the teacher calls on one child, you see looks of disappointment and dismay on the faces of the eager students, who missed a chance to get the teacher's approval; and you will see relief on the faces of the others who didn't know the answer.. This game is fiercely competitive and the stakes are high, because the kids are competing for the love and approval of one of the two or three most important people in their world.
一般来说，游戏规则是这样的：老师站在教室前面提问。六到十个孩子在座位上挤来挤去，在老师面前挥舞着手，渴望被点名，以展现自己的聪明才智。还有一些孩子安静地坐在那里，眼神躲闪，试图让自己不被注意到。当老师点到一个孩子时，你会看到那些急于求成的学生脸上露出失望和沮丧的表情，他们错失了获得老师认可的机会；而那些不知道答案的孩子则如释重负。这场游戏竞争激烈，意义重大，因为孩子们是在争夺他们生命中最重要的两三个人之一的喜爱和认可。
Further, this teaching process guarantees that the children will not learn to like and understand each other. Conjure up your own experience. If you knew the right answer and the teacher called on someone else, you probably hoped that he or she would make a mistake so that you would have a chance to display your knowledge. If you were called on and failed, or if you didn't even raise your hand to compete, you probably envied and resented your classmates who knew the answer. Children who fail in this system become jealous and resentful of the successes, putting them down as teacher's pets or even resorting to violence against them in the school yard. The successful students, for their part, often hold the unsuccessful children in contempt, calling them "dumb" or "stupid."
此外，这种教学方式注定孩子们无法学会彼此喜欢和理解。想想你自己的经历。如果你知道正确答案，而老师点名了其他人，你可能希望他/她犯错，这样你就有机会展示自己的知识。如果你被点名却答错了，或者你甚至没有举手参与竞争，你可能就会嫉妒和怨恨那些知道答案的同学。在这种制度下，失败的孩子会嫉妒和怨恨那些成功的孩子，贬低他们是老师的宠儿，甚至在操场上对他们施暴。而成功的学生则常常鄙视那些失败的孩子，称他们“笨”或“傻”。
This competitive process does not encourage anyone to look benevolently and happily upon his fellow students.
这种竞争过程并不会鼓励任何人以仁慈和快乐的态度看待他的同学。

Should we wonder, then, why raw school desegregation—whether by enforced busing, district rezoning, or school closures—so frequently produces increased rather than decreased prejudice? When our own children find their pleasant social and friendship contacts within their own ethnic boundaries and get repeated exposure to other groups only in the competitive cauldron of the classroom, we might expect as much.

那么，我们是否应该质疑，为什么粗暴的学校种族融合——无论是强制校车接送、学区重新划分还是学校关闭——往往导致偏见加剧而非减少？当我们的孩子只能在自己的族群范围内找到愉快的社交和友谊，而只有在竞争激烈的课堂上才能反复接触到其他群体时，我们或许就能预料到这种情况。

Are there available solutions to this problem? One possibility might be to end our attempts at school integration. But that hardly seems workable. Even were we to ignore the inevitable legal and constitutional challenges and the disruptive societal wrangle such a retreat would provoke, there are solid reasons for pursuing classroom integration. For instance, although white students' achievement levels remain steady, it is ten times more likely that the academic performance of minority students will significantly increase rather than significantly decline after desegregation. We must be cautious in our approach to school desegregation not to throw out the baby because it is sitting in some dirty bath water.

这个问题有可行的解决方案吗？一种可能性是停止学校种族融合的尝试。但这似乎行不通。即使我们忽略不可避免的法律和宪法挑战，以及这种退缩会引发的社会动荡，我们仍然有充分的理由继续推进课堂种族融合。例如，尽管白人学生的学业成绩保持稳定，但少数族裔学生在种族融合后学业成绩显著提高的可能性是显著下降的十倍。我们在推进学校种族融合时必须谨慎，切勿因为一些小问题就彻底放弃。

The idea, of course, is to jettison just the water, leaving the baby shining from the bath. Right now, though, our baby is soaking in the schmutzwasser of increased racial hostility. Fortunately, real hope for draining away that hostility is emerging from the research of education specialists into the concept of "cooperative learning." Because much of the heightened prejudice from classroom desegregation seems to stem from increased exposure to outside group members as rivals, these educators have experimented with forms of learning in which cooperation rather than competition with classmates is central.

当然，我们的想法是只去除水，让婴儿沐浴后容光焕发。然而，眼下我们的婴儿却浸泡在日益增长的种族敌意的污浊水中。幸运的是，教育专家对“合作学习”概念的研究带来了一线希望，有望消除这种敌意。由于课堂种族融合后偏见加剧，很大程度上源于学生更多地接触到外部群体成员，并将他们视为竞争对手，这些教育工作者尝试了以合作而非竞争为核心的学习模式。

Off to camp. To understand the logic of the cooperative approach, it helps to reexamine the fascinating, three-decades-old research program of Turkish-born social scientist Muzafer Sherif. Intrigued with the issue of intergroup conflict, Sherif decided to investigate the process as it developed in boys' summer camps. Although the boys never realized that they were participants in an experiment, Sherif and his associates consistently engaged in artful manipulations of the camp's social environment to observe the effects on group relations.

出发去夏令营。为了理解合作式教学方法的逻辑，我们不妨重新审视一下土耳其裔社会科学家穆扎费尔·谢里夫（Muzafer Sherif）长达三十年的精彩研究项目。谢里夫对群体间冲突问题很感兴趣，于是决定研究男孩夏令营中冲突的发展过程。尽管男孩们从未意识到自己是实验的参与者，但谢里夫和他的同事们始终巧妙地操纵着夏令营的社会环境，以观察这些操纵对群体关系的影响。

It didn't take much to bring on certain kinds of ill will. Simply separating the boys into two residence cabins was enough to stimulate a "we vs. they" feeling between the groups; and assigning names to the two groups (the Eagles and the Rattlers) accelerated the sense of rivalry. The boys soon began to demean the qualities and accomplishments of the other group. But these forms of hostility were minor compared to what occurred when the experimenters purposely introduced competitive activities into the factions' meetings with one another. Cabin against cabin treasure hunts, tugs-of-war, and athletic contests produced name-calling and physical friction. During the competitions, members of the opposing team were labeled "cheaters," "sneaks," and "stinkers." Afterward, cabins were raided, rival banners were stolen and burned, threatening signs were posted, and lunchroom scuffles were commonplace.

只需稍加挑衅，就能激起某些敌意。仅仅将男孩们分成两组，分别住在两个宿舍里，就足以在两组之间激起“我们与他们”的对立感；给两组分别取名为“雄鹰”和“响尾蛇”，更是加剧了这种竞争。男孩们很快便开始贬低对方的品质和成就。然而，与实验人员刻意在两组学生的聚会中引入竞争活动相比，这些敌意显得微不足道。宿舍间的寻宝游戏、拔河比赛和体育竞赛引发了互相辱骂和肢体冲突。比赛期间，对方队员会被贴上“作弊者”、“偷偷摸摸的人”和“讨厌鬼”的标签。比赛结束后，宿舍遭到洗劫，敌对旗帜被偷走并焚烧，恐吓标语被张贴，午餐室里的冲突也屡见不鲜。

At this point, it was evident to Sherif that the recipe for disharmony was quick and easy: Just separate the participants into groups and let sit for a while in their own juices. Then mix together over the flame of continued competition. And there you have it: Cross-group hatred at a rolling boil.

此时，谢里夫很清楚，制造不和的秘诀简单快捷：只需将参与者分成几组，让他们各自沉浸在自己的矛盾中一段时间，然后再在持续的竞争中将他们重新混在一起。瞧，组间仇恨就此沸腾起来。

A more challenging issue then faced the experimenters: how to remove the entrenched hostility they had created. They first tried the contact approach of bringing the bands together more often. But even when the joint activities were pleasant ones, such as movies and social events, the results were disastrous. Picnics produced food fights, entertainment programs gave way to shouting contests, dining-hall lines degenerated into shoving matches. Sherif and his research team began to worry that in Dr. Frankenstein fashion, they might have created a monster they could no longer control. Then, at the height of the strife, they hit on a resolution that was at once simple and effective.

接下来，实验人员面临着一个更具挑战性的问题：如何消除他们一手造成的根深蒂固的敌意。他们首先尝试了接触式方法，让这些群体更频繁地聚在一起。但即使是像看电影和参加社交活动这样愉快的共同活动，结果也令人失望。野餐演变成食物大战，娱乐节目变成了叫喊比赛，食堂排队变成了推搡。谢里夫和他的研究团队开始担心，他们是否像弗兰肯斯坦博士一样，创造了一个无法控制的怪物。就在冲突最激烈的时候，他们想出了一个既简单又有效的解决办法。

They constructed a series of situations in which competition between the groups would have harmed everyone's interests, in which cooperation was necessary for mutual benefit. On a daylong outing, the single truck available to go into town for food was "found" to be stuck. The boys were assembled and all pulled and pushed together until the vehicle was on its way. In another instance, the researchers arranged for an interruption of the camp's water supply, which came through pipes from a distant tank. Presented with the common crisis and realizing the need for unified action, the boys organized themselves harmoniously to find and fix the problem before day's end. In yet another circumstance requiring cooperation, the campers were informed that a desirable movie was available for rental but that the camp could not afford it.
