"My heart sank,” Gulban recalled. "I was not greedy. I just hoped I would see better days.” Gulban never recouped his losses.

“我当时心都凉了，”古尔班回忆道，“我并不贪婪，我只是希望将来能有更好的日子。”古尔班再也没能挽回损失。

让古尔班先生“不假思索地快速购买”。点击，模糊。

(PETER KERR , THE NEW YORK TIMES)

（彼得·克尔，《纽约时报》）

A variant of the deadline tactic is much favored by some face-to-face, high-pressure sellers because it carries the purest form of decision deadline: right now. Customers are often told that unless they make an immediate decision to buy, they will have to purchase the item at a higher price or they will be unable to purchase it at all. A prospective health-club member or automobile buyer might learn that the deal offered by the salesperson is good only for that one time; should the customer leave the premises, the deal is off. One large child-portrait photography company urges parents to buy as many poses and copies as they can afford because "stocking limitations force us to burn the unsold pictures of your children within twenty-four hours." A door-to-door magazine solicitor might say that salespeople are in the customer's area for just a day; after that, they—and the customer's chance to buy their magazine package—will be long gone. A home vacuum-cleaner operation I infiltrated instructed its sales trainees to claim, "I have so many other people to see that I have the time to visit a family only once. It's company policy that even if you decide later that you want this machine, I can't come back and sell it to you." This, of course, is nonsense; the company and its representatives are in the business of making sales, and any customer who called for another visit would be accommodated gladly. As the company sales manager impressed on his trainees, the true purpose of the can't-come-back claim has nothing to do with reducing overburdened sales schedules. It is to "keep the prospects from taking the time to think the deal over by scaring them into believing they can't have it later, which makes them want it now."

一些面对面、高压销售的推销员非常青睐一种“截止日期”策略，因为它包含了最纯粹的决策期限：即刻。他们经常告诉顾客，除非立即决定购买，否则要么只能以更高的价格购买，要么根本买不到。潜在的健身俱乐部会员或汽车买家可能会被告知，销售员提供的优惠仅限一次；如果顾客离开，优惠就失效了。一家大型儿童肖像摄影公司敦促家长尽可能多地购买照片和照片，因为“库存有限，我们将在24小时内销毁您孩子未售出的照片”。挨家挨户推销杂志的推销员可能会说，销售人员只在顾客所在地区停留一天；之后，他们——以及顾客购买杂志的机会——都将消失得无影无踪。我卧底调查的一家家用吸尘器公司指示其销售培训生这样说：“我还有很多客户要拜访，所以只能抽出时间去一家客户家一次。公司规定，即使您之后决定要买这台机器，我也不能再回来卖给您。” 这当然是无稽之谈；公司及其销售代表的本质就是销售，任何要求再次拜访的客户都会欣然接受。正如公司销售经理向培训生强调的那样，这种“不能再次拜访”的说法真正的目的并非为了减轻销售人员的负担，而是为了“吓唬潜在客户，让他们觉得以后买不到，从而让他们没有时间仔细考虑，急于求成”。

PSYCHOLOGICAL REACTANCE

心理抗拒

The evidence, then, is clear. Compliance practitioners' reliance on scarcity as a weapon of influence is frequent, wide-ranging, systematic, and diverse. Whenever such is the case with a weapon of influence, we can feel assured that the principle involved has notable power in directing human action. In the instance of the scarcity principle, that power comes from two major sources. The first is familiar. Like the other weapons of influence, the scarcity principle trades on our weakness for shortcuts. The weakness is, as before, an enlightened one. In this case, because we know that the things that are difficult to possess are typically better than those that are easy to possess, we can often use an item's availability to help us quickly and correctly decide on its quality. Thus, one reason for the potency of the scarcity principle is that, by following it, we are usually and efficiently right. 3

因此，证据显而易见。合规从业者利用稀缺性作为影响力武器的现象十分普遍、广泛、系统且多样。每当一种影响力武器出现这种情况时，我们就可以确信，其中涉及的原则在指导人类行为方面具有显著的力量。就稀缺性原则而言，这种力量主要来源于两个方面。第一个方面我们并不陌生。与其他影响力武器一样，稀缺性原则利用了我们寻求捷径的弱点。而这种弱点，一如既往，是一种明智的弱点。在这种情况下，因为我们知道难以获得的东西通常比容易获得的东西更好，所以我们常常可以利用物品的可获得性来帮助我们快速准确地判断其质量。因此，稀缺性原则之所以如此有效，原因之一在于，遵循这一原则，我们通常能够高效地做出正确的判断。

FIGURE 7-3 Don't Wait! Last chance to read this now before you turn the page ( ROBERT B. CIALDINI)

图 7-3 别再犹豫！翻页前最后的机会，赶紧阅读！（罗伯特·B·西奥迪尼）

In addition, there is a unique, secondary source of power within the scarcity principle: As opportunities become less available, we lose freedoms; and we hate to lose the freedoms we already have. This desire to preserve our established prerogatives is the centerpiece of psychological reactance theory, developed by psychologist Jack Brehm to explain the human response to diminishing personal control. According to the theory, whenever free choice is limited or threatened, the need to retain our freedoms makes us desire them (as well as the goods and services associated with them) significantly more than previously. So when increasing scarcity—or anything else—interferes with our prior access to some item, we will react against the interference by wanting and trying to possess the item more than before. 4

此外，稀缺性原则中还蕴含着一种独特的、次要的力量来源：随着机会的减少，我们会失去自由；而我们不愿失去已有的自由。这种维护既有特权的愿望正是心理抗拒理论的核心，该理论由心理学家杰克·布雷姆提出，旨在解释人类对个人控制力减弱的反应。根据该理论，每当自由选择受到限制或威胁时，为了维护自由，我们会比以往更加渴望这些自由（以及与之相关的商品和服务）。因此，当稀缺性增加——或其他任何因素——干扰我们先前获得某些物品的途径时，我们会对这种干扰做出反应，比以往更加渴望并试图拥有该物品。

As simple as the kernel of the theory seems, its shoots and roots curl extensively through much of the social environment. From the garden of young love to the jungle of armed revolution to the fruits of the marketplace, impressive amounts of our behavior can be explained by examining for the tendrils of psychological reactance. Before beginning such an examination, though, it would be helpful to know when people first show the desire to fight against restrictions of their freedoms.

尽管这一理论的核心看似简单，但它的枝叶却广泛渗透到社会环境的各个角落。从青涩的爱情花园到武装革命的丛林，再到熙熙攘攘的市场，我们许多行为都可以通过探究心理抗拒的蛛丝马迹来解释。然而，在展开这样的探究之前，了解人们何时开始表现出反抗自由限制的意愿，将大有裨益。

Child psychologists have traced the tendency back to the start of the third year of life—a year independently identified as a problem by parents and widely known to them as "the terrible twos." Most parents can attest to the development of a decidedly more contrary style in their children around this period. Two-year-olds seem masters of the art of resistance to outside, especially parental, pressure: Tell them one thing, they do the opposite; give them one toy, they want another; pick them up against their will, they wriggle and squirm to be put down; put them down against their will, they claw and struggle to be carried.

儿童心理学家发现，这种倾向最早出现在孩子三岁左右——父母们普遍认为这一年是个问题，并称之为“可怕的两岁”。大多数父母都能证实，孩子在这个时期会表现出明显的叛逆倾向。两岁的孩子似乎天生就擅长反抗外界压力，尤其是来自父母的压力：你告诉他们一件事，他们就反其道而行之；你给他们一个玩具，他们就想要另一个；你强行抱起他们，他们就扭来扭去要你放下；你强行放下他们，他们就抓挠挣扎要你抱。

One Virginia-based study nicely captured the terrible twos style among boys who averaged twenty-four months in age. The boys accompanied their mothers into a room containing two equally attractive toys. The toys were always arranged so that one stood next to a transparent Plexiglas barrier and the other stood behind the barrier. For some of the boys, the Plexiglas sheet was only a foot tall—forming no real barrier to the toy behind, since the boys could easily reach over the top. For the other boys, however, the Plexiglas was two feet tall, effectively blocking the boys' access to one toy unless they went around the barrier. The researchers wanted to see how quickly the toddlers would make contact with the toys under these conditions. Their findings were clear. When the barrier was too small to restrict access to the toy behind it, the boys showed no special preference for either of the toys; on the average, the toy next to the barrier was touched just as quickly as the one behind. But when the barrier was big enough to be a true obstacle, the boys went directly to the obstructed toy, making contact with it three times faster than with the unobstructed toy. In all, the boys in this study demonstrated the classic terrible twos' response to a limitation of their freedom: outright defiance. 5

弗吉尼亚州一项研究巧妙地捕捉到了平均年龄为24个月的男孩在“可怕的两岁”时期的行为模式。研究人员让男孩们跟随母亲进入一个房间，房间里摆放着两个同样吸引他们的玩具。玩具的摆放方式是：一个玩具紧挨着透明的有机玻璃板，另一个则位于板后。对于一些男孩来说，有机玻璃板只有一英尺高——由于他们可以轻松地越过板顶拿到后面的玩具，因此对后面的玩具几乎没有任何阻碍。然而，对于另一些男孩来说，有机玻璃板的高度为两英尺，有效地阻挡了他们接触其中一个玩具，除非他们绕过板。研究人员想要观察在这种情况下，幼儿接触玩具的速度有多快。他们的研究结果很明确：当板的高度不足以限制他们接触后面的玩具时，男孩们对两个玩具都没有表现出明显的偏好；平均而言，他们触摸板旁玩具和板后玩具的速度几乎相同。但当障碍物足够大，构成真正的阻碍时，男孩们会径直走向被阻挡的玩具，接触速度比接触未被阻挡的玩具快三倍。总而言之，这项研究中的男孩们表现出了典型的“可怕的两岁”时期对自由受限的反应：公然反抗。

Why should psychological reactance emerge at the age of two? Perhaps the answer has to do with a crucial change that most children go through around this time. It is then that they first come to a full recognition of themselves as individuals. No longer do they view themselves as mere extensions of the social milieu but rather as identifiable, singular, and separate. This developing concept of autonomy brings naturally with it the concept of freedom. An independent being is one with choices; and a child with the newfound realization that he or she is such a being will want to explore the length and breadth of the options. Perhaps we should be neither surprised nor distressed, then, when our two-year-olds strain incessantly against our will. They have come to a recent and exhilarating perspective on themselves as free-standing human entities. Vital questions of volition, entitlements, and control now need to be asked and answered within their small minds. The tendency to fight for every liberty and against every restriction might be best understood as a quest for information. By testing severely the limits of their freedoms (and coincidentally, the patience of their parents), the children are discovering where in their worlds they can expect to be controlled and where they can expect to be in control. As we will see later, the wise parent provides highly consistent information.

为什么心理抗拒会在两岁时出现？或许答案与大多数孩子在这个时期经历的关键转变有关。正是在这个时期，他们第一次真正认识到自身的个体性。他们不再将自己视为社会环境的延伸，而是将自己视为可识别的、独特的、独立的个体。这种自主意识的萌芽自然而然地带来了自由的概念。一个独立的个体拥有选择权；而一个孩子一旦意识到自己是这样的个体，就会渴望探索各种选择。因此，当我们的两岁孩子不断地反抗我们的意愿时，或许我们既不应该感到惊讶，也不应该感到焦虑。他们刚刚对自身作为独立的个体有了全新的、令人兴奋的认知。关于意志、权利和控制等至关重要的问题，现在需要在他们幼小的心灵中提出并解答。他们争取每一项自由、反对每一项限制的倾向，或许可以被理解为一种对信息的渴求。孩子们通过不断试探自身自由的极限（同时也考验着父母的耐心），逐渐发现，在他们的世界里，哪些方面需要被控制，哪些方面需要掌控。正如我们稍后将看到的，明智的父母会提供高度一致的信息。

Although the terrible twos may be the most noticeable age of psychological reactance, we show the strong tendency to react against restrictions on our freedoms of action throughout our lives. One other age does stand out, however, as a time when this tendency takes an especially rebellious form: teenage. Like the twos, this is a period characterized by an emerging sense of individuality. For teenagers, the emergence is from the role of child, with all of its attendant parental control, and toward the role of adult, with all of its attendant rights and duties. Not surprisingly, adolescents tend to focus less on the duties than on the rights they feel they have as young adults. Not surprisingly, again, imposing traditional parental authority at these times is often counterproductive; the teenager will sneak, scheme, and fight to resist such attempts at control.

虽然“可怕的两岁”可能是心理抗拒最明显的时期，但我们一生中都会表现出对行动自由受到限制的强烈反抗倾向。然而，还有一个时期尤为突出，这种倾向会以特别叛逆的形式表现出来：那就是青少年时期。与两岁时期一样，青少年时期也是一个个体意识逐渐形成的时期。对青少年而言，这种转变是从儿童角色（伴随着父母的所有控制）向成人角色（伴随着所有权利和义务）的转变。不出所料，青少年往往更关注他们作为年轻成年人所拥有的权利，而不是义务。同样不出所料，在这个时期强加传统的父母权威往往会适得其反；青少年会偷偷摸摸、耍阴谋诡计、甚至反抗这种控制。

Nothing illustrates the boomerang quality of parental pressure on adolescent behavior quite so clearly as a phenomenon known as the "Romeo and Juliet effect." As we know, Romeo Montague and Juliet Capulet were the ill-fated Shakespearean characters whose love was doomed by a feud between their families. Defying all parental attempts to keep them apart, the teenagers won a lasting union in their tragic act of twin suicide, an ultimate assertion of free will.

没有什么比“罗密欧与朱丽叶效应”更能清晰地展现父母压力对青少年行为的反噬效应了。众所周知，罗密欧·蒙太古和朱丽叶·凯普莱特是莎士比亚笔下命运多舛的人物，他们的爱情因家族世仇而注定悲剧收场。尽管父母百般阻挠，这对少年最终还是选择了双双殉情，以悲剧的方式捍卫了自由意志，成就了一段永恒的姻缘。

The intensity of the couple's feelings and actions has always been a source of wonderment and puzzlement to observers of the play. How could such inordinate devotion develop so quickly in a pair so young? A romantic might suggest rare and perfect love. A social scientist, though, might point to the role of parental interference and the psychological reactance it can produce. Perhaps the passion of Romeo and Juliet was not initially so consuming that it transcended the extensive barriers erected by the families. Perhaps, instead, it was fueled to a white heat by the placement of those barriers. Could it be that had the youngsters been left to their own devices, their inflamed devotion would have amounted to no more than a flicker of puppy love?

这对恋人炽烈的情感和行为一直令剧迷们感到惊奇和困惑。如此年轻的恋人，为何会如此迅速地发展出如此强烈的爱恋？浪漫主义者或许会认为这是罕见而完美的爱情。然而，社会学家则可能指出父母的干预及其引发的心理抗拒。或许罗密欧与朱丽叶的激情最初并非如此强烈，以至于能够超越家族设置的重重障碍。或许，正是这些障碍反而将他们的爱火烧得炽烈。如果这对年轻人能够自由自在地相处，他们炽热的爱恋是否也只会像懵懂的初恋般短暂呢？

Because the story is fiction, such questions are, of course, hypothetical, and any answers to them are speculative. However, it is possible to ask and answer with more certainty similar questions about modern-day Romeos and Juliets. Do couples suffering parental interference react by committing themselves more firmly to the partnership and falling more deeply in love? According to a study done with 140 Colorado couples, that is exactly what they do. In fact, the researchers found that although parental interference was linked to some problems in the relationship—the partners viewed one another more critically and reported a greater number of negative behaviors in the other—that interference also made the pair feel greater love and desire for marriage. During the course of the study, as parental interference intensified, so did the love experience; and when the interference weakened, romantic feelings actually cooled. 7

由于故事是虚构的，这些问题当然只是假设，任何答案也只是推测。然而，对于现代的罗密欧与朱丽叶，我们可以提出并更有把握地回答类似的问题。遭受父母干预的情侣是否会更加坚定地投入这段关系，并坠入更深的爱河？一项针对科罗拉多州140对情侣的研究表明，事实正是如此。研究人员发现，尽管父母干预与一些关系问题有关——伴侣们对彼此的评价更加苛刻，并报告了更多对方的负面行为——但这种干预也让情侣们感受到更浓烈的爱意和对婚姻的渴望。在研究过程中，随着父母干预的加剧，情侣们的爱情体验也随之增强；而当干预减弱时，浪漫的情感反而会冷却下来。

Although the Romeo and Juliet effect among modern teenagers may seem cute—to outside observers—other manifestations of teenage reactance can prove tragic. For more than a decade, the major message of a massive advertising campaign for Virginia Slims cigarettes has been that today's women "have come a long way" from the old days when they were required by social norms to be subdued, proper, and ladylike. No longer, imply these ads, should a woman have to feel bound by chauvinistic and outmoded constraints on her independence and, pointedly, on her freedom to smoke cigarettes. Has the message been successful in triggering defiance of the old strictures among the target audience? One dismaying statistic suggests a lamentable answer: During the lengthy duration of this campaign, the percentage of cigarette smokers has risen in only one U.S. demographic group—teenage women.

尽管现代青少年中出现的“罗密欧与朱丽叶效应”在外人看来或许可爱，但青少年反抗情绪的其他表现形式却可能酿成悲剧。十多年来，弗吉尼亚纤细香烟的大规模广告宣传活动一直强调，如今的女性“已经与过去截然不同”，不再像过去那样被社会规范要求温顺、得体、举止淑女。这些广告暗示，女性不应再受沙文主义和过时的束缚，她们的独立性，尤其是吸烟的自由，不应再受到限制。然而，这一信息是否成功地激发了目标受众对旧有束缚的反抗呢？一项令人沮丧的统计数据表明，答案令人遗憾：在这场漫长的广告宣传期间，美国只有一个群体——青少年女性——的吸烟率有所上升。

For twos and teens, then, psychological reactance flows across the broad surface of experience, always turbulent and forceful. For most of the rest of us, the pool of reactant energy lies quiet and covered, erupting geyserlike only on occasion. Still, these eruptions manifest themselves in a variety of fascinating ways that are of interest not only to the student of human behavior but to lawmakers and policymakers as well.

因此，对于两岁和青少年来说，心理抗拒贯穿于他们广阔的体验之中，始终汹涌澎湃、势不可挡。而对于我们大多数人来说，这种抗拒能量则静静地潜藏着，只有偶尔才会像间歇泉般喷发。然而，这些喷发却以各种引人入胜的方式呈现出来，不仅对研究人类行为的学者意义非凡，也同样能引起立法者和政策制定者的关注。

For instance, there's the odd case of Kennesaw, Georgia, the town that enacted a law requiring every adult resident to own a gun and ammunition, under penalty of six months in jail and a two-hundred-dollar fine. All the features of the Kennesaw gun law make it a prime target for psychological reactance: The freedom that the law restricts is an important, long-standing one to which most American citizens feel entitled. Furthermore, the law was passed by the Kennesaw City Council with a minimum of public input. Reactance theory would predict that under these circumstances few of the adults in the town of fifty-four hundred would obey. Yet newspaper reports testified that three to four weeks after passage of the law, firearms sales in Kennesaw were—no pun intended—booming.

例如，佐治亚州肯尼索市就是一个奇特的例子。该市颁布了一项法律，规定所有成年居民必须拥有枪支和弹药，违者将面临六个月监禁和两百美元罚款。肯尼索枪支法的种种特点使其成为心理抗拒的绝佳目标：该法律限制的自由是一项重要的、由来已久的自由，大多数美国公民都认为自己理应享有这项自由。此外，肯尼索市议会在几乎没有征求公众意见的情况下通过了这项法律。根据抗拒理论，在这种情况下，这个拥有五千四百名居民的小镇上，很少有成年人会遵守这项法律。然而，报纸报道显示，该法律通过三到四周后，肯尼索的枪支销量——毫不夸张地说——出现了爆炸式增长。

How are we to make sense of this apparent contradiction of the reactance principle? By looking a bit more closely at those who were buying Kennesaw's guns. Interviews with Kennesaw store owners revealed that the gun buyers were not town residents at all, but visitors, many of them lured by publicity to purchase their initial gun in Kennesaw. Donna Green, proprietor of a shop described in one newspaper article as a virtual "grocery store of firearms," summed it up: "Business is great. But they're almost all being bought by people from out of town. We've only had two or three local people buy a gun to comply with the law." After passage of the law, then, gun buying had become a frequent activity in Kennesaw, but not among those it was intended to cover; they were massively noncompliant. Only those individuals whose freedom in the matter had not been restricted by the law had the inclination to live by it.

我们该如何理解这种看似矛盾的逆反心理原理呢？答案在于更仔细地观察肯尼索的枪支购买者。对肯尼索商店老板的采访显示，购枪者并非本地居民，而是外地游客，其中许多人是被媒体宣传吸引而来，在肯尼索购买了他们的第一支枪。唐娜·格林（Donna Green）的商店被一家报纸形容为“枪支杂货店”，她总结道：“生意很好。但几乎所有枪支都被外地人买走了。只有两三个本地人为了遵守法律而购买了枪支。” 因此，法律通过后，购枪在肯尼索变得十分普遍，但并非在法律旨在约束的人群中；他们大多不遵守法律。只有那些在购枪方面没有受到法律限制的人，才倾向于遵守法律。

A similar situation arose a decade earlier and several hundred miles to the south of Kennesaw, when Dade County (containing Miami), Florida, imposed an antiphosphate ordinance prohibiting the use—and possession!—of laundry or cleaning products containing phosphates. A study done to determine the social impact of the law discovered two parallel reactions on the part of Miami residents. First, in what seems a Florida tradition, many Miamians turned to smuggling. Sometimes with neighbors and friends in large "soap caravans," they drove to nearby counties to load up on phosphate detergents. Hoarding quickly developed; and in the rush of obsession that frequently characterizes hoarders, families were reported to boast of twenty-year supplies of phosphate cleaners.

十年前，在肯尼索以南数百英里的佛罗里达州戴德县（迈阿密所在地）也出现了类似的情况。当时，该县颁布了一项反磷酸盐法令，禁止使用——甚至持有！——含磷酸盐的洗衣或清洁产品。一项旨在评估该法令社会影响的研究发现，迈阿密居民出现了两种截然不同的反应。首先，似乎出于佛罗里达州的传统，许多迈阿密人开始走私。他们有时会和邻居朋友组成大型“肥皂车队”，驱车前往邻近县市大量囤积含磷酸盐的洗涤剂。囤积现象迅速蔓延；在囤积者常见的狂热驱使下，据报道，一些家庭甚至炫耀自己囤积了足够使用二十年的含磷酸盐清洁剂。

The second reaction to the law was more subtle and more general than the deliberate defiance of the smugglers and hoarders. Spurred by the tendency to want what they could no longer have, the majority of Miami consumers came to see phosphate cleaners as better products than before. Compared to Tampa residents, who were not affected by the Dade County ordinance, the citizens of Miami rated phosphate detergents as gentler, more effective in cold water, better whiteners and fresheners, more powerful on stains. After passage of the law, they had even come to believe that phos 8 phate detergents poured more easily than did the Tampa consumers. 8

对该法律的第二次反应比走私者和囤积者的蓄意违抗更为微妙和普遍。由于渴望那些他们再也无法拥有的东西，大多数迈阿密消费者开始认为磷酸盐清洁剂比以前更好。与不受戴德县法令影响的坦帕居民相比，迈阿密市民认为磷酸盐洗涤剂更温和，在冷水中效果更好，增白和清新效果更佳，去污力更强。该法律通过后，他们甚至开始认为磷酸盐洗涤剂比坦帕消费者更容易倾倒。

This sort of response is typical of individuals who have lost an established freedom and is crucial to an understanding of how psychological reactance and scarcity work on us. When our freedom to have something is limited, the item becomes less available, and we experience an increased desire for it. However, we rarely recognize that psychological reactance has caused us to want the item more; all we know is that we want it. Still, we need to make sense of our desire for the item, so we begin to assign it positive qualities to justify the desire. After all, it is natural to suppose that if one feels drawn to something, it is because of the merit of the thing. In the case of the Dade County antiphosphate law—and in other instances of newly restricted availability—that is a faulty supposition. Phosphate detergents clean, whiten, and pour no better after they are banned than before. We just assume they do because we find that we desire them more.

这种反应常见于失去既有自由的人，对于理解心理抗拒和稀缺性如何影响我们至关重要。当我们拥有某样东西的自由受到限制时，该物品的获取难度增加，我们对它的渴望也随之增强。然而，我们很少意识到是心理抗拒导致我们更加渴望该物品；我们只知道自己想要它。尽管如此，我们仍然需要理解自己对物品的渴望，因此我们开始赋予它积极的特质来为这种渴望辩解。毕竟，人们自然会认为，如果自己被某样东西吸引，那是因为它本身具有价值。但在戴德县的反磷酸盐法案以及其他一些新近限制磷酸盐供应的案例中，这种假设是错误的。磷酸盐洗涤剂在被禁用后，其清洁、增白和倾倒效果并不会比禁用前更好。我们之所以会这样认为，仅仅是因为我们发现自己更渴望它们了。

The tendency to want what has been banned and therefore to presume that it is more worthwhile is not limited to such commodities as laundry soap. In fact, the tendency is not limited to commodities at all but extends to restrictions on information. In an age when the ability to acquire, store, and manage information is becoming increasingly the determinant of wealth and power, it is important to understand how we typically react to attempts to censor or otherwise constrain our access to information. Although much data exist on our reactions to various kinds of potentially censorable material—media violence, pornography, radical political rhetoric—there is surprisingly little evidence as to our reactions to the act of censoring them. Fortunately, the results of the few studies that have been done on the topic are highly consistent. Almost invariably, our response to the banning of information is a greater desire to receive that in 9 formation and a more favorable attitude toward it than before the ban.

人们往往倾向于渴望被禁之物，并因此认为它更有价值，这种倾向并非仅限于洗衣皂之类的商品。事实上，这种倾向根本不局限于商品，而是延伸至信息限制领域。在信息获取、存储和管理能力日益成为财富和权力决定因素的时代，了解我们通常如何应对审查或以其他方式限制我们获取信息的企图至关重要。尽管关于我们对各种潜在审查内容（例如媒体暴力、色情内容、激进政治言论）的反应已有大量数据，但令人惊讶的是，关于我们对审查行为本身的反应却鲜有证据。幸运的是，少数相关研究的结果高度一致。几乎无一例外，我们对信息禁令的反应是：比禁令实施前更渴望获取该信息，并且对其持有更积极的态度。

The intriguing thing about the effects of censoring information is not that audience members want to have the information more than they did before; that seems natural. Rather, it is that they come to believe in the information more, even though they haven't received it. For example, when University of North Carolina students learned that a speech opposing coed dorms on campus would be banned, they became more opposed to the idea of coed dorms. Thus, without ever hearing the speech, they became more sympathetic to its argument. This raises the worrisome possibility that especially clever individuals holding a weak or unpopular position can get us to agree with that position by arranging to have their message restricted. The irony is that for such people—members of fringe political groups, for example—the most effective strategy may not be to publicize their unpopular views, but to get those views officially censored and then to publicize the censorship. Perhaps the authors of this country's Constitution were acting as much as sophisticated social psychologists as staunch civil libertarians when they wrote the remarkably permissive free-speech provision of the First Amendment. By refusing to restrain freedom of speech, they may have been attempting to minimize the chance that new political notions would win support via the irrational course of psychological reactance.

审查信息的影响中最引人入胜之处，并非在于受众比以往更渴望获得信息；这似乎是人之常情。而在于，即便他们并未接触到这些信息，他们也会更加相信这些信息。例如，当北卡罗来纳大学的学生得知反对男女同住宿舍的演讲将被禁止时，他们反而更加反对男女同住宿舍的想法。因此，即便从未听过演讲，他们也更加认同演讲者的论点。这引发了一种令人担忧的可能性：一些特别精明的人，即使持有弱势或不受欢迎的立场，也能通过安排限制其信息的传播，让我们认同他们的立场。讽刺的是，对于这些人——例如边缘政治团体的成员——最有效的策略或许并非公开宣扬他们不受欢迎的观点，而是先让这些观点遭到官方审查，然后再公开揭露审查行为。或许，美国宪法的制定者们在撰写第一修正案中那条极其宽容的言论自由条款时，既是深谙此道的社会心理学家，也是坚定的公民自由主义者。他们拒绝限制言论自由，或许是为了尽可能降低新的政治理念因非理性的心理抗拒而获得支持的可能性。

Of course, political ideas are not the only kind that are susceptible to restriction. Access to sexually relevant material is frequently limited. Although not as sensational as the occasional police crackdowns on "adult" bookstores and theaters, regular pressure is applied by parents and by citizens' groups to censor the sexual content of educational material ranging from sex education and hygiene texts to books on the shelves of school libraries. Both sides in the struggle seem to be well intentioned, and the issues are not simple, since they involve such matters as morality, art, parental control over the schools, and First Amendment freedoms. But from a purely psychological point of view, those favoring strict censorship may wish to examine closely the results of a study done on Purdue University undergraduates. The students were shown some advertisements for a novel. For half the students, the advertising copy included the statement, "a book for adults only, restricted to those 21 years and over"; the other half of the students read about no such age restriction on the book. When the researchers later asked the students to indicate their feelings toward the book, they discovered the same pair of reactions we have noted with other bans: Those who learned of the age restriction (1) wanted to read the book more and (2) believed that they would like the book more than did those who thought their access to the book was unlimited.

当然，政治思想并非唯一容易受到限制的领域。获取与性相关的材料也常常受到限制。虽然不像警方偶尔突击检查“成人”书店和剧院那样引人注目，但家长和公民团体经常施压，要求审查教育材料中的性内容，这些材料涵盖性教育和卫生教材，以及学校图书馆书架上的书籍。这场斗争双方似乎都出于好意，而且问题也并非简单，因为它涉及道德、艺术、家长对学校的控制权以及宪法第一修正案赋予的自由等诸多方面。但从纯粹的心理学角度来看，那些支持严格审查制度的人或许应该仔细研究一下普渡大学本科生的一项研究结果。研究人员向学生们展示了一些小说广告。其中一半学生看到的广告文案包含“仅限成人阅读，21岁及以上人士阅读”的字样；而另一半学生看到的广告则没有提及该书的年龄限制。当研究人员后来询问学生们对这本书的感受时，他们发现了与我们对其他禁书相同的两种反应：那些得知年龄限制的学生（1）更想读这本书，（2）相信他们会比那些认为自己可以不受限制地阅读这本书的学生更喜欢这本书。

It might be argued that although these results may be true for a small sample of sexually inclined college students, they would not apply to students in junior and senior high schools, where the sex curricula battles are actually being waged. Two factors make me doubt such an argument. First, developmental psychologists report that as a general style, the desire to oppose adult control begins quite soon in adolescence, around the start of the teenage years. Nonscientific observers have also noted the early rise of these strong oppositional tendencies. Shakespeare, scholars tell us, placed Romeo and Juliet at the ages of fifteen and thirteen years, respectively. Second, the pattern of reactions exhibited by the Purdue students is not unique and thus can't be attributed to any great preoccupation with sex that college students may have. The pattern is common to externally imposed restrictions in general. Limiting access to the book had the same effects as did banning phosphate detergent in Florida or censoring a speech in North Carolina: The people involved came to want the restricted item more and, as a result, came to feel more favorable toward it.

有人可能会认为，虽然这些结果可能适用于一小部分性倾向较强的大学生，但它们并不适用于初高中学生，因为性教育之争实际上正是在初高中展开的。有两个因素让我对这种论点表示怀疑。首先，发展心理学家指出，反抗成人控制的倾向通常在青春期早期，也就是青少年时期开始出现。非科学观察者也注意到了这种强烈的反抗倾向的早期出现。学者们告诉我们，莎士比亚笔下的罗密欧和朱丽叶分别只有十五岁和十三岁。其次，普渡大学学生所表现出的反应模式并非个例，因此不能归因于大学生对性的过度关注。这种模式在普遍存在的外部限制下更为常见。限制人们获取这本书的途径，其效果与在佛罗里达州禁止使用磷酸盐洗涤剂或在北卡罗来纳州审查演讲的效果相同：相关人员更加需要被限制的物品，结果，他们对这类物品产生了更好感。

Those who support the official banning of sexually relevant materials from school curricula have the avowed purpose of reducing the orientation of the society, especially its youth, toward eroticism. In the light of the Purdue study and in the context of other research on the effects of imposed restraints, one must wonder whether official censorship as a means may not be antithetical to the goal. If we are to believe the implications of the research, then the censorship is likely to increase the desire of students for sexual material and, consequently, to cause them to view themselves as the kind of individuals who like such material.

那些支持官方禁止在学校课程中引入性相关内容的人，其公开目的是为了降低社会，尤其是青少年群体对色情的倾向。然而，结合普渡大学的研究以及其他关于强制限制措施影响的研究，我们不禁要问，官方审查作为一种手段，是否反而会与目标背道而驰。如果这项研究的结论成立，那么审查制度很可能会增强学生对性相关内容的渴望，并最终导致他们认为自己就是喜欢这类内容的人。

The term "official censorship" usually makes us think of bans on political or sexual material; yet there is another common sort of official censorship that we don't think of in the same way, probably because it occurs after the fact. Often in a jury trial, a piece of evidence or testimony will be introduced, only to be ruled inadmissi-ble by the presiding judge, who may then admonish the jurors to disregard that evidence. From this perspective, the judge may be viewed as a censor, though the form of censorship is odd. The presentation of the information to the jury is not banned—it's too late for that—it's the jury's use of the information that is banned. How effective are such instructions from a judge? And is it possible that, for jury members who feel it is their right to consider all the available information, declarations of inadmissibility may actually cause psychological reactance, leading the jurors to use the evidence to a greater extent?

“官方审查”一词通常会让我们想到对政治或色情内容的禁令；然而，还有另一种常见的官方审查形式，我们却往往不会这样看待，这可能是因为它发生在事后。在陪审团审判中，经常会出现这样的情况：证据或证词被提交，但随后被主审法官裁定为不可采纳，法官甚至可能告诫陪审员忽略该证据。从这个角度来看，法官可以被视为审查者，尽管这种审查形式很奇特。向陪审团呈现信息本身并没有被禁止——为时已晚——被禁止的是陪审团对信息的使用。法官的这种指示究竟有多大效果？对于那些认为自己有权考虑所有可用信息的陪审员来说，宣布证据不可采纳是否反而会引发心理抵触情绪，促使他们更多地使用这些证据？

These were some of the questions asked in a large-scale jury-research project conducted by the University of Chicago Law School. One reason the results of the Chicago jury project are informative is that the participants were individuals who were actually on jury duty at the time and who agreed to be members of "experimental juries" formed by the researchers. These experimental juries then heard tapes of evidence from previous trials and deliberated as if they were deciding the case. In the study most relevant to our interest in official censorship, thirty such juries heard the case of a woman who was injured by a car driven by a careless male defendant. The first finding of the study was no surprise: When the driver said he had liability insurance, the jurors awarded his victim an average of four thousand dollars more than when he said he had no insurance (thirty-seven thousand dollars vs. thirty-three thousand dollars). Thus, as insurance companies have long suspected, juries make larger awards to victims if an insurance company will have to pay. The second finding of the study is the fascinating one, though. If the driver said he was insured and the judge ruled that evidence inadmissible (directing the jury to disregard it), the instruction to disregard had a boomerang effect, causing an average award of forty-six thousand dollars. So when certain juries learned that the driver was insured, they increased the damage payment by four thousand dollars. But when other juries were told officially that they must not use that information, they used it still more, increasing the damage payment by thirteen thousand dollars. It appears, then, that even proper, official censorship in a courtroom setting creates problems for the censor. We react to information restriction there, as usual, by valuing the banned information more than ever.

这些问题是芝加哥大学法学院开展的一项大型陪审团研究项目中提出的问题之一。芝加哥陪审团项目之所以具有参考价值，原因之一在于参与者均为当时正在履行陪审义务的人员，他们同意加入研究人员组建的“实验陪审团”。这些实验陪审团随后听取了以往审判的证据录音，并像审理案件一样进行审议。在与我们关注的官方审查制度最为相关的研究中，30个这样的陪审团审理了一起女性被粗心男性被告驾驶的汽车撞伤的案件。该研究的第一个发现并不令人意外：当司机声称自己购买了责任保险时，陪审团判给受害者的赔偿金平均比他声称自己没有保险时高出4000美元（3.7万美元对比3.3万美元）。因此，正如保险公司长期以来所怀疑的那样，如果保险公司最终需要赔付，陪审团就会判给受害者更高的赔偿金。然而，该研究的第二个发现却引人入胜。如果司机声称自己有保险，而法官裁定该证据不可采纳（指示陪审团忽略该证据），那么这种不采纳的指示反而产生了反作用，导致平均赔偿金额仅为四万六千美元。因此，当某些陪审团得知司机有保险时，他们将赔偿金额增加了四千美元。但当另一些陪审团被正式告知不得使用该信息时，他们反而更多地使用了该信息，导致赔偿金额增加了一万三千美元。由此可见，即使是法庭上合乎规范的官方审查，也会给审查者带来麻烦。我们面对信息限制的反应，一如既往，是比以往任何时候都更加重视被禁止的信息。

The realization that we value limited information allows us to apply the scarcity principle to realms beyond material commodities. The principle works for messages, communications, and knowledge, too. Taking this perspective, we can see that information may not have to be censored for us to value it more; it need only be scarce. According to the scarcity principle, then, we will find a piece of information more persuasive if we think we can't get it elsewhere. This idea that exclusive information is more persuasive information is central to the thinking of two psychologists, Timothy Brock and Howard Fromkm, who have developed a "commodity theory" analysis of persuasion.

我们意识到自己珍视有限的信息，这使得我们可以将稀缺性原则应用于物质商品以外的领域。这一原则同样适用于信息、沟通和知识。从这个角度来看，信息无需经过审查就能让我们更加珍视它；它只需要稀缺即可。根据稀缺性原则，如果我们认为无法从其他途径获得某条信息，那么这条信息就更具说服力。这种“独家信息更具说服力”的观点是两位心理学家蒂莫西·布罗克和霍华德·弗罗姆克的核心思想，他们发展出了一种“商品理论”来分析说服力。

The strongest support I know for Brock and Fromkin's theory comes from a small experiment done by a student of mine. At the time, the student was also a successful businessman, the owner of a beef-importing company, who had returned to school to get advanced training in marketing. After we talked in my office one day about scarcity and exclusivity of information, he decided to do a study using his sales staff. The company's customers—buyers for supermarkets or other retail food outlets—were phoned as usual by a salesperson and asked for a purchase in one of three ways. One set of customers heard a standard sales presentation before being asked for their orders. Another set of customers heard the standard sales presentation plus information that the supply of imported beef was likely to be scarce in the upcoming months. A third group received the standard sales presentation and the information about a scarce supply of beef, too; however, they also learned that the scarce-supply news was not generally available inform-ation—it had come, they were told, from certain exclusive contacts that the company had. Thus the customers who received this last sales presentation learned that not only was the availability of the product limited, so also was the news concerning it—the scarcity double whammy.

我所知的对布罗克和弗罗姆金理论最有力的支持来自我的一位学生做的一个小实验。当时，这位学生也是一位成功的商人，拥有一家牛肉进口公司，他重返校园接受市场营销方面的进阶培训。有一天，我们在我的办公室里讨论了信息的稀缺性和排他性之后，他决定利用他的销售人员进行一项研究。公司的客户——超市或其他零售食品店的采购员——像往常一样接到销售人员的电话，并以三种方式之一被要求下单。一组客户在被要求下单之前先听了标准的销售介绍。另一组客户在听完标准销售介绍后，被告知未来几个月进口牛肉的供应可能会短缺。第三组客户同样听了标准销售介绍和牛肉供应短缺的信息；然而，他们还了解到，供应短缺的消息并非公开信息——他们被告知，这是公司通过某些独家渠道获得的。因此，收到最后一份销售演示的客户了解到，不仅产品的供应有限，而且有关该产品的消息也有限——稀缺性的双重打击。

The results of the experiment quickly become apparent when the company salespeople began to urge the owner to buy more beef because there wasn't enough in the inventory to keep up with all the orders they were receiving. Compared to the customers who got only the standard sales appeal, those who were also told about the future scarcity of beef bought more than twice as much. But the real boost in sales occurred among the customers who heard of the impending scarcity via "exclusive" information. They purchased six times the amount that the customers who received only the standard sales pitch did. Apparently the fact that the news carrying the scarcity of information was itself scarce made it especially persuasive.

当公司销售人员开始敦促老板增购牛肉，因为库存不足以满足所有订单需求时，实验结果很快就显现出来。与只收到标准销售说辞的顾客相比，那些被告知牛肉未来将短缺的顾客购买量是前者的两倍多。但真正的销售增长出现在那些通过“独家”信息得知即将短缺的顾客身上。他们的购买量是只收到标准销售说辞的顾客的六倍。显然，传播牛肉短缺信息的渠道本身就十分有限，这使得它格外具有说服力。

OPTIMAL CONDITIONS

最佳条件

Much like the other effective weapons of influence, the scarcity principle is more effective at some times than at other times. An important practical problem, then, is to find out when scarcity works best on us. A great deal can be learned in this regard from an experiment devised by social psychologist Stephen Worchel. The basic procedure used by Worchel and his research team was simple: Participants in a consumerpreference study were given a chocolate-chip cookie from a jar and asked to taste and rate its quality. For half of the raters, the jar contained ten cookies; for the other half, it contained just two. As we might expect from the scarcity principle, when the cookie was one of the only two available, it was rated more favorably than when it was one of ten. The cookie in short supply was rated as more desirable to eat in the future, more attractive as a consumer item, and more costly than the identical cookie in abundant supply.

与其他有效的策略一样，稀缺性原则有时比其他时候更有效。因此，一个重要的实际问题是：如何才能找到稀缺性对我们最有效的时机？社会心理学家斯蒂芬·沃切尔设计的一项实验在这方面提供了许多启示。沃切尔及其研究团队采用的基本方法很简单：他们让参与消费者偏好研究的受试者从罐子里取出一块巧克力曲奇，并要求他们品尝并评价其品质。一半受试者的罐子里装有十块曲奇，另一半受试者的罐子里只有两块。正如我们从稀缺性原则中预期的那样，当曲奇是仅有的两块之一时，它的评价比有十块时更高。供应短缺的曲奇被认为更令人向往，更具消费吸引力，也更昂贵，而供应充足的同类曲奇则不然。

Although this pattern of results provides a rather striking validation of the scarcity principle, it doesn't tell us anything we don't already know. Once again, we see that a less-available item is more desired and valued. The real worth of the cookie study comes from two additional findings. Let's take them one at a time, as each deserves a thorough consideration.

尽管这一结果模式有力地验证了稀缺性原则，但它并没有告诉我们任何我们原本不知道的信息。我们再次看到，越稀缺的物品越受欢迎，也越受珍视。这项饼干研究的真正价值在于另外两项发现。让我们逐一分析，因为每一项都值得深入探讨。

The first of these noteworthy results involved a small variation in the experiment's basic procedure. Rather than rating the cookies under conditions of constant scarcity, some participants were first given a jar of ten cookies that was then replaced by a jar of two cookies. Thus, before taking a bite, certain of the participants saw their abundant supply of cookies reduced to a scarce supply. Other participants, however, knew only scarcity of supply from the outset, since the number of cookies in their jars was left at two. With this procedure, the researchers were seeking to answer a question about types of scarcity: Do we value more those things that have recently become less available to us, or those things that have always been scarce? In the cookie experiment, the answer was plain. The drop from abundance to scarcity produced a decidedly more positive reaction to the cookies than did constant scarcity.

这些值得注意的结果中，第一个源于实验基本流程的一个细微变化。研究人员并没有让参与者在持续稀缺的条件下评价饼干，而是先给他们一罐十块饼干，然后换成一罐两块。这样，在咬一口之前，一些参与者就看到了自己原本丰富的饼干供应量骤减至稀缺状态。而另一些参与者从一开始就只知道饼干供应稀缺，因为他们罐子里的饼干数量始终是两块。研究人员通过这种方式试图解答一个关于稀缺类型的问题：我们更珍惜那些最近变得稀缺的东西，还是那些一直稀缺的东西？在饼干实验中，答案显而易见。从充足到稀缺的转变，比持续稀缺的状态，更能激发人们对饼干的积极反应。

The idea that newly experienced scarcity is the more powerful kind applies to situations well beyond the bounds of the cookie study. For example, social scientists have determined that such scarcity is a primary cause of political turmoil and violence. Perhaps the most prominent proponent of this argument is James C. Davies, who states that we are most likely to find revolutions where a period of improving economic and social conditions is followed by a short, sharp reversal in those conditions. Thus it is not the traditionally most downtrodden people—who have come to see their deprivation as part of the natural order of things—who are especially liable to revolt. Instead, revolutionaries are more likely to be those who have been given at least some taste of a better life. When the economic and social improvements they have experienced and come to expect suddenly become less available, they desire them more than ever and often rise up violently to secure them.

新近体验到的匮乏更具威力，这一观点远不止于饼干实验所探讨的范畴。例如，社会科学家已经证实，这种匮乏是政治动荡和暴力事件的主要原因之一。詹姆斯·C·戴维斯或许是这一论点的最杰出支持者，他指出，我们最有可能在经济和社会状况改善之后，紧接着出现短暂而急剧的逆转时，发现革命的爆发。因此，并非那些传统上最受压迫的人们——他们已经将自身的匮乏视为自然规律的一部分——特别容易发动起义。相反，革命者更有可能是那些至少尝到过一些美好生活滋味的人。当他们已经体验并习以为常的经济和社会改善突然变得难以获得时，他们比以往任何时候都更加渴望这些改善，并常常以暴力手段来争取这些改善。

Davies has gathered persuasive evidence for his novel thesis from a range of revolutions, revolts, and internal wars, including the French, Russian, and Egyptian revolutions as well as such domestic uprisings as Dorr's Rebellion in nineteenth-century Rhode Island, the American Civil War, and the urban black riots of the 1960s. In each case, a time of increasing well-being preceded a tight cluster of reversals that burst into violence.

戴维斯从一系列革命、起义和内战中收集了令人信服的证据来支持他的新论点，其中包括法国大革命、俄国革命和埃及革命，以及诸如19世纪罗德岛州的多尔叛乱、美国内战和20世纪60年代的城市黑人骚乱等国内起义。在每一种情况下，一段日益繁荣的时期之后都紧接着一系列急剧的逆转，最终演变成暴力冲突。

The racial conflict in America's cities during the mid-1960s represents a case in point that many of us can recall. At the time, it was not uncommon to hear the question, "Why now?" It didn't seem to make sense that within their three-hundred-year history, most of which had been spent in servitude and much of the rest in privation, American blacks would choose the socially progressive sixties in which to revolt. Indeed, as Davies points out, the two decades after the start of World War II had brought dramatic political and economic gains to the black population. In 1940, blacks faced stringent legal restrictions in such areas as housing, transportation, and education; moreover, even with the same amount of education, the average black family earned only a bit more than half of its counterpart white family. Fifteen years later, much had changed. Federal legislation had struck down as unacceptable formal and informal attempts to segregate blacks in schools, public places, housing, and employment settings. Large economic advances had been made, too; black family income had risen from 56 percent to 80 percent of that of a comparably educated white family.

20世纪60年代中期美国城市的种族冲突就是一个典型的例子，许多人对此都记忆犹新。当时，人们常常会问：“为什么偏偏是现在？”美国黑人有着三百年的历史，其中大部分时间都在奴役中度过，其余时间也饱受贫困之苦，他们为何偏偏选择在社会进步的六十年代发动反抗，这似乎令人费解。事实上，正如戴维斯所指出的，二战爆发后的二十年里，黑人在政治和经济方面都取得了显著的进步。1940年，黑人在住房、交通和教育等领域面临着严格的法律限制；此外，即使接受的教育水平相同，黑人家庭的平均收入也仅略高于白人家庭的一半。十五年后，情况发生了巨大的变化。联邦立法废除了在学校、公共场所、住房和就业方面对黑人进行种族隔离的正式和非正式做法，并认定这些做法是不可接受的。经济方面也取得了长足的进步；黑人家庭的收入已从受教育程度相当的白人家庭的 56% 上升到 80%。

But then, according to Davies's analysis of social conditions, this rapid progress was stymied by events that soured the heady optimism of previous years. First, political and legal change proved substantially easier to enact than social change. Despite all the progressive legislation of the forties and fifties, blacks perceived that most neighborhoods, jobs, and schools remained segregated. Thus the Washington-based victories came to feel like defeats at home. For example, in the four years following the U.S. Supreme Court's 1954 decision to integrate all public schools, blacks were the targets of 530 acts of violence (direct intimidation of black children and parents, bombings, and burnings) designed to prevent school integration. This violence generated the perception of another sort of setback in black progress. For the first time since well before World War II, when lynchings had occurred at an average rate of seventy-eight per year, blacks had to be concerned about the basic safety of their families. The new violence was not limited to the education issue, either. Peaceful civil-rights demonstrations of the time were frequently confronted by hostile crowds—and police.

然而，根据戴维斯对社会状况的分析，这种快速进步却被一些事件所阻碍，这些事件冲淡了前几年令人振奋的乐观情绪。首先，政治和法律变革的实施远比社会变革容易得多。尽管四五十年代出台了许多进步的立法，但黑人仍然感到大多数社区、工作场所和学校仍然存在种族隔离。因此，华盛顿取得的胜利在他们自己的家乡却如同失败一般。例如，在1954年美国最高法院裁定所有公立学校实行种族融合后的四年里，黑人成为530起暴力事件（包括直接恐吓黑人儿童和家长、爆炸和纵火）的目标，这些事件旨在阻止学校种族融合。这种暴力事件使黑人感到他们的进步遭遇了另一种挫折。自二战前私刑事件平均每年发生78起以来，黑人第一次不得不担忧自己家人的基本安全。而且，这种新的暴力事件并不局限于教育问题。当时的和平民权示威活动经常遭到敌对人群和警察的阻挠。

Still another type of downturn occurred—in pocketbook prog-ress. In 1962, the income of a black family had slid back to 74 percent of that of a similarly educated white family. By Davies's argument, the most illuminating aspect of this 74 percent figure is not that it represented a long-term increase in prosperity from pre-1940s levels but that it represented a short-term decline from the flush mid-1950s levels. In the next year came the Birmingham riots and, in staccato succession, scores of violent demonstrations, building toward the major upheavals of Watts, Newark, and Detroit.

还有另一种衰退——经济状况的下滑。1962年，黑人家庭的收入下滑至同等教育水平白人家庭的74%。戴维斯认为，这74%的数字最能说明问题的地方不在于它代表着比1940年代以前水平的长期繁荣，而在于它代表着比1950年代中期繁荣水平的短期下滑。次年，伯明翰爆发骚乱，随后一系列暴力示威活动接踵而至，最终演变为瓦茨、纽瓦克和底特律的大规模动乱。

In keeping with a distinct historical pattern of revolution, blacks in the United States were more rebellious when their prolonged progress was curtailed somewhat than they were before it began. This pattern offers a valuable lesson for would-be rulers: When it comes to freedoms, it is more dangerous to have given for a while than never to have given at all. The problem for a government that seeks to improve the political and economic status of a traditionally oppressed group is that, in so doing, it establishes freedoms for the group where none existed before. And should these now established freedoms become less available, there will be an especially hot variety of hell to pay.

与历史上革命的典型模式相符，美国黑人在长期进步受到一定程度阻碍后，比进步开始前更加反抗。这一模式给潜在的统治者敲响了警钟：在自由问题上，暂时让步比从未让步更加危险。一个政府如果试图改善传统上受压迫群体的政治和经济地位，问题在于，这样做实际上是为该群体创造了原本不存在的自由。而一旦这些新获得的自由受到限制，他们将面临极其惨痛的后果。

We can look to much more recent events in the former Soviet Union for evidence that this basic rule still holds. After decades of repression, Mikhail Gorbachev began granting the Soviet populace new liberties, privileges, and choices via the twin policies of glasnost and perestroika. Alarmed by the direction their nation was taking, a small group of government, military, and KGB officials staged a coup, placing Gorbachev under house arrest and announcing on August 19, 1991, that they had assumed power and were moving to reinstate the old order. Most of the world imagined that the Soviet people, known for their characteristic acquiescence to subjugation, would passively yield as they had always done. Time magazine editor Lance Morrow described his own reaction similarly: "At first the coup seemed to confirm the norm. The news administered a dark shock, followed immediately by a depressed sense of resignation: of course, of course, the Russians must revert to their essential selves, to their own history. Gorbachev and glasnost were an aberration; now we are back to fatal normality."

我们可以从前苏联近期发生的事件中寻找证据，证明这条基本规律依然适用。经过数十年的镇压，米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫开始通过“公开性”和“改革”这两项政策赋予苏联民众新的自由、特权和选择。然而，一小撮政府、军方和克格勃官员对国家的发展方向感到担忧，于是发动政变，将戈尔巴乔夫软禁在家，并于1991年8月19日宣布他们已经掌权，并将着手恢复旧秩序。世界上大多数人认为，以逆来顺受著称的苏联人民会像以往一样被动屈服。 《时代》杂志编辑兰斯·莫罗也描述了自己的类似反应：“起初，政变似乎印证了既定的常态。消息传来，令人震惊，紧接着便涌起一种沮丧的无奈感：当然，当然，俄罗斯人终究会回归本源，回归他们自己的历史。戈尔巴乔夫和公开性政策是例外；现在我们又回到了致命的常态。”

But these were not to be normal times. For one thing, Gorbachev had not governed in the tradition of the czars or Stalin or any of the line of oppressive postwar rulers who had not allowed even a breath of freedom to the masses. He had ceded them certain rights and choices. And when these now-established freedoms were threatened, the people lashed out the way a dog would if someone tried taking a fresh bone from its mouth. Within hours of the junta's announcement, thousands were in the streets, erecting barricades, confronting armed troops, surrounding tanks, and defying curfews. The uprising was so swift, so massive, so unitary in its opposition to any retreat from the gains of glasnost that after only three riotous days, the astonished officials relented, surrendering their power and pleading for mercy from President Gorbachev. Had they been students of history—or of psychology—the failed plotters would not have been so surprised by the tidal wave of popular resistance that swallowed their coup. From the vantage point of either discipline, they could have learned an invariant lesson: Freedoms once granted will not be relinquished without a fight.

但这并非寻常时期。首先，戈尔巴乔夫的统治方式与沙皇、斯大林或任何战后压迫统治者截然不同，后者从未给予民众丝毫自由。他赋予了民众某些权利和选择。当这些来之不易的自由受到威胁时，民众便如同狗咬断鲜嫩的骨头一般奋起反抗。军政府宣布消息后数小时内，成千上万的民众走上街头，设置路障，对抗武装部队，包围坦克，无视宵禁。这场起义如此迅速、如此大规模、如此团结一致地反对任何放弃公开性政策成果的行为，以至于仅仅三天暴乱之后，震惊的官员们便被迫让步，交出权力，并向戈尔巴乔夫总统乞求宽恕。如果这些政变失败者是历史学家或心理学家，他们就不会对席卷政变的民众抵抗浪潮感到如此惊讶。从这两个学科的角度来看，他们都能领悟到一个永恒不变的道理：一旦获得的自由，就绝不会轻易放弃，必将遭到反抗。

The lesson applies as well to the politics of family as country. The parent who grants privileges or enforces rules erratically invites rebelliousness by unwittingly establishing freedoms for the child. The parent who only sometimes prohibits between-meal sweets may create for the child the freedom to have such snacks. At that point, enforcing the rule becomes a much more difficult and explosive matter because the child is no longer merely lacking a never-possessed right but is losing an established one. As we have seen in the case of political freedoms and (especially pertinent to the present discussion) chocolate-chip cookies, people see a thing as more desirable when it has recently become less available than when it has been scarce all along. We should not be surprised, then, when research shows that parents who enforce discipline inconsistently produce generally rebellious children.

这个道理同样适用于家庭政治和国家政治。父母如果时而给予特权时而强制执行规则，就会在无意中为孩子创造自由，从而诱发孩子的叛逆。例如，父母如果只是偶尔禁止孩子在两餐之间吃甜食，就可能无意中给了孩子享用这类零食的自由。此时，执行规则就变得更加困难，也更容易引发冲突，因为孩子不再仅仅是失去了一项从未拥有过的权利，而是失去了一项既有的权利。正如我们在政治自由和（尤其与本文讨论相关的）巧克力曲奇饼干的例子中所看到的，人们往往认为，当某种东西最近变得稀缺时，它比一直稀缺的东西更令人渴望。因此，当研究表明，那些在管教方面前后不一致的父母，往往会养出叛逆的孩子时，我们就不应该感到惊讶了。

Let's look back to the cookie study for another insight into the way we react to scarcity. We've already seen from the results of that study that scarce cookies were rated higher than abundant cookies and that newly scarce cookies were rated higher still. Staying with the newly scarce cookies now, there was a certain cookie that was the highest rated of all: those that became less available because of a demand for them.

让我们回顾一下饼干研究，以进一步了解我们对稀缺性的反应。我们已经从该研究的结果中看到，稀缺的饼干比丰富的饼干评价更高，而新近稀缺的饼干评价更高。现在我们继续讨论新近稀缺的饼干，其中有一种饼干的评价最高：那就是因为需求量增加而变得稀缺的饼干。

Remember that in the experiment the participants who experienced new scarcity had been given a jar of ten cookies that was then replaced with a jar of only two cookies. Actually, the researchers did this in one of two ways. To certain participants, it was explained that some of their cookies had to be given away to other raters to supply the demand for cookies in the study. To another set of participants, it was explained that their number of cookies had to be reduced because the researcher had simply made a mistake and given them the wrong jar initially. The results showed that those whose cookies became scarce through the process of social demand liked them significantly more than those whose cookies became scarce by mistake. In fact, the cookies made less available through social demand were rated the most desirable of any in the study.

请记住，在实验中，经历新稀缺的参与者最初会得到一罐十块饼干，之后这罐饼干会被替换成只有两块的。实际上，研究人员采用了两种方式之一来实现这一点。对于部分参与者，研究人员解释说，为了满足研究中对饼干的需求，他们手中的一些饼干必须分给其他参与者。而对于另一部分参与者，研究人员则解释说，他们手中的饼干数量减少是因为研究人员犯了一个错误，一开始给他们的罐子装错了。结果表明，那些因为社会需求而导致饼干数量减少的参与者，比那些因为错误而导致饼干数量减少的参与者更喜欢这些饼干。事实上，那些因为社会需求而减少的饼干，在所有饼干中被评为最受欢迎的。

This finding highlights the importance of competition in the pursuit of limited resources. Not only do we want the same item more when it is scarce, we want it most when we are in competition for it. Advertisers often try to exploit this tendency in us. In their ads, we learn that "popular demand" for an item is so great that we must "hurry to buy," or we see a crowd pressing against the doors of a store before the start of a sale, or we watch a flock of hands quickly deplete a supermarket shelf of a product. There is more to such images than the idea of ordinary social proof. The message is not just that the product is good because other people think so, but also that we are in direct competition with those people for it.

这一发现凸显了竞争在争夺有限资源中的重要性。我们不仅在稀缺时更渴望拥有某件物品，而且在竞争激烈时，我们对它的渴望更是强烈。广告商常常试图利用我们这种心理。在他们的广告中，我们了解到某件商品“需求量巨大”，以至于我们必须“赶紧购买”；或者我们看到在促销开始前，商店门口挤满了人；又或者我们看到一大群人迅速将超市货架上的商品抢购一空。这些画面所传递的信息远不止普通的社会认同那么简单。它传递的信息不仅仅是：产品好是因为其他人这么认为，更重要的是，我们正与这些人直接竞争，才能买到它。

The feeling of being in competition for scarce resources has powerfully motivating properties. The ardor of an indifferent lover surges with the appearance of a rival. It is often for reasons of strategy, therefore, that romantic partners reveal (or invent) the attentions of a new admirer. Salespeople are taught to play the same game with indecisive customers. For example, a realtor who is trying to sell a house to a "fence-sitting" prospect will sometimes call the prospect with news of another potential buyer who has seen the house, liked it, and is scheduled to return the following day to talk about terms. When wholly fabricated, the new bidder is commonly described as an outsider with plenty of money: "an out-of-state investor buying for tax purposes" and "a physician and his wife moving into town" are favorites. The tactic, called in some circles "goosing 'em off the fence," can work devastatingly well. The thought of losing out to a rival frequently turns a buyer from hesitant to zealous.

对稀缺资源的竞争感具有强大的激励作用。当竞争对手出现时，原本对伴侣漠不关心的人也会燃起爱火。因此，出于策略考虑，情侣们常常会透露（或编造）新追求者的出现。销售人员也被教导要用同样的策略来对付犹豫不决的客户。例如，一位房地产经纪人如果想把房子卖给一位“观望”的潜在客户，有时会打电话给他，告诉他有另一位潜在买家看过房子，很喜欢，并且计划第二天再来洽谈。如果完全是捏造的，这位新买家通常会被描述成一个财力雄厚的“外地人”：“一位为了避税而购房的外州投资者”和“一对搬到本地的医生夫妇”都是常用的说法。这种策略在某些圈子里被称为“逼迫他们下定决心”，其效果往往非常显著。想到可能会输给竞争对手，买家往往会从犹豫不决转变为充满热情。

There is something almost physical about the desire to have a contested item. Shoppers at big close-out or bargain sales report being caught up emotionally in the event. Charged by the crush of competitors, they swarm and struggle to claim merchandise they would otherwise disdain. Such behavior brings to mind the "feeding frenzy" of wild, indiscriminate eating among animal groups. Commercial fishermen exploit this phenomenon by throwing a quantity of loose bait to large schools of certain fish. Soon the water is a roiling expanse of thrashing fins and snapping mouths competing for the food. At this point, the fishermen save time and money by dropping unbaited lines into the water, since the crazed fish will bite ferociously at anything now, including bare metal hooks.

对抢购商品的渴望几乎带有某种生理上的冲动。大型清仓甩卖或折扣促销的顾客常常表示，他们很容易被这种情绪所感染。在拥挤的竞争压力下，他们蜂拥而至，争抢那些原本可能不屑一顾的商品。这种行为让人联想到动物群体中那种不加选择地疯狂进食的“觅食狂潮”。商业渔民正是利用了这种现象，他们会向大群特定鱼类投放大量散落的鱼饵。很快，水面便会变成一片翻腾的海洋，无数鱼鳍拍打着，血盆大口地争抢着食物。此时，渔民们会直接投放不带鱼饵的鱼线，从而节省时间和成本，因为疯狂的鱼儿会凶猛地攻击任何东西，包括裸露的金属鱼钩。

There is a noticeable parallel between the ways that commercial fishermen and department stores generate a competitive fury in those they wish to hook. To attract and arouse the catch, fishermen scatter some loose bait called chum. For similar reasons, department stores holding a bargain sale toss out a few especially good deals on prominently advertised items called loss leaders. If the bait, of either form, has done its job, a large and eager crowd forms to snap it up. Soon, in the rush to score, the group becomes agitated, nearly blinded, by the adversarial nature of the situation. Humans and fish alike lose perspective on what they want and begin striking at whatever is being contested. One wonders whether the tuna flapping on a dry deck with only a bare hook in its mouth shares the what-hit-me bewilderment of the shopper arriving home with only a load of department-store bilge.

商业渔民和百货公司激起顾客竞争怒火的方式有着明显的相似之处。为了吸引和激起鱼儿的欲望，渔民会撒下一些叫做诱饵的散落饵料。出于类似的原因，百货公司在进行促销活动时，也会推出一些特别划算的特价商品，这些商品被重点宣传，被称为“亏本甩卖”。如果诱饵（无论是哪种形式）奏效，就会吸引大批顾客蜂拥而至，争相抢购。很快，在争抢的过程中，人群变得焦躁不安，几乎被这种竞争氛围蒙蔽了双眼。人和鱼都失去了原本的追求，开始攻击任何争夺的目标。人们不禁会想，一条在干燥甲板上扑腾着、嘴里只挂着光秃秃的鱼钩的金枪鱼，是否也像一个购物者一样，满脑子都是百货商店的垃圾，回到家后感到茫然不知所措。

Lest we believe that the competition-for-limited-resources-fever occurs only in such unsophisticated forms of life as tuna and bargain-basement shoppers, we should examine the story behind a remarkable purchase decision made in 1973 by Barry Diller, who was then vice president for prime-time programming at the American Broadcasting Company, but who has since been labeled the "miracle mogul" by Time magazine in reference to his remarkable successes as head of Paramount Pictures and the Fox Television Network. He agreed to pay $3.3 million for a single television showing of the movie The Poseidon Adventure. The figure is noteworthy in that it greatly exceeded the highest price ever previously paid for a one-time movie showing: $2 million for Patton. In fact, the payment was so excessive that ABC figured to lose $1 million on the Poseidon showing. As NBC vice president for special programs Bill Storke declared at the time, "There's no way they can get their money back, no way at all."

如果我们认为争夺有限资源的狂热只存在于金枪鱼和廉价购物者这类不谙世事的生物身上，那么我们应该探究一下巴里·迪勒在1973年做出的一项惊人的购买决定背后的故事。当时，迪勒是美国广播公司（ABC）黄金时段节目副总裁，后来因其在派拉蒙影业和福克斯电视网的卓越成就而被《时代》杂志誉为“奇迹大亨”。他同意支付330万美元购买电影《海神号遇险记》的单次电视播放权。这个数字之所以引人注目，是因为它远远超过了此前单次电影播放的最高价格：《巴顿将军》的200万美元。事实上，这笔费用如此之高，以至于ABC预计在《海神号遇险记》的播放上会亏损100万美元。正如NBC特别节目副总裁比尔·斯托克当时所言：“他们根本不可能收回成本，绝对不可能。”

How could an astute and experienced businessman like Diller go for a deal that would produce an expected loss of a million dollars? The answer may lie in a second noteworthy aspect of the sale: It was the first time that a motion picture had been offered to the networks in an open-bid auction. Never before had the three major commercial networks been forced to battle for a scarce resource in quite this way. The novel idea of a competitive auction was the brainchild of the movie's flamboyant showman-producer, Irwin Allen, and a 20th Century Fox vice president, William Self, who must have been ecstatic about the outcome. But how can we be sure that it was the auction format that generated the spectacular sales price rather than the blockbuster quality of the movie itself?

像迪勒这样精明老练的商人，怎么会接受一笔预计亏损一百万美元的交易呢？答案或许在于此次交易的第二个值得注意的方面：这是电影史上首次以公开竞标的方式提供给各大电视网。此前，三大商业电视网从未被迫以这种方式争夺稀缺资源。这种竞标方式的创新之处在于影片的制片人兼制片人欧文·艾伦和二十世纪福克斯副总裁威廉·塞尔夫，后者想必对最终结果欣喜若狂。但是，我们又如何确定是竞标模式而非影片本身的票房号召力造就了如此惊人的成交价呢？

Some comments from the auction participants provide impressive evidence. First came a statement from the victor, Barry Diller, intended to set future policy for his network. In language sounding as if it could have escaped only from between clenched teeth, he said, "ABC has decided regarding its policy for the future that it would never again enter into an auction situation." Even more instructive are the remarks of Diller's rival, Robert Wood, then president of CBS Television, who nearly lost his head and outbid his competitors at ABC and NBC:

一些竞标参与者的评论提供了令人印象深刻的证据。首先是胜出者巴里·迪勒的声明，意在为他的电视台制定未来的政策。他用一种仿佛只有咬牙切齿才能说出的语气说道：“ABC已经决定，今后绝不再参与竞标。” 更具启发性的是迪勒的竞争对手，时任CBS电视台总裁的罗伯特·伍德的言论。他当时几乎失去了理智，在竞标中击败了ABC和NBC的竞争对手：

We were very rational at the start. We priced the movie out, in terms of what it could bring in for us, then allowed a certain value on top of that for exploitation.
一开始我们非常理性。我们先估算了这部电影的成本，考虑它能给我们带来多少收益，然后在此基础上预留了一定的商业价值。
But then the bidding started. ABC opened with two million. I came back with two point four. ABC went to two point eight. And the fever of the thing caught us. Like a guy who had lost his mind, I kept bidding. Finally, I went to three point two; and there came a moment when I said to myself, "Good grief, if I get it, what the heck am I going to do with it?" When ABC finally topped me, my main feeling was relief.
但随后竞价开始了。ABC 开价两百万。我出价两百四十万。ABC 又加到两百八十万。我们都被这股热潮感染了。我像个疯子一样不停地加价。最后，我加到了三百二十万；那一刻，我心想：“天哪，如果我赢了，我该拿下它干什么呢？” 当 ABC 最终超过我时，我最大的感受是如释重负。
It's been very educational.
这次经历让我受益匪浅。

According to interviewer Bob MacKenzie, when Wood made his "It's been very educational" statement, he was smiling. We can be sure that when ABC's Diller made his "never again" announcement, he was not. Both men had clearly learned something from the "Great Poseidon Auction." But for one, there had been a $1 million tuition charge. Fortunately, there is a valuable but drastically less expensive lesson here for us, too. It is instructive to note that the smiling man was the one who had lost the highly sought-after prize. As a general rule, whenever the dust settles and we find losers looking and speaking like winners (and vice versa), we should be especially wary of the conditions that kicked up the dust—in the present case, open competition for a scarce resource. As the TV executives now know, extreme caution is advised whenever we encounter the devilish construction of scarcity plus rivalry.

据采访者鲍勃·麦肯齐 (Bob MacKenzie) 所述，伍德 (Wood) 发表“这次经历很有教育意义”的言论时，脸上带着笑容。我们可以肯定，当美国广播公司 (ABC) 的迪勒 (Diller) 宣布“永不再来”时，他脸上并没有笑容。两人显然都从这场“海神拍卖会”中学到了一些东西。但伍德为此付出了100万美元的代价。幸运的是，我们也能从中汲取一个宝贵但成本低得多的教训。值得注意的是，面带笑容的伍德正是错失了梦寐以求的奖品的人。一般来说，当尘埃落定，我们发现失败者看起来和说话都像赢家（反之亦然）时，我们应该格外警惕引发这场风波的根源——在本例中，就是对稀缺资源的公开竞争。正如电视高管们现在所认识到的，每当我们遇到稀缺性加上竞争这种棘手的组合时，都应该格外谨慎。

# ↩

HOW TO SAY NO

如何说“不”

It is easy enough to feel properly warned against scarcity pressures; but it is substantially more difficult to act on that warning. Part of the problem is that our typical reaction to scarcity hinders our ability to think. When we watch something we want become less available, a physical agitation sets in. Especially in those cases involving direct competition, the blood comes up, the focus narrows, and emotions rise. As this visceral current advances, the cognitive, rational side retreats. In the rush of arousal, it is difficult to be calm and studied in our approach. As CBS Television's president, Robert Wood, commented in the wake of his Poseidon adventure, "You get caught up in the mania of the thing, the acceleration of it. Logic goes right out the window."

我们很容易感受到稀缺压力带来的警示，但真正采取行动却难得多。部分原因是，我们对稀缺的典型反应会阻碍我们的思考能力。当我们眼睁睁看着自己想要的东西越来越难获得时，一种生理上的躁动就会涌上心头。尤其是在直接竞争的情况下，我们会热血沸腾，注意力高度集中，情绪也随之高涨。随着这种本能冲动的推进，认知和理性思维就会退缩。在情绪激动的冲击下，我们很难保持冷静和理性。正如哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）总裁罗伯特·伍德在经历“海神号”事件后所说：“你会被那种狂热和加速的情绪所裹挟，逻辑思维瞬间荡然无存。”

Here's our predicament, then: Knowing the causes and workings of scarcity pressures may not be sufficient to protect us from them because knowing is a cognitive thing, and cognitive processes are suppressed by our emotional reaction to scarcity. In fact, this may be the reason for the great effectiveness of scarcity tactics. When they are employed properly, our first line of defense against foolish behavior—a thoughtful analysis of the situation—becomes less likely.

这就是我们面临的困境：了解稀缺压力的成因和运作机制可能不足以保护我们免受其害，因为了解是一种认知过程，而认知过程会被我们对稀缺的情绪反应所抑制。事实上，这或许正是稀缺策略如此有效的原因。当这些策略被恰当运用时，我们抵御愚蠢行为的第一道防线——对形势进行深思熟虑的分析——就变得不太可能了。

If, because of brain-clouding arousal, we can't rely on our knowledge about the scarcity principle to stimulate properly cautious behavior, what can we use? Perhaps, in fine jujitsu style, we can use the arousal itself as our prime cue. In this way we can turn the enemy's strength to our advantage. Rather than relying on a considered, cognitive analysis of the entire situation, we might simply tune ourselves to the internal, visceral sweep for our warning. By learning to flag the experience of heightening arousal in a compliance situation, we can alert ourselves to the possibility of scarcity tactics there and to the need for caution.

如果因为大脑兴奋导致意识混乱，我们无法依靠对稀缺原则的了解来激发恰当的谨慎行为，那么我们该如何应对呢？或许，我们可以像柔术一样，将兴奋本身作为首要线索。这样，我们就能化敌为友。与其依赖对整个情况进行深思熟虑的认知分析，我们或许只需调整自身，关注内在的、本能的警示信号即可。通过学会识别顺从情境中兴奋感增强的体验，我们就能意识到其中可能存在的稀缺策略，并意识到保持警惕的必要性。

But suppose we accomplish this trick of using the rising tide of arousal as a signal to calm ourselves and to proceed with care. What then? Is there any other piece of information we can use to help make a proper decision in the face of scarcity? After all, merely recognizing that we ought to move carefully doesn't tell us the direction in which to move; it only provides the necessary context for a thoughtful decision.

但假设我们成功地利用不断上升的兴奋情绪作为信号，让自己冷静下来，谨慎行事，那么接下来呢？面对资源匮乏，我们还能利用哪些信息来帮助我们做出正确的决定？毕竟，仅仅意识到我们应该谨慎行事并不能告诉我们应该朝哪个方向前进；它只是为深思熟虑的决定提供了必要的背景信息。

Fortunately, there is information available on which we can base thoughtful decisions about scarce items. It comes, once again, from the chocolate-chip-cookie study, where the researchers uncovered something that seems strange but rings true regarding scarcity: Even though the scarce cookies were rated as significantly more desirable, they were not rated as any better-tasting than the abundant cookies. So despite the increased yearning that scarcity caused (the raters said they wanted to have more of the scarce cookies in the future and would pay a greater price for them), it did not make the cookies taste one whit better. Therein lies an important insight. The joy is not in experiencing a scarce commodity but in possessing it. It is important that we not confuse the two.

幸运的是，我们可以利用现有信息来做出关于稀缺物品的明智决策。这些信息再次来自巧克力曲奇饼干研究。研究人员发现了一个看似奇怪但却与稀缺性息息相关的事实：尽管稀缺的曲奇饼干被认为更令人向往，但它们的口感却并不比常见的曲奇饼干更好。因此，尽管稀缺性增强了人们的渴望（评价者表示他们希望将来能拥有更多稀缺的曲奇饼干，并且愿意为此支付更高的价格），但这并没有让曲奇饼干的味道更好。这其中蕴含着一个重要的洞见。真正的快乐不在于体验稀缺商品，而在于拥有它。我们切不可将二者混淆。

Whenever we confront the scarcity pressures surrounding some item, we must also confront the question of what it is we want from the item. If the answer is that we want the thing for the social, economic, or psychological benefits of possessing something rare, then, fine; scarcity pressures will give us a good indication of how much we would want to pay for it—the less available it is, the more valuable to us it will be. But very often we don't want a thing purely for the sake of owning it. We want it, instead, for its utility value; we want to eat it or drink it or touch it or hear it or drive it or otherwise use it. In such cases it is vital to remember that scarce things do not taste or feel or sound or ride or work any better because of their limited availability.

每当我们面临某种物品的稀缺性压力时，我们也必须思考：我们究竟想要从这件物品中获得什么？如果答案是，我们想要这件物品是为了获得拥有稀缺之物所带来的社会、经济或心理上的益处，那么，这很好；稀缺性压力会很好地指示我们愿意为它支付多少钱——越稀缺，对我们来说就越有价值。但很多时候，我们想要某件物品并非仅仅为了拥有它。相反，我们想要它是为了它的实用价值；我们想要吃它、喝它、触摸它、聆听它、驾驶它或以其他方式使用它。在这种情况下，至关重要的是要记住，稀缺之物并不会因为其数量有限而变得更美味、更舒适、更悦耳、更实用或更好用。

Although this is a simple point, it can often escape us when we experience the heightened desirability that scarce items naturally possess. I can cite a family example. My brother Richard supported himself through school by employing a compliance trick that cashed in handsomely on the tendency of most people to miss that simple point. In fact, his tactic was so effective that he had to work only a few hours each weekend for his money, leaving the rest of the time free for his studies.

虽然这一点很简单，但当我们感受到稀缺物品本身所具有的强烈吸引力时，往往会忽略它。我可以举个家庭例子。我的弟弟理查德靠着一个巧妙的“顺从技巧”赚取了丰厚的收入，而这个技巧恰恰利用了大多数人忽略这个简单道理的弱点。事实上，他的策略非常有效，以至于他每个周末只需工作几个小时就能挣到钱，其余时间都可以专心学习。

Richard sold cars, but not in a showroom nor on a car lot. He would buy a couple of used cars sold privately through the newspaper on one weekend and, adding nothing but soap and water, would sell them at a decided profit through the newspaper on the following weekend. To do this, he had to know three things. First, he had to know enough about cars to buy those that were offered for sale at the bottom of their blue-book price range but could be legitimately resold for a higher price. Second, once he got the car, he had to know how to write a newspaper ad that would stimulate substantial buyer interest. Third, once a buyer arrived, he had to know how to use the scarcity principle to generate more desire for the car than it perhaps deserved. Richard knew how to do all three. For our purposes, though, we need to examine his craft with just the third.

理查德卖车，但不是在展厅或汽车销售点。他会在一个周末通过报纸私下购买几辆二手车，然后只加点肥皂和水，再在下一个周末通过报纸以可观的利润出售。为了做到这一点，他必须掌握三件事。首先，他必须对汽车有足够的了解，才能买到那些以蓝皮书价格区间底部出售，但可以合法转售更高价格的车辆。其次，一旦买到车，他必须知道如何撰写能够激发大量买家兴趣的报纸广告。第三，一旦有买家出现，他必须懂得如何利用稀缺性原理，让买家对这辆车产生远超其本身价值的渴望。理查德精通这三点。不过，就我们的目的而言，我们只需要分析他的第三项技巧。

For a car he had purchased on the prior weekend, he would place an ad in the Sunday paper. Because he knew how to construct a good ad, he usually received an array of calls from potential buyers on Sunday morning. Each prospect who was interested enough to want to see the car was given an appointment time —the same appointment time. So if six people were scheduled, they were all scheduled for, say, two o'clock that afternoon. This little device of simultaneous scheduling paved the way for later compliance because it created an atmosphere of competition for a limited resource.

他会在上周末购买一辆车后，在周日的报纸上刊登广告出售。由于他很会写广告，通常周日早上就能接到很多潜在买家的电话。每个对看车感兴趣的潜在客户都会被安排一个时间——而且是同一个时间。所以如果有六个人预约，他们的预约时间都会是下午两点。这种同时预约的小技巧，营造了一种竞争有限资源的氛围，从而促成了后续的销售。

Typically, the first prospect to arrive would begin a studied examination of the car and would engage in standard car-buying behavior, such as pointing out any blemishes or deficiencies or asking if the price was negotiable. The psychology of the situation changed radically, however, when the second buyer drove up. The availability of the car to either prospect suddenly became limited by the presence of the other.

通常情况下，第一个到达的潜在买家会仔细检查车辆，并进行一些标准的购车行为，例如指出任何瑕疵或缺陷，或者询问价格是否可以商量。然而，当第二个买家到达时，情况就发生了根本性的变化。由于另一位买家的出现，两位潜在买家对车辆的选择权突然受到了限制。

Often the earlier arrival, inadvertently stoking the sense of rivalry, would assert his right to primary consideration. "Just a minute, now. I was here first." If he didn't assert that right, Richard would do it for him. Addressing the second buyer, Richard would say, "Excuse me, but this other gentleman was here before you. So can I ask you to wait on the other side of the driveway for a few minutes until he's finished looking at the car? Then, if he decides he doesn't want it or if he can't make up his mind, I'll show it to you."

通常情况下，先到的人会无意中激起竞争意识，坚持自己拥有优先权。“稍等一下，我先来的。” 如果他没有坚持，理查德就会替他这么做。理查德会对第二位买家说：“不好意思，这位先生比您先到。所以，请您在车道另一边稍等几分钟，等他看完车。如果他决定不买了，或者拿不定主意，我会把车给您看。”

Richard claims it was possible to watch the agitation grow on the first buyer's face. His leisurely assessment of the car's pros and cons had suddenly become a now-or-never, limited-time-only rush to decision over a contested resource. If he didn't decide for the car—at Richard's asking price—in the next few minutes, he might lose it for good to that... that ...lurking newcomer over there. For his part, the second buyer would be equally agitated by the combination of rivalry and restricted availability. He would pace on the periphery, visibly straining to get at this now more desirable hunk of metal. Should two-o'clock appointment number one fail to buy or even fail to decide quickly enough, two-o'clock appointment number two was ready to pounce.

理查德声称，他能清楚地看到第一位买家脸上焦躁不安的神情。他原本悠闲地权衡着这辆车的优缺点，突然间变成了争先恐后、时不我待的局面，必须争抢这辆炙手可热的车。如果他不能在接下来的几分钟内，以理查德的要价买下这辆车，他可能就永远失去它，落入那个……那个……潜伏在旁边的新人手中。而第二位买家，同样也会因为竞争和车源有限而焦躁不安。他会在车流边缘踱步，明显渴望能抢到这辆现在更令人垂涎的车。如果下午两点钟的第一个买家没能买下这辆车，或者甚至没能及时做出决定，那么下午两点钟的第二个买家已经准备好出手了。

If these conditions alone were not enough to secure a favorable purchase decision immediately, the trap snapped surely shut as soon as the third two-o'clock appointment arrived on the scene. According to Richard, stacked-up competition was usually too much for the first prospect to bear. He would end the pressure quickly by either agreeing to Richard's price or by leaving abruptly. In the latter instance, the second arrival would strike at the chance to buy out of a sense of relief coupled with a new feeling of rivalry with that... that... lurking newcomer over there.

如果这些条件还不足以立即促成理想的购买决定，那么一旦第三个下午两点钟的预约出现，陷阱就肯定会立刻落下。据理查德说，多重竞争通常会让第一个潜在买家难以承受。他会迅速结束压力，要么接受理查德的价格，要么直接离开。如果是后者，第二个买家就会抓住机会，既如释重负，又会因为与那个……那个……潜伏在旁边的新来者之间的竞争而迅速出手。

All those buyers who contributed to my brother's college education failed to recognize a fundamental fact about their purchases: The increased desire that spurred them to buy had little to do with the merits of the car. That failure of recognition occurred for two reasons. First, the situation Richard arranged for them produced an emotional reaction that made it difficult for them to think straight. Second, as a consequence, they never stopped to think that the reason they wanted the car in the first place was to use it, not merely to have it. And the com-petition-for-a-scarce-resource pressures Richard applied affected only their desire to have the car in the sense of possessing it. Those pressures did not affect the value of the car in terms of the real purpose for which they had wanted it.

所有资助我哥哥上大学的买家都未能意识到他们购买行为的一个根本事实：促使他们购买的欲望与汽车本身的优劣几乎无关。他们未能认识到这一点有两个原因。首先，理查德为他们安排的局面引发了强烈的情绪反应，使他们难以理性思考。其次，结果，他们从未停下来思考，他们最初想要这辆车的真正目的是为了使用它，而不仅仅是拥有它。理查德施加的“争夺稀缺资源”的压力，仅仅影响了他们拥有汽车的欲望，而没有影响他们真正想要这辆车的目的——使用它。

Should we find ourselves beset by scarcity pressures in a compliance situation, then, our best response would occur in a two-stage sequence. As soon as we feel the tide of emotional arousal that flows from scarcity influences, we should use that rise in arousal as a signal to stop short. Panicky, feverish reactions have no place in wise compliance decisions. We need to calm ourselves and regain a rational perspective. Once that is done, we can move to the second stage by asking ourselves why we want the item under consideration. If the answer is that we want it primarily for the purpose of owning it, then we should use its availability to help gauge how much we want to spend for it. However, if the answer is that we want it primarily for its function (that is, we want something good to drive, drink, eat, etc.), then we must remember that the item under consideration will function equally well whether scarce or plentiful. Quite simply, we need to recall that the scarce cookies didn't taste any better.

如果我们在需要遵守规定的情境中面临稀缺压力，那么最佳应对方式应分两步进行。一旦感受到稀缺带来的情绪波动，我们就应该立即停止。恐慌和冲动的反应不利于做出明智的遵守规定决定。我们需要冷静下来，重新建立理性的视角。之后，我们可以进入第二阶段，问问自己为什么想要这件物品。如果答案是主要为了拥有它，那么我们应该根据它的可获得性来衡量我们愿意为此支付多少钱。但是，如果答案是主要为了它的功能（例如，我们想要一些好的东西来开车、喝、吃等等），那么我们必须记住，无论稀缺还是充足，这件物品的功能都是一样的。简而言之，我们需要记住，稀缺的饼干味道并不会更好。

READER'S REPORT

读者报告

From a Blacksburg, Virginia, Woman

来自弗吉尼亚州布莱克斯堡的一位女士

"Last Christmas I met a twenty-seven-year-old man. I was nineteen. Although he really wasn't my type, I went out with him—probably because it was a status thing to date an older man—but I really didn't become interested in him until my folks expressed their concern about his age. The more they got on my case about it, the more in love I became. It only lasted five months, but this was about four months longer than it would have lasted if my parents hadn't said anything."

“去年圣诞节我认识了一个27岁的男人。我当时19岁。虽然他并不是我喜欢的类型，但我还是和他约会了——大概是因为和年纪大的男人交往是一种身份象征——但我真正对他产生兴趣，是在我父母对他的年龄表示担忧之后。他们越是唠叨，我就越是爱上他。这段感情只维持了五个月，但如果我父母什么都没说，这段感情大概会持续四个月左右。”

Although Romeo and Juliet have long since passed away, it appears that the "Romeo and Juliet effect" is alive and well and making regular appearances in places like Blacksburg, Virginia.

虽然罗密欧与朱丽叶早已作古，但“罗密欧与朱丽叶效应”似乎依然存在，并在弗吉尼亚州布莱克斯堡等地频繁出现。

# ↩

Epilogue - INSTANT INFLUENCE

尾声——即时影响

Primitive Consent for an Automatic Age

自动年龄的原始同意

Every day in every way, I'm getting better.
我每天在各个方面都在进步。
—Emile Coue
——埃米尔·库埃
Every day in every way, I'm getting busier.
我每天在各方面都变得越来越忙。
—Robert Cialdini
——罗伯特·西奥迪尼

B ACK IN THE 1960s A MAN NAMED JOE PINE HOSTED A RATHER remarkable TV talk show that was syndicated from California. The program was made distinctive by Pine's caustic and confrontational style with his guests—for the most part, a collection of exposure-hungry entertainers, would-be celebrities, and representatives of fringe political or social organizations. The host's abrasive approach was designed to provoke his guests into arguments, to fluster them into embarrassing admissions, and generally to make them look foolish. It was not uncommon for Pine to introduce a visitor and launch immediately into an attack on the individual's beliefs, talent, or appearance. Some people claimed that Pine's acid personal style was partially caused by a leg amputation that had embittered him to life; others said no, that he was just vituperous by nature.

上世纪60年代，一位名叫乔·派恩的男士主持了一档颇为引人注目的电视脱口秀节目，该节目在加利福尼亚州播出。派恩以其尖刻且咄咄逼人的风格著称，他的嘉宾大多是渴望出名的艺人、梦想成名的年轻人以及一些边缘政治或社会组织的代表。派恩这种尖锐的风格旨在激怒嘉宾，引发争论，迫使他们做出尴尬的供述，总之就是让他们出丑。派恩经常会在介绍完一位嘉宾后，立即对其信仰、才华或外貌进行攻击。有人认为，派恩这种尖酸刻薄的个人风格部分源于一次截肢手术，使他变得愤世嫉俗；也有人说并非如此，他只是天生如此尖刻。

One evening rock musician Frank Zappa was a guest on the show. This was at a time in the sixties when very long hair on men was still unusual and controversial. As soon as Zappa had been introduced and seated, the following exchange occurred:

一天晚上，摇滚音乐家弗兰克·扎帕做客节目。当时正值六十年代，男士留长发还很不寻常，也颇具争议。扎帕刚被介绍出场并落座，就发生了以下对话：

PINE: I guess your long hair makes you a girl.

派恩：我猜你的长头发让你看起来像个女孩。

ZAPPA: I guess your wooden leg makes you a table.

扎帕：看来你的木腿让你变成了一张桌子。

Aside from containing what may be my favorite ad-lib, the above dialogue illustrates a fundamental theme of this book: Very often in making a decision about someone or something, we don't use all the relevant available information; we use, instead, only a single, highly representative piece of the total. And an isolated piece of information, even though it normally counsels us correctly, can lead us to clearly stupid mistakes—mistakes that, when exploited by clever others, leave us looking silly or worse.

除了包含我最喜欢的即兴发挥之外，上述对话还阐明了本书的一个基本主题：在对某人或某事做出决定时，我们常常不会使用所有相关的可用信息；相反，我们只会使用其中极具代表性的一小部分信息。而孤立的信息，即使通常情况下它能给我们正确的建议，也可能导致我们犯下明显的愚蠢错误——这些错误一旦被聪明人利用，就会让我们显得愚蠢，甚至更糟。

At the same time, a complicating companion theme has been present throughout this book: Despite the susceptibility to stupid decisions that accompanies a reliance on a single feature of the available data, the pace of modern life demands that we frequently use this shortcut. Recall that early in Chapter 1, our shortcut approach was likened to the automatic responding of lower animals, whose elaborate behavior patterns could be triggered by the presence of a lone stimulus feature—a "cheep-cheep" sound, a shade of red breast feather, or a specific sequence of light flashes. The reason infrahumans must often rely on such solitary stimulus features is their restricted mental capability. Their small brains cannot begin to register and process all the relevant information in their environments. So these species have evolved special sensitivities to certain aspects of the information. Because those selected aspects of information are normally enough to cue a correct response, the system is usually very efficient: Whenever a female turkey hears "cheep-cheep," click, whirr, out rolls the proper maternal behavior in a mechanical fashion that conserves much of her limited brainpower for dealing with the variety of other situations and choices she must face in her day.

与此同时，本书贯穿着一个更为复杂的主题：尽管依赖单一数据特征容易导致愚蠢的决策，但现代生活的快节奏迫使我们频繁使用这种捷径。回想一下，在第一章开头，我们将这种捷径比作低等动物的自动反应，它们复杂的行为模式可能由单一的刺激特征触发——例如“唧唧”的叫声、某种红色的胸羽，或特定的闪光序列。低等生物之所以常常依赖这种单一的刺激特征，是因为它们认知能力有限。它们的大脑容量小，无法接收和处理环境中所有相关信息。因此，这些物种进化出了对某些特定信息的特殊敏感性。由于这些选定的信息通常足以引发正确的反应，因此该系统通常非常高效：每当雌火鸡听到“唧唧”声、咔哒声、呼呼声时，就会机械地表现出适当的母性行为，从而节省了她有限的脑力来应对她一天中必须面对的各种其他情况和选择。

We, of course, have vastly more effective brain mechanisms than mother turkeys, or any other animal group, for that matter. We are unchallenged in the ability to take into account a multitude of relevant facts and, consequently, to make good decisions. Indeed, it is this information-processing advantage over other species that has helped make us the dominant form of life on the planet.

当然，我们的大脑机制比母火鸡，或者任何其他动物群体都要高效得多。我们能够同时考虑大量相关事实，并因此做出正确的决策，这一点无人能及。事实上，正是这种信息处理方面的优势，使我们成为地球上的主宰物种。

Still, we have our capacity limitations, too; and, for the sake of efficiency, we must sometimes retreat from the time-consuming, sophisticated, fully informed brand of decision making to a more automatic, primitive, single-feature type of responding. For instance, in deciding whether to say yes or no to a requester, it is clear that we frequently pay attention to but one piece of the relevant information in the situation. We have been exploring several of the most popular of the single pieces of information that we use to prompt our compliance decisions. They are the most popular prompts precisely because they are the most reliable ones, those that normally point us toward the correct choice. That is why we employ the factors of reciprocation, consistency, social proof, liking, authority, and scarcity so often and so automatically in making our compliance decisions. Each, by itself, provides a highly reliable cue as to when we will be better off saying yes than no.

然而，我们的能力也有限；为了提高效率，我们有时不得不放弃耗时费力、复杂且信息全面的决策方式，转而采用更自动化、更原始、基于单一特征的响应模式。例如，在决定是否答应请求时，我们通常只会关注情境中的一条相关信息。我们一直在探讨一些最常用的、用于指导我们做出服从决定的单一信息。它们之所以最常用，正是因为它们最可靠，通常能指引我们做出正确的选择。这就是为什么我们在做出服从决定时如此频繁且如此自动地运用互惠、一致性、社会认同、喜好、权威和稀缺性等因素。每一项因素本身都能提供高度可靠的线索，告诉我们何时说“是”比说“不”更有利。

We are likely to use these lone cues when we don't have the inclination, time, energy, or cognitive resources to undertake a complete analysis of the situation.
